topics.title: Understanding and managing frequent HA audit log 0108035018
topics.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrading to FortiOS 7.4.13, you may observe frequent event logs on a FortiGate High Availability (HA) cluster with log ID 0108035018.A sample log message appears as follows:date=2026-10-23 time=10:33:00 logid="0108035018" type="event" subtype="ha" level="information" vd="root" logdesc="HA secondary received CLI commands" user="FGT_ha_admin" ui="ha_daemon" msg="Received CMD from ip:169.254.0.1 vdom:vsys_ha type:1, msg_type:66"In FortiOS 7.4.13, security audit logging was added to record commands exchanged between HA cluster members across the internal heartbeat channel.Before FortiOS 7.4.13, these internal exchanges occurred silently. In FortiOS 7.4.13, each received command generates an informational event log.ScopeFortiOS 7.4.13.SolutionThese logs are purely informational. They do not cause packet loss, do not trigger failovers, and do not indicate a configuration defect.You can confirm that your cluster is healthy, or configure a log filter to exclude this message if you prefer not to retain it.Confirm HA Cluster SynchronizationTo verify that the cluster is healthy and in sync, run the following commands on the primary FortiGate:get system ha status diagnose sys ha statusVerify that both cluster members show an in-sync state and that the secondary node is reachable over all configured heartbeat interfaces.Filter the Log from Local Disk Storage (Optional)If your FortiGate has an onboard disk and you wish to stop recording this informational log to disk, configure a free-style exclusion filter in the CLI:config log disk filter config free-style edit 1 set category event set filter "(logid 0108035018)" set filter-type exclude next end endFilter the Log from FortiAnalyzer (Optional)If you send logs to FortiAnalyzer and wish to exclude this message, apply a free-style filter on the FortiGate:config log fortianalyzer filter config free-style edit 1 set category event set filter "(logid 0108035018)" set filter-type exclude next end end

topics.title: Metadata variables in CLI scripts use global or default values instead of mapped (per-device/VDOM) values
topics.summary: Description How metadata variables works in a CLI script. Scope FortiManager. Solution Metadata variables referenced inside CLI scripts in FortiManager do not resolve to a device‑specific mapped value when the script is executed on the Device Database. The script applies the value defined for the global context, or the default value if no global value is set — not the value mapped for a specific device or VDOM. Scenario A metadata variable is created with a default value and a per‑device mapped value (e.g. mapped for a root or named VDOM). If used inside a firewall object (e.g. an Address), the variable correctly resolves to the device's mapped value. The same variable used inside a CLI script run on the Device Database resolves to the global value — or the default value when no global value exists — instead of the per‑device/VDOM mapped value. This is an expected behavior. Metadata variables used in CLI scripts executed on the Device Database only support the global context or the default value. VDOM‑context (per‑device/VDOM) mapped values are not resolved within CLI scripts. Below a practical example. This is the metadata variable: FMG_Test # execute fmpolicy print-adom-object 179 3200 test_metadataDump object ttest_metadata] of category dfmg variable] in adom vTEST]:---------------config fmg variableedit "test_metadata"set value "1"config dynamic_mappingedit "Test_Firewall"-"global"set value "5"nextedit "Test_Firewall"-"SDWAN"set value "12"nextedit "Test_Firewall"-"root"set value "9"nextendnextend Script: config vdomedit SDWANconfig router static edit 1 set gateway 1.$(test_metadata).$(test_metadata).4 nextendendconfig vdomedit rootconfig router static edit 1 set gateway 1.$(test_metadata).$(test_metadata).4 nextendend This script is run on the Device DB on Test_Firewall. Note that the "global" value was used. The values assigned to "root" or "SDWAN" were not used. View the log of script Test: running on device Test_Firewall (Test)-------Executing time: Thu Oct 22 15:33:07 2026-----------Starting log (Run on database)config vdomedit SDWANconfig router staticedit 2set gateway 1.5.5.4nextendendconfig vdomedit rootconfig router staticedit 2set gateway 1.5.5.4 nextendendRunning script(Test) on DB success

topics.title: Prevent unnecessary FortiLink frames on FortiSwitch edge ports
topics.summary: DescriptionThe reasons why Managed FortiSwitch ports configured with the default-auto-isl LLDP profile may forward unnecessary FortiLink protocol frames (EtherType 0x88FF) to connected end devices. Devices that do not support or process these frames may discard them, resulting in rapidly increasing packet discard counters and unnecessary network traffic.ScopeFortiSwitch.SolutionFortiSwitch ports configured with the default-auto-isl LLDP profile by default.This profile supports automatic Inter-Switch Link (ISL) formation, allowing FortiSwitches to discover each other and establish inter-switch trunks.When this profile is applied to ports connected to end devices that do not require automatic ISL formation, FortiLink protocol frames with EtherType 0x88FF may reach those devices.The receiving devices may discard these frames because the EtherType is unsupported, causing unnecessary increases in packet discard counters.SolutionChange the LLDP profile on affected edge ports from default-auto-isl to default.Important: Do not apply this change indiscriminately to ports connected to other FortiSwitches that rely on automatic ISL formation.Configuration via FortiGate CLIIdentify the FortiSwitch and its connected edge ports.Verify that the ports do not require automatic ISL formation.Apply the following configuration:config switch-controller managed-switch edit config ports edit set lldp-profile "default" next end next endExpected resultUnnecessary FortiLink protocol frames are prevented from reaching connected devices on the affected ports, reducing avoidable frame discards and preventing servers from receiving a flood of unnecessary Ethernet frames.

topics.title: FortiAppSec Cookie Security causing HTTP 403 Forbidden errors
topics.summary: DescriptionEnabling the Set HttpOnly Cookie feature in FortiWeb Cloud may cause applications to return HTTP 403 Forbidden errors if the application relies on JavaScript to read CSRF tokens from cookies.ScopeFortiAppSec Cloud.SolutionSymptomsUsers encounter HTTP 403 Forbidden (Authentication Error) responses on various application pages after a successful login. These errors occur specifically when Cookie Security features are enabled in FortiWeb Cloud. No corresponding security violations or blocks appear in the Web Application Firewall (WAF) event logs, even when the policy is set to Alert mode.Root CauseThe issue is caused by the Set HttpOnly Cookie setting. When this feature is enabled, FortiWeb Cloud adds the HttpOnly flag to cookies passed to the browser. This flag prevents client-side JavaScript from accessing the cookie.If the application is designed to read a Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) token from a cookie using JavaScript, the browser cannot access the token. Consequently, the application receives a request with a missing or empty CSRF token and returns an HTTP 403 Access Denied response. Because this is an application-level authentication failure and not a WAF security block, no events are logged in the FortiWeb Cloud WAF logs.ResolutionDisable the Set HttpOnly Cookie option while maintaining other security settings.Log in to the FortiWeb Cloud console.Navigate to the Cookie Security settings for the affected policy.Disable the Set HttpOnly Cookie option.Keep the Set Secure Cookie option enabled if the application supports it.Save the configuration and test the application functionality.

topics.title: How to create a CLI script that runs automatically after every policy package or device settings installation on FortiManager
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to create a CLI script on FortiManager and configure it to run automatically on the FortiGate after every device install (policy package or device settings installation).ScopeFortiManager 7.x and 8.x.SolutionSome settings are changed or reverted by an install from FortiManager, or cannot be managed from the policy package or device database. A CLI script that runs directly on the FortiGate after each install can restore the required configuration without a manual step.For this, create a script with the target "Remote FortiGate Directly (via CLI)", then enable "Automatic execute after each device install" in the script schedule.Step 1: Create the scriptGo to "Device Manager" -> Script.Select "Create New".Enter a name for the script (for example, "post-install-script").Set "Type" to "CLI Script".Set "Run script on" to "Remote FortiGate Directly (via CLI)".In "Script Detail", enter the CLI commands to run on the FortiGate. For example, for a FortiGate with VDOMs enabled:config vdom edit root config set end next endFor a FortiGate without VDOMs, enter the commands without the "config vdom" and "edit root" lines:config set endSelect "OK".Step 2: Run the script automatically after every installEnable the scheduled and automatic script options in the FortiManager CLI:config system admin setting set show_automatic_script enable set show_schedule_script enable endGo to "Device Manager" -> "Scripts".Right-click the CLI script and select "Schedule Script".Select the FortiGate devices that the script will run on.Select "Enable Automatic execute after each device install".Select "OK".Once enabled, the script runs on the selected FortiGate devices after each install, including every policy package installation and device settings installation. No manual step is needed.VerificationInstall a policy package or the device settings to one of the selected FortiGate devices.When the installation finishes, go to "Device Manager" -> "Scripts" and open the script execution history ("Script Log") to check that the script ran on the device.On the FortiGate CLI, check that the configuration was applied. For example:show full | grep Note:"Automatic execute after each device install" is only available when "Run script on" is set to "Remote FortiGate Directly (via CLI)". It cannot be used with scripts that target "Policy Package" or "ADOM Database".When "Automatic execute after each device install" is enabled, a time-based schedule (one time, daily, weekly, monthly) cannot be configured for the same script.A script that runs directly on the FortiGate triggers an automatic retrieve back to FortiManager. The policy package status may temporarily show "Unknown".The script runs after the install, so the change is applied on the FortiGate but does not become part of the policy package or the device database in FortiManager. The next install can overwrite it, which is why the script runs after every install.Related documents:Troubleshooting Tip: Useful workaround when FortiManager does not install configuration as expectedTechnical Tip: CLI Script behavior to run in FortiManager

topics.title: FortiManager Policy Package install fails with verification error due to "antiphish: max-body-len" parameter
topics.summary: Description An issue where FortiManager Policy Package installation fails with a verification error due to the " antiphish: max-body-len" parameter under webfilter profiles. Scope FortiManager and FortiProxy 7.4.9 and higher, FortiProxy 7.6.1 and higher Solution When installing a Policy Package from FortiManager to FortiProxy 7.4.9, the installation fails with verification messages similar to the following: (vdom root: webfilter profile "monitor-all" antiphish:max-body-len) remote original: to be installed: 65536 <--- done generating verification report install failed The same message may be reported for multiple webfilter profiles. The root cause is a difference in the default value of the max-body-len parameter between FortiProxy and FortiManager. Starting with FortiProxy 7.4.9 and 7.6.1, the default value of max-body-len was changed from 65535 to 1024 . However, FortiManager continues to use 65535 as the default value for this parameter. This difference in default values can result in installation verification failure in FortiManager. topics.title: Technical Tip: Retrieve configuration file using GUI or CLI from a FortiManager
topics.summary: Description This article describes how the configuration file of a FortiGate can be retrieved by a FortiManager through the GUI or the CLI. Retrieving the configuration file using CLI can be used to gather more debug information if the retrieval process fails in the GUI. Scope FortiManager. Solution Via GUI: From: Device Manager -> Device & Group, as shown below: Select the managed FortiGate for which it is necessary to retrieve the configuration. Scroll down until the section: Configuration and Installation is visible; Click the button to the right of the Total Revision number called: Revision history. In the section that appears on the right, there is the Retrieve config button. Via CLI: Use the following debug to retrieve the OID of the device in question: diagnose dvm device list Once the OID value is known, the following command can be executed to retrieve the configuration file of the device in question: diagnose test deploymanager reloadconf <----- OID value from the previous step. Sample Configuration: diagnose dvm device list --- There are currently 2 devices/vdoms managed --- TYPE OID SN HA IP NAME ADOM IPS FIRMWARE fmg/faz enabled 158 FGVM0X00000XXXX - 10.5.60.3 FGVM010000****** root 6.00741 (regular) 5.0 MR4 (7605) |- STATUS: db: not modified; conf: out of sync; cond: unknown; dm: autoupdated; conn: down |- vdom:[3]root flags:1 adom:root pkg:[imported]FGVM010000****** Where the OID will be 158 for the respective FortiGate: diagnose test deploymanager reloadconf 158 Note: This operation is possible if the FGFM tunnel between the FortiGate and the FortiManager is up; otherwise, it will be necessary to perform troubleshooting as explained in Troubleshooting Tip: How to troubleshoot connectivity issues The following is an explanation of when it is useful to perform the Retrieve: FortiManager device settings and sync status Related articles: Technical Tip: How to fix synchronization issue in FortiManager Technical Tip: How to do bulk retrieve config in FortiManager using a script

topics.title: FortiNAC-F does not assign a VLAN via MAB to FortiAPs managed by a FortiGate
topics.summary: DescriptionReasons why FortiNAC-F answers MAB requests for FortiGate-managed FortiAPs with an Access-Accept that carries no VLAN, and how to fix it. The fix is one global setting: Enable Network Access Policy for Wireless Access Points, under System -> Settings -> Network Device.ScopeFortiNAC-F 7.6.x (validated on 7.6.7).FortiGate acting as wireless controller for FortiAPs, modeled in FortiNAC Network -> Inventory.FortiAPs connected to a third-party access switch (example: Aruba CX 6200) that uses FortiNAC as RADIUS server for MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB).SolutionSymptoms:The FortiAP's switch port stays in the static access VLAN instead of moving to the VLAN set in the Network Access Policy.The FortiAP appears under the FortiGate in Network -> Inventory as a Wireless Access Point.Searching the AP MAC in Users & Hosts -> Hosts returns nothing.Device Profiling Rules (for example Vendor OUI, type Wireless Access Point) never process the AP.Network Access Policies whose User/Host Profile matches the AP MAC never match.Deleting the AP from Inventory makes the policy work temporarily; the AP returns under the FortiGate at the next poll or reconnect.The RADIUS log shows an Access-Accept with no VLAN attributes (example values):[Access-Request] AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF USER [aabbccddeeff] DEVICE [10.0.0.10] ATTRIBUTES [ User-Name = aabbccddeeff, Service-Type = Call-Check, Calling-Station-Id = AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF, NAS-Identifier = ACCESS-SW-01, NAS-Port-Type = Ethernet, NAS-Port-Id = 1/1/2 ] [Access-Accept] AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF USER [aabbccddeeff] DEVICE [10.0.0.10] ATTRIBUTES [ REST-HTTP-Status-Code = 200, Cleartext-Password = "aabbccddeeff", Class = 0x..., Hint = "...", Tmp-String-1 = "request" ]The Access-Accept carries no Tunnel-Type, Tunnel-Medium-Type or Tunnel-Private-Group-ID, so the switch keeps the port in its default VLAN.Cause:This is expected behavior. FortiNAC models FortiGate-managed FortiAPs as network devices (Inventory elements), not as hosts. When a Wireless Access Point connects to a managed switch port, FortiNAC changes the port type to WAP Uplink.By default, FortiNAC does not evaluate Network Access Policies for Wireless Access Points and does not enforce any policy on a WAP Uplink port. With no host record and no applicable policy, the MAB Access-Accept carries no VLAN.SolutionEnable Network Access Policy evaluation for Wireless Access Points. No other change is required when the Network Access Policy and port configuration are already in place.In the FortiNAC GUI, go to System -> Settings -> Network Device.Select Enable Network Access Policy for Wireless Access Points.Select Save Settings.Confirm the switch port where the FortiAP connects is a member of the Role-Based Access port group. This is required for the setting to take effect.Optional: Set Wireless Access Point Enforcement Group to a port group. FortiNAC adds a port to it when a Wireless Access Point connects; it does not remove the port automatically.Reconnect the FortiAP or bounce its switch port so a new MAB request is sent.Verification:The RADIUS Access-Accept for the AP MAC now includes Tunnel-Type = VLAN, Tunnel-Medium-Type = IEEE-802 and Tunnel-Private-Group-ID = the policy VLAN.Network -> Inventory -> switch -> Ports: The AP port shows the expected VLAN, and Port Changes records the change.Verify the VLAN assigned to the switch port interface.Notes:Deleting FortiAPs from Inventory is not a workaround; FortiNAC re-adds them under the FortiGate.The AP port must not be in the Authorized Access Points group, which prevents VLAN switching on the port.If the port is also in Reset Forced Default, set its Default VLAN equal to the policy VLAN to avoid the VLAN cycling between the two.Confirm RADIUS and VLAN switching are enabled in the switch Model Configuration, with a RADIUS attribute group that includes RFC VLAN attributes.Tunnel-mode SSIDs are preferred. With bridge-mode SSIDs, wireless client MACs also appear on the AP port, which can affect port classification and MAB on the switch.Alternative: Network Device Roles (role assigned to the FortiAP + mapping by port group and VLAN), with the port in Role-Based Access.Related articles:Administration Guide (FortiNAC-F 7.6): Network device settingsAdministration Guide (FortiNAC-F 7.6): Network device rolesWAP behavior when connected to WAP Uplink ports

topics.title: Preserving client IP addresses across AP group VLANs with Layer 3 intra controller roaming
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to enable a new Layer 3 intra-controller roaming feature on a bridge-mode SSID, so wireless clients can move between FortiAP groups that are mapped to different VLANs, while retaining their original IP address.ScopeFortiGate 60F with FortiOS 7.4.11 and two FortiAP-441K access points with FortiAP firmware 7.6.3, managed by the same FortiGate.The source lab used feature-specific STS builds. The version labels above identify the tested release families and do not establish support in every build. Confirm that the target build exposes 'l3-intra-roaming' before applying this configuration.Solution1. Prepare the environmentUse two authorized FortiAPs managed by the same FortiGate and broadcasting the same bridge-mode SSID. Configure the SSID authentication before applying the following changes. The selected test used WPA2 Personal.Create two managed AP groups and assign one access point to each:FortiAPAP groupClient VLANManagement IPFAP1-loungeNorth10010.10.201.2FAP2-officeSouth20010.10.202.2Provide the required VLANs, DHCP scopes, gateways, and routing. Ensure the FortiAPs can communicate directly, without NAT in the path, when using direct roaming mode.Advertise the SSID on both access points. The tested 5 GHz channels were 140 and 132. Adjust transmit power to provide overlapping coverage and allow the client to select another access point when moving. Check the RF environment before starting the test.2. Map the AP groups to VLANs and enable intra-controller roamingOn the FortiGate, edit the existing SSID object. Replace with its configured name. The groups North and South must already exist and contain the corresponding access points.config wireless-controller vap edit " " set local-bridging enable set vlan-pooling wtp-group config vlan-pool edit 100 set wtp-group "North" next edit 200 set wtp-group "South" next end set l3-roaming enable set l3-intra-roaming enable set l3-roaming-mode direct next endThe key setting is 'set l3-intra-roaming enable' in the SSID configuration. The VLAN pool associates each participating AP group with its local client VLAN. Configure both groups; enabling the roaming setting alone does not replace this mapping.These changes modify an existing SSID, not a complete SSID creation script. Preserve the existing authentication and radio assignments. Review existing VLAN pool entries before applying the example.3. Validate IP preservationConnect a client to the SSID and record its IP address, associated FortiAP, and VLAN. Start a continuous connectivity test to a reachable destination. Move the client between the coverage areas, then return to the original access point.In the FortiGate wireless client monitor, compare the IP, FortiAP, FortiAP IP, and VLAN fields. The access point and local VLAN context should change while the client IP remains unchanged during the roaming test.Figure 1: iPhone test across FAP1-lounge (VLAN 100) and FAP2-office (VLAN 200). Both records show the client IP 10.10.200.3. Customer SSID labels are redacted.Figure 2: The iPhone is shown back on FAP2-office in VLAN 200 with the same IP, 10.10.200.3.Figure 3: Android test showing the same client IP, 10.10.100.2, across the two FortiAPs and VLAN contexts.Figure 4: Windows test showing client IP 10.10.200.4 across the same VLAN 100 and VLAN 200 roaming path. Customer SSID and personal device labels are redacted.The tested monitor sometimes retained duplicate client records after roaming. The paired rows show the observed IP and VLAN contexts; they do not prove simultaneous associations. Correlate the monitor with reassociation events and the client-side connectivity test.ResultThe selected local-lab test successfully validated roaming between North/VLAN 100 and South/VLAN 200 with iPhone, Android, and Windows clients retaining their original IP addresses. The report also records successful return to the original access point.IP preservation applies to the tested roaming sequence. It does not imply that a client keeps its address indefinitely after disconnecting or rehoming. The results do not establish zero packet loss or a universal roaming-time guarantee.

topics.title: Capturing Zebra ZS300 BLE data with FortiAP for temperature monitoring
topics.summary: DescriptionConfigure BLE scanning on a FortiAP to collect advertisements from Zebra ZS300 temperature sensors for processing and visualization by an external application.ScopeThe main proof of concept used a FortiGate 60F running FortiOS 7.4.12 and a FortiAP-233G running firmware 7.4.5. A separate local validation used a FortiAP-234F.The workflow illustrates BLE scanning on both models. Configuration availability depends on the FortiAP model and firmware.Solution1. Configure BLE scanningOn the FortiGate, create a BLE profile using the scan parameters validated during the proof of concept:config wireless-controller ble-profile edit "ZEBRA-ZS300-BLE" set ble-scanning enable set scan-type active set scan-threshold "-90" set scan-period 4000 set scan-time 1000 set scan-interval 50 set scan-window 50 next endAssign the BLE profile to the FortiAP profile. Replace with the existing profile name.config wireless-controller wtp-profile edit " " set ble-profile "ZEBRA-ZS300-BLE" next endIf the FortiAP profile is shared, this change affects the other access points using it.2. Verify the BLE configurationFrom the FortiAP CLI, run:cw_diag -c ble-configThe following excerpt shows the scan configuration observed during the main proof of concept:WTP Bluetooth Low Energy Configuration: ble scan report interval : 30 ble scanning : enabled (mode=active,thresh=-90,period=4000,time=1000,intv=50,wind=50)BLE scanning must be enabled. The iBeacon and Eddystone advertising settings also displayed by this command describe advertisements transmitted by the FortiAP and are not required to interpret the Zebra sensor data.3. Verify sensor receptionPlace the active sensor within BLE coverage and run:cw_diag -c ble-scanThe following output is transcribed from the local validation screenshot:BLE_DEV (001/001), mac ce:c3:25:fc:4e:a0 gen : 1 rssi : -88 addr type : random name : GEOMOV14587_LE manufacture : first seen : Mar 17 14:55:48 last seen : Mar 17 14:55:48 channel : 38 raw data : 22 0201020f0947454f 4d4f563134353837 5f4c45020a00Use the known sensor MAC address and its serial-number mapping in the sensor inventory to identify the intended device. Check the reception timestamps, RSSI, and raw data field.For devices using random BLE addresses, verify the identity mapping instead of assuming that the displayed address remains permanent.Figure 1: BLE configuration and scan output from the FortiAP-234F used for local validation. The main laboratory used a FortiAP-233G. The screenshot illustrates the scan workflow on another model; it does not independently demonstrate Zebra temperature decoding.4. Display temperature dataDuring the proof of concept, an external collector accessed the FortiAP over SSH through an IPsec VPN and retrieved BLE scan output every five seconds. The external application identified the Zebra sensor, processed the captured payload, and displayed temperature information in a dashboard.The FortiAP provided BLE scan data. The external application decoded the payload, stored historical data, and visualized it on a dashboard.Figure 2: Dashboard supplied as evidence of the proof of concept. The displayed period includes 12,044 events, an average RSSI of -78 dBm, an average battery level of 68.5%, and an average temperature of -19.01 °C. The dashboard also displays a mean kinetic temperature of -19.18 °C. topics.title: RMA Information: Hardware failure and replacement with a spare unit on-site (support procedure)
topics.summary: Description This KB article describes, how to manage an RMA request (a hardware replacement request within the technical support contract) with the Fortinet Customer Service and Support (Fortinet CSS), when another (possibly temporary) spare unit is already available on-site. In case of a hardware failure on a Fortinet product and a need for replacement, when a spare unit is already available on-site (for example: a "cold spare" unit, or a temporarily loaned unit from a Fortinet reseller or distributor), for a smooth RMA exchange of the defective unit by the Fortinet CSS, Fortinet recommends to proceed as follows: 1. With the Fortinet CSS, create an RMA ticket first, using the serial number of the defective unit.2. In the RMA ticket, describe the problem with the defective unit, and make sure to mention to which spare/replacement unit (specify the serial number) the support contract will be transferred to.3. Once the RMA ticket has been created, request the Fortinet Customer Service (Fortinet CS) to transfer the support contract from the defective unit to the spare unit, possibly by creating another ticket (this time, a CS ticket), or making a phone call. Important step is to create an RMA ticket with Fortinet before transfering the support contract and all FortiGuard service subscriptions to the spare/replacement unit. Proceeding this way will prevent the defective unit to be considered as not covered by a valid support contract later on, resulting in an RMA refusal by Fortinet internal customer support systems. For more information on how to contact Fortinet CSS, please see our Contact Us page and refer to the Ticket Creation Guide, available for download on the Fortinet support portal (on the main Fortinet website, select Service & Support > Support Login > login with your credentials).

topics.title: How to fix "error firewall service custom protocol" after ADOM upgrade
topics.summary: Description A fix for the installation issue with multiple "firewall service custom" objects that may occur after an ADOM upgrade. Post vdom failed: error firewall service custom protocol- TCP_UDP_20101 TCP/UDP/SCTP:-999 - invalid value - prop[protocol]: option(TCP/UDP/SCTP) Copy objects for vdom Main_VDOM "firewall ssl-ssh-profile", "certificate-inspection", id=18459, SKIP - (null) "firewall ssl-ssh-profile", "deep-inspection", id=18474, SKIP - (null) Scope FortiManager. Solution When upgrading from FortiOS 7.4 to 7.6, the default protocol changes from TCP/UDP/SCTP to TCP/UDP/UDP-Lite/SCTP. To match this logic, a 7.6 ADOM should be used in FortiManager. However, it might appear that after upgrading the ADOM, "firewall service custom" objects fail to be installed. When drilling down to the object, it can be observed that the UUID of the object is set to ZERO, which is causing the issue during the installation: To resolve this problem and generate a correct UUID, it is possible to add the comment to the object, click the "Ok" button to update the object, and verify that a new UUID was generated. However, it may be challenging if it requires updating a bunch of such objects. To address this situation, use a script: Step 1: First, print a list of all objects to check how many have a ZERO UUID. execute fmpolic print-adom-object 167 +all Step 2: Take note of all affected objects and create a script. config firewall service custom edit "Jitsi_TCP_4443" unset uuid end Step 3: Run the script against the "Policy Package or ADOM DB". Step 4: Verify the object has a new, updated UUID and the installation runs without an error.

topics.title: Upgrade firmware fails with 'New image is too big'
topics.summary: Description This article describes troubleshooting steps for issues related to the error 'New image is too big '. Scope FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer. Solution Typically, this error occurs during a FortiAnalyzer or FortiManager 8.0.X firmware update when the target device lacks sufficient flash memory storage to accommodate the new firmware image. This is most commonly documented for FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer VM platforms, where the error message reads: 'New image is too big'. This error is not caused by a bug ; it is due to a system requirement to upgrade the products to the latest and larger firmware releases, as indicated here: The minimum size for the flash disk in FortiAnalyzer-VM is 4 GB Most common causes: Insufficient flash disk space : The flash partition does not have enough free space to store the new firmware image during the upgrade process. Small virtual disk allocation : The VM was originally provisioned with a flash disk that is too small for the target firmware version. Diagnostic steps: Take the firmware update from version 8.0.0 to 8.0.1 for FortiAnalyzer VM as an example. Check flash disk usage: Run the following command on the FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer CLI to view the flash disk size and current usage: diagnose system flash list Example output showing the flash disk status: ImageName Version TotalSize(KB) Used(KB) Use% BootImage RunningImage primary FLVM64-8.0-FW-build0105-260420 1006252 592344 59% Yes Yes If the Use% is high or the total size is too small for the target firmware, this confirms the issue. Resolution: Expand the flash disk (FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer VM). Take a config backup of the FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer. Shut down the VM using the following CLI command: execute shutdown Delete all snapshots and wait for the operations to be completed. Important note : Without deleting existing snapshots, the disk expansion on the hypervisor side will not be reflected in the flash memory expansion of the FortiManager or FortiAnalyzer. Expand Disk 1 (or 0) by 4 GB or more in the hypervisor. Note: Do not expand the virtual disk too much, as the additional space will not be available for data. Boot up the VM and verify the flash disk was automatically extended: diagnose system flash list Important note : In some cases, it has been observed that the Totalsize value remains 1006252 KB after the reboot despite the 4 GB assigned to disk 1, as confirmed also by the output of the command. FAZ # diagnose sys print partitions major minor #blocks name fstype 1 0 4096 ram0 ext4 1 1 4096 ram1 ext4 1 2 4096 ram2 1 3 4096 ram3 7 0 10240 loop0 ext2 253 0 4194304 zram0 ext4 8 0 4194304 sda 8 1 1048576 sda1 ext3 8 16 2147483648 sdb 8 32 2147483648 sdc 8 48 2147483648 sdd 252 0 6442438656 dm-0 253 1 425984 zram1 ext4 Referring to the first 2 rows starting with 8. Also, in this case, is possible to upload the new 'big' image; the error 'New image is too big' does not appear again. It happens because, at the beginning of the upgrade process, the partition sda1 is extended, the additional disk space is made available and formatted to support the new image, and the TotalSize is automatically increased to 2012008 KB , as can be verified by executing the commands again after the upgrade If the VM witnesses a file system error, run: diagnose system fsck harddisk Perform the firmware upgrade by manually uploading the firmware image and verify the error no longer appears. topics.title: FortiManager to FortiGate policy install fails with a custom protocol error
topics.summary: Description Troubleshooting steps for a custom protocol error that occurs when performing a policy installation to FortiGate. Scope FortiManager. Solution The following issue may be encountered by users when performing policy installation to FortiGate v7.6 to a v7.4 ADOM in FortiManager. This issue occurs because the protocol types defined in the default firewall service objects differ between ADOM versions. For example, in v7.4, the default protocol for the DNS service is TCP/UDP/SCTP , whereas in v7.6, it has been updated to TCP/UDP/UDP-Lite/SCTP . To resolve this issue, upgrade the ADOM to v7.6 so that the default firewall service object definitions in FortiManager align with those on the FortiGate. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiClient installer Download Link not working as expected
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot the FortiClient installer 'Download Link' not working properly. Scope FortiClient EMS version 7.4 and above. Solution After creating a FortiClient installer in FortiClient EMS, clicking on 'Download Link' should open a new browser tab and display the installer directory. Expected behavior: Issue symptoms that might occur: 'The requested resource was not found on this server.'. Solution: SSH to the FortiClient EMS server. Verify if the installer exists on the server; run the command: emscli execute ls /opt/forticlientems/data/clients/installers/default/ emscli execute ls /opt/forticlientems/data/clients/installers/default/ The FortiClient installer should exist in the directory: If the FortiClient installer does not exist, contact Support and share the related screenshots: 'The connection was reset.'. Solution: Verify that port 10443 to FortiClient EMS is reachable. In this example, the EMS IP is 192.168.188.44. Open Windows Command Prompt and run the command: telnet 192.168.188.44 10443 If it is showing a blank black screen, meaning it is reachable. This is the first checkpoint. Next is to verify the SSL handshake. Open a Windows Command Prompt and run the command: curl.exe -vk https://10.47.188.44:10443/installers/default/ / On the right, it should get a 'Moved Permanently' message: If it is showing 'Connection was reset', meaning there is some upstream devices blocking port 10443. Check further on upstream devices to see where the SSL handshake is failing. This is the second checkpoint. After identifying and resolving the issue on upstream devices (it can be Fortinet or non-Fortinet devices), the installer link should work fine. topics.title: FortiClient EMS - Invalid Credentials
topics.summary: I am writing to submit a critical product architectural improvement request regarding how FortiClient EMS 8.0.0 on Linux establishes secure directory integrations.During our recent deployment of FortiClient EMS 8.0.0 on Ubuntu 24, we encountered persistent authentication failures when connecting EMS to our Windows Server Domain Controllers via secure LDAPS (Port 636). Real-time debugging via the adconnector.log file revealed that the authentication loop continuously failed with the following explicit Windows SChannel error wrapper:LDAP Result Code 49 "Invalid Credentials": 80090302: LdapErr: DSID-0C09089D, comment: AcceptSecurityContext error, data 1In the Windows security subsystem, Windows Error Code 80090302 translates directly to SEC_E_UNSUPPORTED_FUNCTION. This protocol violation occurs because the FortiClient EMS backend engine is compiled to automatically encapsulate its Active Directory GUI bind traffic using an NTLM/SPNEGO negotiated token handshake.The Troubleshooting Barrier

replies.author: sjoshi
replies.text: this appears to be a protocol negotiation issue rather than a credential problem, since ldapsearch from the same host authenticates successfully. The most likely explanation is the Kerberos configuration format. FortiClient EMS supports both Kerberos and NTLM for LDAP(S) connections, and for Kerberos the Hostname field must contain the domain FQDN (not the DC IP), and the username must be case-sensitive in the format \ or @ .com. If your DCs are blocking NTLM, switching to the Kerberos format may resolve this without any code change. topics.title: Unable to delete a VDOM from FortiManager when its management VDOM is in a different ADOM
topics.summary: Description How to delete the VDOM using FortiManager when the management VDOM is not present in the same ADOM as the target VDOM. Scope FortiManager. Solution FortiManager enforces a device/VDOM model constraint that prevents deleting a VDOM while its management VDOM resides in a different ADOM. This article explains the constraint and provides two practical workarounds. FortiManager's ADOM (Administrative Domain) architecture determines how VDOMs are assigned and managed. In Normal Device Mode, all VDOMs from a single FortiGate must be placed in the same ADOM. In Advanced Device Mode, individual VDOMs from the same FortiGate can be assigned to separate ADOMs, enabling multi-tenant management. The deletion restriction occurs because FortiManager's device database tracks the management VDOM's ADOM assignment. When the management VDOM is in a different ADOM than the target VDOM, FortiManager cannot process the deletion through its normal device database operations. This is consistent with expected behavior where FortiManager displays errors when the management VDOM is not in the current ADOM for example, the error 'The management VDOM for device xxxxxx is not in the current advanced ADOM'. Workaround 1: Move the VDOM to the Same ADOM. Temporarily move the non-management VDOM so that both the management VDOM and the target VDOM reside in the same ADOM, then delete the VDOM. Workaround 2: Delete Directly on the FortiGate and Resync. Delete the VDOM directly on the FortiGate (bypassing FortiManager's ADOM restriction), then resynchronize the FortiGate on FortiManager. Verify the VDOM is removed from FortiManager's device database. Note : If the VDOM was created in FortiManager's device database but not properly saved, you may encounter an "Internal error" (code -20001) when attempting deletion. In such cases, run the following command on FortiManager to fix the database: diagnose cdb upgrade check resync-dev-vdoms This resyncs and removes any missing VDOMs from the device database.

topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiGate unable to ping FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer even the ping is allow
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot FortiGate unable to ping FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer even the ping is allow. Scope FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer. Solution Device information: FortiGate port1 = 10.47.6.72/20 ; port4 = 10.133.6.72/20. FortiAnalyzer port1 = 10.47.3.243/20 ; port3 = 10.133.3.243/20. Expected scenario: FortiGate port1 is able to ping FortiAnalyzer port1. FortiGate port4 is able to ping FortiAnalyzer port3. Issue scenario: FortiGate port1 is able to ping FortiAnalyzer port1. FortiGate port4 is unable to ping FortiAnalyzer port3. Check steps: In FortiAnalyzer, check that both port1 and port3 configurations are allowed to use the ping service. At FortiAnalyzer, check whether all Administrator Accounts are configured as Trusted Hosts. Solution steps: When in FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer, all Administrator Accounts are configured as Trusted Hosts, the FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer Administrative Access settings will be allowed based on the Trusted Host information. Therefore in FortiAnalyzer, one of the Administrator Accounts must be configured as a Trusted Host that only allows for the IP address range 10.133.0.0/16. After that, FortiGate port4 will be able to ping FortiAnalyzer port3, and also FortiGate port1 will be able to ping FortiAnalyzer port1. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: How to resolve the issue of FortiClient Mac installer not working when Apple's Gatekeeper is set to 'App Store only'
topics.summary: Description This article describes the issue of the FortiClient Mac installer not working when Apple's Gatekeeper is set to 'App Store only'. Scope FortiClient. Solution When trying to deploy the FortiClient Mac installer via a Jamf Pro instance, the installer generated by FortiClient/EMS does not work in this context. To resolve the issue of the FortiClient Mac installer not working with Gatekeeper, follow these steps: Locate the FortiClient app in Finder (e.g., Downloads folder). 'Right-click' (or 'Ctrl-click') the FortiClient app icon. Select Open from the context menu. A warning dialog will appear; select Open. This creates a specific exception for that specific application. After doing this once, FortiClient will open normally by double-clicking in the future. Alternatively, it is possible to try temporarily disabling Gatekeeper: Go to System Preferences -> Security & Privacy -> General . Select the lock icon and enter the password to make changes. Change the setting from App Store to App Store and identified developers (or anywhere if available on older macOS). Install FortiClient. Change the setting back to App Store after the installation is completed. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: SCEP decryption failure with aes-256-cbc encryption
topics.summary: Description This article describes the cause of SCEP decryption failures on FortiAuthenticator when receiving enrollment requests encrypted with aes-256-cbc from certain third-party devices. Scope FortiAuthenticator, FortiManager, FortiGate. Solution When a third-party device uses aes-256-cbc encryption for SCEP enrollment requests, FortiAuthenticator may fail to decrypt the PKCS#7 enveloped data. This results in a decryption failure during the SCEP process. Root cause: The issue is caused by a compatibility problem in how FortiAuthenticator handles SCEP requests encrypted with aes-256-cbc. While other encryption methods like des-ede3-cbc work correctly, requests using aes-256-cbc trigger a decryption error in the SCEP daemon. Symptoms: The following error messages appear in the FortiAuthenticator debug logs: PKCS7 message encrypted with aes-256-cbc (427) utils.cpp:386: decryption failed mo_pkcs7unwrap.cpp:526: cannot decrypt PKCS#7 enveloped data error:1C800064:Provider routines:ossl_cipher_unpadblock:bad decrypt Resolution: This is a known issue tracked under engineering ticket 1198353 and is expected to be resolved in an upcoming FortiAuthenticator 8.0.4 GA release. topics.title: Technical Tip: Unable to receive authentication code via SMS
topics.summary: Description This article describes the procedure for sending an authentication code through SMS when the user reports that the authentication code message was not received. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution If the SMS gateway message template is configured with the variable {{:token_code}} , but users receive a message without the OTP code, such as: "Your OTP login is . Valid for 3 minutes. Do not share the OTP." This indicates that the token code placeholder is not being substituted with the generated authentication code , resulting in a blank value in the SMS content. If the OTP code is missing when using the {{:token_code}} variable, modify the SMS gateway message template to: Your OTP login is {{:message}}. Valid for 3 minutes. Do not share the OTP. After updating the template, the authentication code will be included correctly in the SMS message delivered to the user. Configure the SMS gateway replacement message as shown below: Plain Text Your OTP login is {{:token_code}}. Valid for 3 minutes. Do not share the OTP. Show more lines The {{:token_code}} placeholder will be replaced with the generated OTP, ensuring that users receive the authentication code in the SMS message. Modify the replacement message to {{:token_code}} . Navigate to System -> Administration -> Replacement messages . After changing the replacement message variable to {{:message}} , the authentication code is populated correctly in the SMS message. Example configuration: Plain Text Your OTP login is {{:message}}. Valid for 3 minutes. Do not share the OTP. Show more lines Result: Plain Text Your OTP login is 123456. Valid for 3 minutes. Do not share the OTP. Show more lines The {{:message}} variable is replaced with the generated OTP, allowing the user to receive the authentication code in the SMS message. When using the Test Settings option, the SMS message may be received as: Plain Text Your OTP login is FAC_FQDN. Valid for 3 minutes. Do not share the OTP. This behavior is expected because FortiAuthenticator does not generate an actual token code during the test. Instead, it sends a test message in which the {{:message}} variable is replaced with the FortiAuthenticator FQDN (FAC_FQDN) to verify SMS gateway connectivity and message delivery. Note : When using the Test Settings option, the test message will not contain an OTP code because FortiAuthenticator does not generate a token during the test process. As a result, the message will contain the test value instead of an actual authentication code. To verify OTP delivery with a generated token code, perform a real authentication request rather than using Test Settings .

topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: SCIM user and group synchronization failure between FortiAuthenticator and FortiGate
topics.summary: Description This article explains how to resolve an issue where users and groups do not synchronize from FortiAuthenticator to FortiGate despite a successful TLS connection. Scope FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator. Solution When FortiAuthenticator acts as a SCIM client and FortiGate acts as a SCIM server, the synchronization of users and groups may fail if the base URL is configured incorrectly. Even if the TLS connection is established, the FortiGate SCIM daemon may fail to associate the incoming request with the configured SCIM client. The issue occurs when the base-url in the FortiGate SCIM configuration includes a port number. The base URI should typically consist of the protocol, domain name, and initial path. Including the port number in the base-url prevents the FortiGate from correctly identifying the SCIM client, resulting in the following debug error: diagnose debug reset diagnose debug application scim -1 diagnose debug enable url:https://10.5.146.127/scim/v2/Users/user_2 HTTP/1.1 used to find client:NULL. can't found client or client disabled. change state from wait_req to disconnect change state from disconnect to done change state from init to accepting change state from accepting to connect SSL_accept succeeded. Resolution Log in to the FortiGate command line interface. Verify the current SCIM configuration to check for a port number in the base-url: show user scim Remove the port number from the base-url. For example, change https://10.5.146.127:44559/scim/v2 to https://10.5.146.127/scim/v2: config user scim edit set base-url "https:// /scim/v2" next end Perform the user and group synchronization from FortiAuthenticator. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: How to resolve 'Error importing configuration file' in FortiClient on macOS
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to resolve the 'Error importing configuration file' message when importing a modified FortiClient configuration file on macOS. Scope FortiClient. Solution When importing a FortiClient configuration file through the FortiClient GUI on macOS, the following error may be encountered: The FortiClient FCConfig command-line utility can be used to export and import the configuration instead of using the FortiClient GUI. Creating a backup of the existing FortiClient configuration is recommended before making any configuration changes. Export the FortiClient configuration: Open Terminal and navigate to the FortiClient binary directory: cd "/Library/Application Support/Fortinet/FortiClient/bin" Export the existing FortiClient configuration: sudo ./FCConfig -f "/Users/$USER/Downloads/settings.xml" -m all -o export The exported configuration file is saved under the Downloads directory: /Users/ /Downloads/settings.xml Keep a copy of the original settings.xml file as a backup before making any modifications. Modify the configuration: Open settings.xml using a text or XML editor and make the required configuration changes. Save the modified file as settings.xml . Import the configuration using FCConfig. Confirm that settings.xml is located in the Downloads directory. Open Terminal and navigate to the FortiClient binary directory: cd "/Library/Application Support/Fortinet/FortiClient/bin" Import the configuration: sudo ./FCConfig -m all -f "/Users/$USER/Downloads/settings.xml" -o import After the import is completed, open FortiClient and verify that the required configuration has been applied. Importing the configuration to additional Mac devices: If multiple Mac devices require the same FortiClient configuration, the successfully tested settings.xml file can be copied to the additional devices. Copy settings.xml to the Downloads directory of each destination Mac. Run the following commands on each destination Mac: cd "/Library/Application Support/Fortinet/FortiClient/bin" sudo ./FCConfig -m all -f "/Users/$USER/Downloads/settings.xml" -o import After the import is completed, open FortiClient and verify that the required configuration has been applied. Note: The -m all option exports or imports all applicable FortiClient configuration contained in the XML file. Creating a backup of the existing FortiClient configuration is recommended before importing a modified configuration. When using the same settings.xml file on multiple Mac devices, confirm that all destination devices are intended to use the same FortiClient configuration. For large-scale deployments, FortiClient EMS or an appropriate MDM solution can be considered instead of manually importing the configuration on each Mac device. topics.title: Technical Tip: FortiClient installer download fails when the package name contains spaces
topics.summary: Description This article describes a FortiClient installer download failure associated with spaces in the installer package name and provides a workaround with examples. Scope FortiClient EMS 7.4.8 and FortiClient EMS Cloud. Solution A space in the installer package name may cause the executable download to fail, even when the package directory is accessible and lists the installer files. Example 1: Package name containing a space: For the package named fct 7.4 , the directory listing displays the executable forticlientsetup_7.4.8_x64.exe. However, selecting the executable returns the following error: Not Found The requested resource was not found on this server. Example download path: /installers/default/fct%207.4/forticlientsetup_7.4.8_x64.exe The %20 sequence represents the space in the package name. The directory listing shows that the file is present, but does not confirm that its download will succeed. Example 2: Package name without spaces: For the package named 7.4.8 , selecting the executable opens the browser's Save As dialog, showing that the download can be initiated. Example download path: /installers/default/7.4.8/forticlientsetup_7.4.8_x64.exe Workaround Create a new installer package in FortiClient EMS using a name without spaces, such as prueba_server_EMS. Wait for package creation to complete. Open the newly generated download link and select the executable to verify that the download starts successfully. Distribute the new download link after validation. Replacing %20 with an underscore in the existing URL alone does not create a corresponding package. Use the download link generated for the newly created installer. Additional checks: If the download still fails, verify the required network connectivity and license synchronization status before generating another package. Planned improvement: An improvement related to installer download links for package names containing spaces is currently planned for FortiClient EMS 7.4.9 . Inclusion remains subject to successful QA validation and may change. Consult the release notes when the version becomes available to confirm inclusion. Until the improvement is available and validated, continue using installer package names without spaces. topics.title: Technical Tip: Clarification of the 'cannot get DNS name of domain x.x.x.x from Domain Manager' in FSSO debug log when Entra ID is being used
topics.summary: Description This article clarifies the error log message 'cannot get DNS name of domain x.x.x.x from Domain Manager' in the FSSO debug log in the FortiAuthenticator when Entra ID is being used and remote LDAP is not configured. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution FortiAuthenticator FSSO supports logon events from native Microsoft Entra ID-joined workstations through the FortiClient SSOMA (FortiClient Single Sign-On Mobility Agent). For example, when an endpoint joined to Microsoft Entra ID connects to the network, FortiClient SSOMA sends the user identity and endpoint IP address to FortiAuthenticator. FortiAuthenticator then performs a group membership lookup against Microsoft Entra ID through the OAuth API and shares the retrieved Entra ID group membership information with the FortiGate. The configuration example can be found in the following document: FortiAuthenticator SSOMA for native Microsoft Entra ID joined workstation In a normal scenario, the following FSSO debug messages can be observed at 'https:// /debug/fsso-agent/' when FortiAuthenticator processes the SSOMA logon event and performs the Entra ID group membership lookup through the OAuth API: 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] FortiClient connected: 2540D4605FDD4FB125FD1B532DECD268/192.168.1.20 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] Received 1 event(s) from FCT: 192.168.1.20 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] FCT LOGON 2026-02-10-10:50:23/1970-01-01-10:00:00 FortiClient (null):L2003.TESTDOMAIN.COM/192.168.1.20 TESTDOMAIN.COM/JOHN.SMITH 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] Exclusion List [DEBUG]: Looking up user JOHN.SMITH [3,-1] in exclusion table 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] FCT 192.168.1.20: SSOMA UUID: 2540D4605FDD4FB125FD1B532DECD268 EMS S/N: (null) EMS tenant ID: (null) 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] FCT 192.168.1.20: domain TESTDOMAIN.COM tenant ID 443EE9E8-11FF-4C82-9E41-39331045260A 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] Logon Cache [DEBUG]: Allow newer FortiClient logon L2003.TESTDOMAIN.COM:192.168.1.20 to overwrite existing older FortiClient logon L2003.TESTDOMAIN.COM:192.168.1.20 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] Group Cache [DEBUG]: cache disabled for FortiClient logon, try to load user groups for TESTDOMAIN.COM/JOHN.SMITH 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] FCT 192.168.1.20: pending user TESTDOMAIN.COM/JOHN.SMITH group lookup with tenant ID 442EE2E1-22FF-4C82-9E41-39321045460A 08/19/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] FCT disconnected: 192.168.1.20 There could be a scenario following error log is observed when FortiAuthenticator is doing the group membership lookup in Entra ID: 02/10/2026 08:28:20 [9DC456C0] FortiClient connected: 2540D4605FDD4FB125FD1B532DECD268/192.168.1.20 02/10/2026 08:28:20 [9DC456C0] Received 1 event(s) from FCT: 192.168.1.20 02/10/2026 08:28:20 [9DC456C0] FCT LOGON 2026-02-10-08:28:19/1970-01-01-10:00:00 FortiClient (null):L2003.TESTDOMAIN.COM/192.168.1.20 TESTDOMAIN.COM/JOHN.SMITH 02/10/2026 08:28:20 [9DC456C0] Exclusion List [DEBUG]: Looking up user JOHN.SMITH [3,-1] in exclusion table 02/10/2026 08:28:20 [9DC456C0] FCT 192.168.1.20: SSOMA UUID: 2250D4202FDD4FB125FD1B512DECD268 EMS S/N: (null) EMS tenant ID: (null) 02/10/2026 08:28:20 [9DC456C0] FCT 192.168.1.20: cannot get DNS name of domain TESTDOMAIN.COM from Domain Manager 02/10/2026 08:28:20 [9D3E16C0] FCT session SSL connection established (172.11.0.80) The error 'cannot get DNS name of domain TESTDOMAIN.COM from Domain Manager' does not necessarily indicate a DNS resolution problem or an issue with the FortiAuthenticator Domain Manager itself. Instead, it is related to how FortiAuthenticator processes the incoming FSSO logon event received from FortiClient SSOMA. The general procedure is as follows: When FortiAuthenticator receives an SSOMA logon event from a native Microsoft Entra ID-joined endpoint, it requires the tenant ID provided by FortiClient SSOMA in order to perform the Microsoft Entra ID group membership lookup. In the working example above, the Tenant ID 443EE9E8-11FF-4C82-9E41-39331045260A was present, which can be found in the debug log. FortiAuthenticator can therefore associate the logon with the correct Microsoft Entra ID tenant and retrieve the user's group membership through OAuth. If the tenant ID is missing from the SSOMA logon event, FortiAuthenticator cannot identify the corresponding Entra ID tenant. It then falls back to processing the user as an on-premises Active Directory user. As part of this fallback process, FortiAuthenticator queries the Domain Manager for the corresponding domain and attempts to perform the group lookup through a configured remote LDAP server. If no matching remote LDAP server or domain is configured on FortiAuthenticator, the error 'cannot get DNS name of domain x.x.x.x from Domain Manager' is generated. In this scenario, troubleshooting should focus on the FortiClient/SSOMA side to determine why the tenant ID is not included in the logon information sent to FortiAuthenticator. Review the FortiClient SSOMA debug logs and verify that the endpoint

topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: certificate-based VPN authentication on FortiClient Android fails for devices managed by Microsoft Intune
topics.summary: Description This article describes a configuration issue that prevents certificate-based VPN authentication on FortiClient Android to work correctly, when the device running FortiClient Android is managed by Microsoft Intune. This article also proposes a proper solution for the issue in question. Scope FortiClient EMS, FortiClient Android. Solution FortiClient EMS supports Microsoft Intune integration, including FortiClient Android and FortiClient iOS for mobile platforms. Certificate-based VPN authentication can be configured to authenticate FortiClient Android and FortiClient iOS mobile devices. The Intune Deployment provides all the details on how to deploy FortiClient using Microsoft Intune integration. Certificates can be deployed to mobile devices using two distinct certificate profiles for Microsoft Intune (see Trusted root certificate profiles for Microsoft Intune ): SCEP certificate profile. PKCS certificate profile. In the course of certificate-based VPN authentication setup procedure, if an SCEP certificate profile is deployed to Android devices, no configured VPN connections can be established. FortiClient Android will fail immediately, without trying to connect to the FortiGate unit (VPN peer device). Due to a Microsoft Intune limitation, SCEP certificate profiles do not support VPN configuration for general Android devices. Therefore, FortiClient Android does not work with an SCEP certificate profile. To solve this issue with the FortiClient Android and Microsoft Intune integration, use a PKCS certificate profile. When deploying certificate-based VPN authentication to FortiClient Android, the only supported certificate profile type is PKCS. SCEP certificate profiles are only supported for FortiClient iOS. android FortiClient EMS Like Reply Follow Share Powered by Gainsight Terms & Conditions Cookie settings Accessibility statement Sign up Already have an account? topics.title: Technical Tip: FortiClient VPN IKEv2 Token login not working when using EAP-MS-AUTH (mschapv2)
topics.summary: Description This article describes an issue that occurs when attempting to log in with a user account that has a second factor assigned to it. Removing the token from the user lets the login succeed. Scope FortiAuthenticator, FortiClient, FortiGate with IPsec IKEv2 dial-up VPN and FortiToken 2FA. Solution A user with a token assigned to the user account fails to log in. At the time of failure, the FortiAuthenticator RADIUS debug log shows entries similar to the following: 2026-09-01T17:07:40.780491+02:00 FortiAuthenticator radiusd[48048]: (2) eap: Peer sent packet with method EAP GTC (6) 2026-09-01T17:07:40.780499+02:00 FortiAuthenticator radiusd[48048]: (2) eap: Calling submodule eap_gtc to process data 2026-09-01T17:07:40.780508+02:00 FortiAuthenticator radiusd[48048]: (2) eap_gtc: # Executing group from file /usr/etc/raddb/sites-enabled/default 2026-09-01T17:07:40.780516+02:00 FortiAuthenticator radiusd[48048]: (2) eap_gtc: Auth-Type FACAUTH { 2026-09-01T17:07:40.780524+02:00 FortiAuthenticator radiusd[48048]: (2) facauth: This is a response to Access-Challenge 2026-09-01T17:07:40.780533+02:00 FortiAuthenticator radiusd[48048]: (2) facauth: ERROR: partial auth user not found A 'partial auth' user is a user who has passed the first factor (password) but has not yet completed the second factor (token code). The error means the token response arrived, but FortiAuthenticator no longer holds the authentication context from the first step. The authentication flow is as follows: FortiClient initiates an IKEv2 connection. IKEv2 requires EAP for user authentication, and FortiClient offers EAP-TTLS and EAP-MSCHAPv2. The user's password is validated successfully, and FortiAuthenticator sends an Access-Challenge requesting the token code. FortiClient returns the token code (EAP-GTC in the log above). FortiAuthenticator cannot match this response to the pending partial authentication, logs 'partial auth user not found', and rejects the request. This behavior is expected when FortiAuthenticator is not configured to allow 2FA for this type of EAP authentication. Note that FortiAuthenticator supports EAP-TTLS with 2FA as of version 8.0.4 and it is recommended to switch to EAP-TTLS when possible due to security considerations on EAP-MSCHAPv2. Enable the setting that allows two-factor authentication for IKEv2 EAP authentication from FortiClient, as described in the FortiAuthenticator Administration Guide under Policies . In short: Go to GUI -> Authentication -> RADIUS Service -> Policies and edit the policy matching the FortiGate RADIUS client. Go to 'Authentication factors' and expand the 'Advanced options'. Enable the setting 'Allow OTP for EAP-MSCHAPv2 Authentication with FortiClient'. Save the policy and test the VPN connection again. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Resolving authentication errors for child domain users in FortiAuthenticator
topics.summary: Description This article describes a solution to the authentication error encountered by child domain users when logging in to VPN via FortiAuthenticator. The user may experience an error message indicating that the machine is protected by an authentication firewall and the specified account is not allowed to authenticate to the machine. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution After upgrading FortiAuthenticator from version 6.5.6 to 6.6.9 , authentication failures may occur for users from a child domain. The following error is seen in the RADIUS logs: mschap: ERROR: Program returned code (1) and output 'Logon Failure: The machine you are logging onto is protected by an authentication firewall. The specified account is not allowed to authenticate to the machine. (0xc0000413)' To resolve the authentication issue for child domain users: Navigate to Authentication -> Remote Auth. Servers -> LDAP . Edit the configured Active Directory LDAP server. Under Windows Active Directory Domain Authentication , enable Allow Trusted Domain . Ensure that the FortiAuthenticator is joined to the Active Directory domain. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiAuthenticator HA secondary node failing to synchronize TACACS+ related tables
topics.summary: Description This article describes the issue of a FortiAuthenticator High Availability (HA) secondary node failing to synchronize TACACS+ related tables. The user may experience issues with TACACS+ clients, policy mapping, and policy-realm-group mappings not being synchronized between the primary and secondary nodes. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution In certain scenarios, the TACACS+ related database tables on the FortiAuthenticator HA secondary node fail to synchronize correctly with the primary node. To resolve the issue of a FortiAuthenticator HA secondary node failing to synchronize TACACS+ related tables, follow these steps: Navigate to System -> Dashboard -> HA Status on the load balancer node and select the Rebuild Tables button. This causes the load-balancing node to rebuild its database from information synced from the primary. If the tables appear to be in sync (same number of entries) but the status still shows out of sync, recalculate the cluster checksums by navigating to the debug page of the primary FortiAuthenticator at https:// /debug, then go to High Availability -> Loadbalancing HA Sync and select Recalculate LB-HA checksums . Verify that TACACS+ configuration references objects (e.g., remote servers, groups) that exist on the load-balancing node. If a TACACS+ policy references a remote LDAP server that is not present on the load-balancing node, this will result in an error. Check the FortiAuthenticator version and consider upgrading to the latest version if necessary, as there may be known issues with older versions. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Authentication Failure for Administrator Role Users After Upgrading FortiAuthenticator
topics.summary: Description This article describes an issue where administrator role users are unable to authenticate after upgrading FortiAuthenticator from version 6.6.2 to 6.6.10, while other users can log in successfully. The issue is related to CHAP authentication. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution If an administrator-role user is unable to authenticate through SSL VPN after upgrading FortiAuthenticator to version 6.6.10, recreate the affected user account in FortiAuthenticator and reassign the FortiToken. Perform the following steps: Delete the affected administrator user from FortiAuthenticator. Re-import the user from the configured LDAP server. Reassign the FortiToken to the newly imported user. Test SSL VPN authentication with the affected user. After completing these steps, the user should be able to authenticate successfully through SSL VPN. This procedure can be used as a workaround when only specific administrator-role users are affected following the FortiAuthenticator upgrade. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Linux FortiClient installation fails RPM digest verification in Fedora 43 and later
topics.summary: Description This article describes a known issue that causes FortiClient installations on distributions using DNF5 to fail due to a lack of digest. Scope FortiClient Linux. Linux distributions using RPM v6.0, such as Fedora 43 and higher. Solution Fedora Linux 43 and higher updates the included RPM package manager to RPM 6.0, which deprecates support for SHA1 digests. When attempting to install the FortiClient v7.4.7 and earlier as an RPM package with DNF on these distributions, the install will fail and the following error message may be seen: package forticlient-7.4.7.5438-1.el7.x86_64 does not verify: no digest This occurs because the current FortiClient RPM package headers only including SHA1 digests. Workaround: DNF does not allow skipping the digest check for packages. It is possible to workaround this issue using a different package management tool, for example the included RPM: sudo dnf install dnf-utils nss-tools sudo rpm -i --nodigest forticlient-7.4.7.5438-1.el7.x86_64.rpm Note: Unlike DNF, RPM does not automatically install dependencies. If the FortiClient installation still fails, verify any missing dependencies. Resolution: The issue is resolved in the following FortiClient Linux versions, which include a SHA256 signature: FortiClient Linux v7.4.8. FortiClient Linux v8.0.0. Note: the latest FortiClient Standalone version is currently v7.4.7. A FortiClient Standalone version with the fix is planned for release in FortiClient Linux v8.0.2. topics.title: Technical Tip: How to fix BdsDxe : failed to load Boot0001 UEFI NUTANUX VDISK in Nutanix Environment
topics.summary: Description This article describes a failed deployment of a FortiAnalyzer instance when performing VM migrations from VMware (ESXi) to Nutanix. Scope FortiAnalyzer. Solution Error: Reason: Wrong boot mode selection: FortiAnalyzer firmware images have strict requirements regarding the hypervisor BIOS type. The boot disk is attached to the wrong bus: FortiAnalyzer images expect the virtual disk to be mapped correctly so the bootloader can initialize. Missing or unassigned secondary data: DiskFortiAnalyzer is a logging and reporting tool; it cannot function or boot correctly without a dedicated storage partition. Resolution: Change the boot mode in the Nutanix Environment: In the Nutanix Prism console, go to Update VM -> Boot Configuration -> Change the boot mode from UEFI to Legacy BIOS (or Default) . Cloned .qcow2 boot image disk: Clone the image and explicitly attach it to the SCSI bus (e.g., SCSI Index 0). Add a new disk to the instance: Create a second, empty disk on the SCSI bus (e.g., 100 GB+ depending on licensing requirements) alongside the primary boot disk.

topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiClient auto-patch failure due to certificate validation issues
topics.summary: Description This article describes a scenario where the FortiClient auto-patch feature fails to download and install patches due to certificate validation issues. The user may encounter an error code 60, indicating a problem with the TLS certificate validation. Scope FortiClient v7.2 and v7.4. Solution The FortiClient vulnerability scan logs will show the following error: installerURL: https://github.com/notepad-plus-plus/notepad-plus-plus/releases/download/v8.9.1/npp.8.9.1.Installer.x64.exe ... Downloading installer. Attempt: 1/3 Download attempt 1 failed with error code: 60 Downloading installer. Attempt: 2/3 Download attempt 2 failed with error code: 60 Downloading installer. Attempt: 3/3 Download attempt 3 failed with error code: 60 ... Downloading Error. Max attempts reached. Please check the installer URL: https://github.com/notepad-plus-plus/notepad-plus-plus/releases/download/v8.9.1/npp.8.9.1.Installer.x64.exe This log can be found on the following path and the file name is vcm_result: 'C:\Program Files\Fortinet\FortiClient\logs\vcm'. To resolve the FortiClient Auto-Patch failure due to certificate validation issues, follow these steps: Verify that the Windows Automatic Root Certificate Update feature is enabled on the endpoint. This feature is enabled by default on Windows 10 and later versions. Check the Windows Trusted Root Certification Authorities store to ensure it is up-to-date. The store can be updated manually by running the command: certutil -generateSSTFromWU roots.sst certutil -addstore -f root roots.sst Identify the missing root certificate causing the issue. This can be done by extracting the failing URL from the FortiClient logs and inspecting the certificate chain using tools like OpenSSL or Certutil. Deploy the missing root certificate to the Local Computer Trusted Root Certification Authorities store via GPO, SCCM, or Intune. Alternatively, upgrade to FortiClient versions 7.4.9 or 8.0.1, which include a fix for this behavior. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Error 'Image validation failed: The current image model number is different from the appliance's.' when trying to upgrade VM from firmware version 6.6.7
topics.summary: Description This article describes how the error 'Image validation failed: The current image model number is different from the appliance's.' can occur on FortiAuthenticator VM when trying to update from firmware version 6.6.7, and how to resolve it. Scope FortiAuthenticator VM v6.6.7. Solution Under some circumstances, the error message 'Image validation failed: The current image model number is different from the appliance's.' may crop up when trying to upgrade a VM from firmware version 6.6.7. The error usually includes the detail '(current appliance model is FACVMS)'. After uploading the target firmware, FortiAuthenticator can show an error as depicted here: This occurs under the following conditions: The FortiAuthenticator VM is currently in firmware version 6.6.7 (either deployed or upgraded to it). A subscription license was uploaded to FortiAuthenticator VM. Subscription licenses can be identified by the serial number beginning with 'FACVMSxxxxxxxxx' and is visible in the dashboard. Subscription licenses are only meant to be activated on firmware version 8.0 and higher, but firmware version 6.6.7 allows subscription licenses to be applied in error (tracked under Engineering ID 1229991). This breaks the upgrade process, as the VM considers itself a different model and no longer accepts the proper model firmware images. Firmware version 6.6.8 and higher in the v6.6 branch do not allow uploading a subscription license in order to prevent this error. There are two options to solve this: If a different (non-subscription) VM license is available, that can be applied instead to override the subscription license. Once the non-subscription license is validated, the FortiAuthenticator VM allows upgrades again as expected, and the subscription license can be reapplied after upgrading to v8.0.x. Set up a new (unlicensed) VM, upgrade it to firmware version 8.0.x, and then apply the subscription license. This option means a loss of configuration. Switching to a different VM and restoring a configuration backup is not an option, as the VM license information is part of the configuration backup, and the error will persist through migrating the VM. This issue is most commonly observed in Azure VMs, as the marketplace templates start out in firmware version 6.6.7. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Incorrect VLAN assignment when using FortiAuthenticator dynamic VLANs
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot incorrect VLAN assignment when FortiAuthenticator is used to return dynamic VLAN attributes in RADIUS Access-Accept messages. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution Incorrect VLAN assignment may occur when FortiAuthenticator is configured for RADIUS Authentication if the same remote LDAP user or computer object is a member of more than one Active Directory or FortiAuthenticator user group, and when each group has a different RADIUS VLAN attribute configured. For example, if a user or device is a member of both the Students and the Staff group, then the FortiAuthenticator will return both VLANs to the NAC (e.g., FortiGate). Since the NAC (Network Enforcement Device, e.g. a FortiGate) can only assign 1 x VLAN, the latter of the two will be assigned to the client device, which may or may not be correct, possibly resulting in a Student being placed in the Staff VLAN (or vice versa). To troubleshoot this behaviour, check the RADIUS Access-Accept message in FortiAuthenticator's RADIUS debug (i.e. https:// /debug/radius) and confirm whether more than one VLAN is being returned. Correct example (1 x PVID is returned): Tunnel-Medium-Type += IEEE-802 Tunnel-Private-Group-Id += "58" Tunnel-Type += VLAN Problem example (2 x PVIDs are returned): Tunnel-Medium-Type += IEEE-802 Tunnel-Medium-Type += IEEE-802 Tunnel-Private-Group-Id += "58" Tunnel-Type += VLAN Tunnel-Private-Group-Id += "64" Tunnel-Medium-Type += IEEE-802 Tunnel-Type += VLAN If more than one VLAN (referred to as Tunnel-Private-Group-ID) is returned, check the user's group membership (for example in Active Directory) and/or the Synced User Groups on the FortiAuthenticator itself (as it is possible to add user/devices by to multiple groups) and correct it such that the user is only a member of one group.

topics.title: Technical Tip: FortiClient frequently disconnect from EMS cloud telemetry connection
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to check when FortiClient frequently disconnects from the EMS cloud telemetry connection Scope FortiClient EMS v7.2 and v7.4 onwards. Solution Confirm whether the network environment has implemented deep inspection or certificate replacement. Test the connection to the EMS cloud telemetry using a mobile hotspot to cross-verify. Access the path provided below to review either FortiESNAC_1.log or FortiESNAC_2.log based on the latest modification date. C:\Program Files\Fortinet\FortiClient\logs\trace Review the logs for the error message below, which indicates the EMS cloud rejected the telemetry connection because the certificate issuer is a third party.
