topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Addressing ZTNA SAML double authentication prompt
topics.summary: Description This article describes an issue with intermittent double/duplicate login prompts during ZTNA SAML authentication, explains the root cause, and offers a solution. Scope FortiGate. FortiClient. SAML. ZTNA. Solution When a ZTNA user authenticates via SAML but is immediately prompted to authenticate again, two issues may be at play. SAML authentication session has expired. Signed sign-on URL (SAML authentication query) has expired. On FortiGate, the SAML session lifetime is governed by the remoteauthtimeout setting (e.g., 300s). Example below: config system global set remoteauthtimeout 300 end For more information, refer to Technical Tip: 'Error: The authentication did not complete within the specified timeout. Please try again.' when connecting VPN using SAML . The validity of the signed authentication request is controlled by auth-sign-timeout (default 120s). Example: config web-proxy global set auth-sign-timeout 300 end Note : This setting is only available starting FortiOS v7.6.5 (ref. New features or enhancements ). The signed sign-on URL explained. When FortiClient wants to reach a ZTNA destination, the FortiGate sends it to the SAML login page. Before that, FortiGate includes information about the intended ZTNA connection in the URL itself as a signed, time-stamped query parameter (?sq=). Example URL: https://ztna.example.com/remote/saml/login?sq=k6VrYXhJdXJ-6aBAv7HULBFYm3_xOHJr6KsNq8bbEnRjFrpDAAAAALgBEOt_AAAAH32DagAAAAC1BGNwdHlwZT1ja2F1dGgmc2NoZW1lPWh0dHBz... The sq parameter is base64-encoded. Decoded, it encodes the connection details, for example: host=ztna.example.com port=443 rule=1 uri=https://ztna.example.com/... ctype=ckauth scheme=https So, the signed query is a cryptographically stamped token describing which ZTNA destination the user is asking to reach, and when it was issued. It carries an embedded expiration, which auth-sign-timeout controls. Troubleshooting double-prompt for ZTNA SAML Authentication. To verify whether the signed query expiration is the issue, run the commands within the FortiGate CLI before making the ZTNA SAML authentication attempt: diagnose debug application wad -1 diagnose debug application samld -1 diagnose debug enable The CLI output confirming the issue will look similar to the one below: WARNING Query expired, expire=1787246900, now=1787246909 failed to verify query To address this issue, set auth-sign-timeout on the FortiGate so the signed sign-on URL stays valid long enough for realistic IdP login times: config web-proxy global set auth-sign-timeout 300 end Once set, repeat the authentication process and verify the fix. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: 'ZTNA Application Not Found' error with 'Error Code 022' in ZTNA TCP forwarding
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot the ZTNA Application Not Found error with error code 022 when FortiClient attempts to access an application using ZTNA TCP forwarding. Scope FortiGate, FortiClient, ZTNA. Solution When attempting to access an application using ZTNA TCP forwarding, FortiClient may display the ZTNA Application Not Found error with error code 022: This error can occur when the destination application requested by FortiClient does not match a real server configured under the FortiGate ZTNA Access Proxy API gateway. Collect the FortiClient diagnostic logs from an affected endpoint and review the following log file: FCDiagData\general\logs\trace\fortitcs\_1.log Search for ZTNA Application Not Found or error code 022 and review the corresponding TCP-forwarding request. For example: [2026-08-04 17:23:52.3686208] [fortitcs] Request: GET /tcp?address=app.example.com&port=443&tls=0 HTTP/1.1 Host: ztna.example.com:10443 Accept: */* Authorization: ***** Cookie: ***** Upgrade: tcp-forwarding/1.0 User-Agent: Forticlient X-Fos-Auth: [2026-08-04 17:23:52.4849079] [fortitcs] response code: 403 html Reply: ZTNA Access Denied ZTNA Application Not Found Error Code: 022 Error Message: The page you requested has been blocked because the real server in the API gateway cannot be found. The request identifies the destination application and destination port: GET /tcp?address=app.example.com&port=443 In this example: The destination application is app.example.com. The destination port is 443. The ZTNA Access Proxy is ztna.example.com. The ZTNA Access Proxy listener port is 10443. Review the ZTNA Access Proxy configuration on the FortiGate: show firewall access-proxy For example: config firewall access-proxy edit "ZTNA_ACCESS_PROXY" config api-gateway edit 1 set url-map "/tcp" set service tcp-forwarding config realservers edit 1 set address "ztna_https_servers" set mappedport 443 next end next end next end The real server in this example accepts applications referenced by ztna_https_servers on TCP port 443. If ztna_https_servers is an address group, verify its members: show firewall addrgrp ztna_https_servers For example: config firewall addrgrp edit "ztna_https_servers" set member "server1.example.com" "server2.example.com" next end In this example, FortiClient requests app.example.com on TCP port 443. However, app.example.com is not included in the address group referenced by the applicable real server. If the application is intended to be accessible through this ZTNA TCP-forwarding configuration, verify that an appropriate address object exists and add it to the address group referenced by the real server. For example: config firewall addrgrp edit "ztna_https_servers" append member "app.example.com" next end After updating the configuration, retry access to the application and confirm that the ZTNA Application Not Found error with error code 022 no longer occurs. Note: FortiClient can process multiple ZTNA connections concurrently. When reviewing the ' fortitcs' log, correlate the TCP-forwarding request with the HTTP 403 response containing the ZTNA Application Not Found error and error code 022 by using the timestamps. Do not assume that an application appearing near an error message in the log belongs to the same connection. If the requested FQDN and destination port are correctly covered by the configured real server but the ZTNA Application Not Found error continues to occur, further troubleshooting of the FortiGate ZTNA Access Proxy and WAD may be required. topics.title: Technical Tip: Error 'relation does not exist' when running a custom SQL dataset on FortiAnalyzer v7.6.3
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to address the following error which may occur when executing a custom SQL dataset on FortiAnalyzer v7.6.3: ERROR: relation "adom***_fgt_wlog" does not exist LINE 5: ...vname","csf","devgrps" ,ti6.epname AS epname FROM adom***_FG... Scope FortiAnalyzer v7.6.3. Solution The issue occurs when the SQL query generated for the custom dataset references a log table that is not available in the database. For example, the following command is used to execute the custom SQL dataset: execute sql-query-dataset ADOM test1 FGVM8VTM20123456 faz "2026-07-01 00:00:00" "2026-07-01 23:59:59" The command fails with: ERROR: relation "adom***_fgt_wlog" does not exist Command fail. Return code 1 To verify the SQL query generated by FortiAnalyzer, enable SQL query debugging: diagnose sql debug sqlqry dbgon diagnose sql debug sqlqry show The generated SQL query contains a reference to the following table: FROM adom***_FGT_wlog ti1 However, the database returns the following error: ERROR: relation "adom***_fgt_wlog" does not exist This confirms that the custom SQL dataset fails when the generated query attempts to access the referenced log table. After collecting the required debug information, disable SQL query debugging: diagnose sql debug sqlqry dbgoff Upgrade FortiAnalyzer to v7.6.7 or later. The issue is resolved after upgrading FortiAnalyzer from version v7.6.3 to v7.6.7. After completing the upgrade, execute the affected custom SQL dataset again and verify that it completes successfully. topics.title: Technical Tip: EAP-TLS Authentication Fails with error 'Authentication failed for EAP method type 13'
topics.summary: Description This article describes the steps to troubleshoot EAP authentication failure on FortiAuthenticator. The user is experiencing issues with EAP authentication, resulting in an error message indicating that authentication failed for EAP method type 13 (EAP-TLS). This message is generic and returned by the client/supplicant whenever the TLS handshake or certificate validation fails during EAP-TLS negotiation. The actual reason must be identified from FortiAuthenticator debug logs, client-side logs, or packet captures. Scope FortiAuthenticator, FortiGate. Solution To troubleshoot EAP authentication failure on FortiAuthenticator, follow these steps: Verify CA and certificate configuration Confirm that the CA certificate is correctly configured and has the appropriate Client Authentication or Server Authentication entries under its Key Usage / Extended Key Usage list. On the FortiGate CLI, run the following command to check the configured WiFi CA and server certificate: get system global | grep wifi This will show the 'wifi-ca-certificate' and 'wifi-certificate' currently in use, allowing to confirm the correct certificates are assigned. Check the certificate chain. Ensure that the Root CA and any Intermediate CA(s) that issued the client and/or server certificates are installed and trusted: On FortiAuthenticator: under Certificate Management -> Certificate Authorities -> Trusted CAs . On the client device: In the OS/device trusted root and intermediate certificate store. A missing intermediate CA is a common cause of TLS validation failure even when the leaf certificate is valid. Verify CRL/OCSP reachability: Verify that the client can reach the CRL/OCSP endpoints. If not required, consider disabling revocation checks for testing. Investigate logs and packet captures: Enable RADIUS debug logs on FortiAuthenticator and take a packet capture on the FortiGate/FortiAuthenticator during a reproduced failure, to identify the exact point of failure in the TLS/EAP exchange. Resolution : The issue was resolved by changing the fragmentation setting to pre-encap on the FortiGate. Large EAP-TLS certificate exchanges are fragmented across multiple RADIUS packets; incorrect fragmentation handling between the FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator can cause the TLS handshake to fail or time out, surfacing as a generic 'Authentication failed for EAP method type 13' error. To adjust this on the FortiGate, under the relevant EAP/802.1X or WiFi SSID configuration, change the fragmentation as shown below on the IPsec phase1 interface: config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit set ip-fragmentation pre-encapsulation next end Like E 1 Reply Follow Share Powered by Gainsight Terms & Conditions Cookie settings Accessibility statement Sign up Already have an account? topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: YouTube Live video streaming issues with FortiClient
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot an issue where standard YouTube videos may work, but YouTube Live streams fail to play or display a restriction message when using FortiClient. The behavior can be related to Web Filter, Safe Search/YouTube restriction settings, Video Filter, or the security profile applied to the affected traffic. Scope FortiClient, FortiClient EMS. Solution When YouTube Live videos cannot be played while other YouTube content works normally, first determine which security feature is enforcing the restriction. Reproduce and identify the symptom. Test a regular YouTube video and confirm whether it plays normally. Test a YouTube Live stream from the same endpoint and browser. Record the timestamp, endpoint hostname, FortiClient version, and the affected URL. If possible, test the same Live stream with the relevant ZTNA/Web Filter policy temporarily excluded to confirm whether the restriction is policy-related. Check the FortiClient EMS Web Filter profile. In FortiClient EMS, review the Web Filter profile assigned to the affected endpoint. Verify whether Safe Search is enabled and review the configured Restriction Level . Go to Endpoint Profiles -> Web Filter . Confirm whether Enable Safe Search is enabled. Check whether the restriction level is configured as Strict or Moderate . As a troubleshooting test, change the restriction level from Strict to Moderate and reproduce the issue. If YouTube Live is still restricted, temporarily disable Safe Search and test again. If the Live stream works after this change, Safe Search/YouTube restriction is the component affecting the playback. Note: Disabling Safe Search changes the content-control behavior for the endpoints using that profile. Perform the test in a controlled policy or test group whenever possible. Check Video Filter settings. If Video Filter is enabled in the FortiClient/EMS profile or on the FortiGate policy processing the traffic, review the configured YouTube restrictions and filtering rules. Verify that the YouTube Live content is not matching a blocked category, channel, keyword, or other Video Filter rule. Temporarily disable the relevant Video Filter profile, or test with a controlled profile without Video Filter, and reproduce the issue. If the stream works after removing the Video Filter restriction, review and adjust the applicable Video Filter rule. Expected result: If the issue is caused by the YouTube restriction level, changing Safe Search from Strict to Moderate , or disabling Safe Search as a controlled test, should allow the YouTube Live stream to be reproduced successfully. The final setting should be selected according to the organization's security policy. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiClientEMS Upgrade Failure due to Grafana Package Error
topics.summary: Description This article describes a solution to an issue where the upgrade of FortiClientEMS fails due to a Grafana package error. The upgrade from version 7.4.7 to 7.4.8 results in a failed upgrade. The error message observed: Setting up grafana (13.1.1) ... mv: cannot move '/usr/share/grafana/data/plugins-bundled' to '/var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled': Directory not empty dpkg: error processing package grafana (--configure): installed grafana package post-installation script subprocess returned error exit status 1 Errors were encountered while processing: grafana dpkg configure failed. Aborting. Scope FortiClientEMS. Solution The EMS v7.4.8 upgrade includes a Grafana package update (to v13.1.1 in this case). During the package installation, the post-installation script attempts to move the bundled plugins directory from the package's default location (/usr/share/grafana/data/plugins-bundled) to the runtime data directory (/var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled). The error Directory not empty means that /var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled already existed and contained files when the mv command tried to move the new bundled plugins there. Note: This is a known issue with Grafana v13.1.1: Upgrade to Grafana 13.1.1 had errors . To resolve the EMS upgrade failure due to a Grafana package error, follow these steps: Run the command to rename the plugins-bundled directory. sudo mv /var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled /var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled.bak Run the command to configure the packages. sudo dpkg --configure -a Retry the upgrade process to complete the installation of FortiClient/EMS version 7.4.8. By following these steps, the upgrade failure due to the Grafana package error should be resolved, and the FortiClientEMS upgrade should complete successfully. forticlientems Like Reply Follow Share Powered by Gainsight Terms & Conditions Cookie settings Accessibility statement Sign up Already have an account? topics.title: FortiClient (Linux) never decrypts the IPsec preshared key from an SAML XML profile — IKE_AUTH fails with "failed to decrypt pre-shared key
topics.summary: " SUMMARYOn FortiClient for Linux, an IPsec IKEv2 + SAML tunnel imported from an exported XML configuration always fails at IKE_AUTH, even though SAML authentication completes successfully and the encrypted PSK field, password, and profile are all correct. Root-cause analysis shows the client never decrypts the field-level encrypted preshared key (EncX... format) before handing it to iked - it passes the raw encrypted blob through as if it were the plaintext key. ENVIRONMENTFortiClient (Linux), tested and reproduced identically on:- 7.4.3.5411- 7.4.4.1796 (includes the fix for Bug ID 1035496, connection problems with SAML, multifactor authentication, and Linux CLI options)- 7.4.8.1904OS: Debian 13 (Trixie), amd64 - same .deb package family as the supported Ubuntu builds.Connection type: IPsec IKEv2, Preshared Key + SAML/SSO (sso_enabled=1, ike_saml_port=9443), imported via Configure VPN > XML > Import XML Configuration from a profile exported on a Windows FortiClient install. topics.title: Technical tip: Troubleshooting FortiClient EMS classification tag synchronization failures
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot a classification tag sync failure. Scope FortiClient EMS. Solution In some cases, it may be necessary to use classification tags for endpoints in FortiClient EMS. After creation, it can be verified that some of the TAGs were not shared with the FortiGate. The main reasons for this could be: The Fabric connector configuration in FortiClient EMS does not have the classification tag sharing option configured: Therefore, review this configuration by navigating to Fabric & Connectors -> Fabric Devices to enable the Classification Tags tag type. The classification tag contains prohibited characters: Due to restrictions on the use of certain characters in FortiGate objects, an object will not be created on the FortiGate if, for example, a tag containing parentheses is created. This means the tag will not be synchronized to the FortiGate. If a classification tag contains disallowed characters, it will be necessary to delete and recreate the tag. Avoid using characters such as ' <>()#"'' , opting instead for '+', '-', or ' _' to ensure the tag is shared successfully. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: How to troubleshoot a FortiAnalyzer-BigData firmware upgrade that fails the NTP pre-upgrade check due to NTP server rate limiting
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot a FortiAnalyzer-BigData firmware upgrade that fails the NTP pre-upgrade check due to NTP server rate limiting. It also explains the difference between NTP synchronization on the FortiAnalyzer-BigData Main Host and the Security Event Manager Controller, and why the controller may generate significantly more NTP requests than the Main Host. Scope FortiAnalyzer-BigData. Solution Starting from FortiAnalyzer-BigData v7.2.7 , the firmware upgrade process includes an NTP preflight validation. Accurate and consistent time synchronization is important for the distributed BigData cluster. If the configured NTP server cannot be successfully validated, the firmware upgrade is blocked. A typical symptom is that NTP synchronization on the Main Host appears healthy: diagnose system ntp status MS Name/IP address Stratum Poll Reach LastRx Last sample =============================================================================== ^* ntp-server.example.com 2 9 377 301 -92us[-123us] +/- 622us However, checking NTP from the Security Event Manager Controller may intermittently fail: fazbdadm check ntp ntpdate: rate limit response from server. ntpdate: no server suitable for synchronization found [ERR] NTP server ntp-server.example.com is not valid or not reachable Running the same command again may succeed: fazbdadm check ntp server , stratum 2, offset -0.000775, delay 0.02631 adjust time server offset -0.000775 sec NTP server ntp-server.example.com is valid~ This behavior can occur when the external NTP infrastructure applies rate limiting to the Security Event Manager Controller. Main Host and Controller NTP behavior: The Main Host and Security Event Manager Controller are separate components of FortiAnalyzer-BigData. The Main Host runs on Blade A1. The Security Event Manager consists of the remaining blades, with one blade acting as the Security Event Manager Controller (BD Controller). The NTP server configured under the following Main Host configuration is used by the BigData environment: config system ntp config ntpserver edit 1 set server "ntp-server.example.com" next end set status enable end The minpoll and maxpoll settings under config system ntp control the Main Host NTP client. They should not be used to determine the polling interval of the Security Event Manager Controller. The controller maintains its own NTP daemon configuration and uses the configured external NTP server address. Depending on the FortiAnalyzer-BigData version, the controller may use ntpd or chronyd . For example, the effective chrony configuration on a controller may contain: server ntp-server.example.com prefer minpoll 3 maxpoll 4 iburst The values are powers of two: minpoll 3 = 2^3 = 8 seconds maxpoll 4 = 2^4 = 16 seconds Therefore, the controller may poll the external NTP server considerably more frequently than the Main Host. The iburst option can additionally send several NTP queries in a short period when establishing synchronization. Why rate limiting can cause a large number of requests: When the NTP server applies rate limiting, the controller may not receive the responses required to successfully synchronize or validate the server. This can result in additional synchronization attempts and retry behavior: Controller sends NTP queries -> NTP server rate-limits the requests -> NTP operation fails -> Additional synchronization/retry attempts -> More NTP requests. Consequently, rate limiting can have the opposite of the intended effect: instead of reducing the overall traffic, failed synchronization attempts can result in additional requests. For example, in one environment, approximately 59,000 NTP requests in 24 hours were observed from the Security Event Manager Controller, while only a few hundred requests were observed from the Main Host. The high request count was associated with NTP server rate limiting and subsequent retry behavior. Checking NTP on the Security Event Manager Controller: The following command actively validates the configured NTP server: fazbdadm check ntp Depending on the NTP implementation, the check uses an active query such as ' ntpdate -q' or the equivalent chrony query. Active validation can generate a short burst of requests and is more sensitive to server-side rate limiting than normal background synchronization. Avoid running this command repeatedly when investigating an NTP rate-limit issue, as each execution generates additional NTP traffic. For local NTP daemon health, the following internal diagnostic command can be used: fazbdadm check ntp-health This command checks the local host NTP health state. If NTP is healthy, the command returns no output. If NTP is unhealthy, an error similar to the following is returned: Chrony server status is not healthy: This command is useful when troubleshooting because it checks the local NTP daemon health without repeatedly performing the same active external NTP validation. Do not manually modify the controller NT

topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FSSO IP change detection very slow
topics.summary: Description This article describes troubleshooting steps for FSSO issues between FortiAuthenticator and FortiGate. The issue occurs when a user moves to a different network without logging in again, for example, by locking and then unlocking the workstation. As a result, the user's new IP address is not detected for a period of time, and FSSO-based policies may not match the user's traffic until it is. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution In some cases, the new IP address is not displayed on the SSO sessions tab on FortiAuthenticator. This behavior can be seen in the following output: The FSSO debug at https://fac-ip/debug/fsso-agent displays: 06/18/2026 15:02:21 [EE2E36C0] Logon Cache [INFO]: Updated logon, workstation:LAP-MNT-CO1-001 ip:changed from 172.20.10.9 to 172.20.20.51 user:FORTINET/testfsso 06/18/2026 15:03:18 [EE2F46C0] DC/TS Agent [INFO]: LOGON 2026-06-18-15:03:18/2026-06-18-15:03:18 DC Agent (null):LAP-MNT-CO1-001/172.20.20.51 FORTINET/testfsso 06/18/2026 15:03:18 [EE2F46C0] Group Cache [INFO]: Loaded groups for user FORTINET/testfsso The DC agent log shows that FortiAuthenticator identified the new IP correctly: 06/18/2026 15:02:21.510: processing Logon (level=1, logonid=0-0) FORTINET estfsso (Test FSSO) from LAP-MNT-CO1-001 Domain:CZFS DNS suffix added:FORTINET.LOCAL. process_logonevent 940, queue size:0 06/18/2026 15:02:21.525: finish processing. ProcessLogonRequest_thread 496, queue size:1, pRec:000000E3CA9ED290 ProcessRequest 621 Enter workstation IP:172.20.20.51 After switching the network adapters in order to change the IP to 172.20.10.9, the previous IP address is kept. 06/18/2026 16:10:44 [EE2D26C0] Logon Cache [INFO]: Updated logon, workstation:LAP-MNT-CO1-001 ip:172.20.20.51 user:FORTINET/testfsso 06/18/2026 16:15:58 [EE5A76C0] Group Cache [INFO]: pending group lookup for user FORTINET/testfsso 06/18/2026 16:15:58 [EE1CB6C0] Group Cache [INFO]: Loaded groups for user FORTINET/testfsso 06/18/2026 16:15:58 [EE1CB6C0] Group Cache [INFO]: try to remove FORTINET/testfsso((null)) 06/18/2026 16:15:58 [EE1CB6C0] Group Cache [INFO]: added (replaced existing one): FORTINET/testfsso DC agent log: 06/18/2026 16:10:44.043: processing Logon (level=1, logonid=0-0) FORTINET estfsso (Test FSSO) from LAP-MNT-CO1-001 Domain:CZFS DNS suffix added:FORTINET.LOCAL. process_logonevent 940, queue size:0 06/18/2026 16:10:44.059: finish processing. ProcessLogonRequest_thread 496, queue size:1, pRec:000000E3CA9EAD60 ProcessRequest 621 Enter workstation IP:172.20.20.51 ProcessRequest 821 Leave DcAgentSendLogonEvent 190 Enter DcAgentSendLogonEvent 196 len:42 DcAgentSendLogonEvent 208 index:0 DcAgentSendLogonEvent 355 Leave Msv1_0SubAuthenticationFilter is called Suggested Solution: Reduce the maximum Time-to-live (TTL) of the FortiAuthenticator's DNS record cache to a lower number, such as 2 or 5 minutes, to ensure that the original IP address of the workstation does not stick around too long. It is also recommended to force the workstation to update its associated DNS records in Active Directory by running the command ipconfig in an elevated command prompt. ipconfig /registerdns N ote : Setting the value to '0' will use the default TTL handed out in the DNS response. '15' is the default TTL (in Active Directory) value for the DNS records created during the workstation DHCP process. While it can be reduced, making a significant change can likely create other performance bottlenecks. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Password change with FortiToken is not working with third-party RADIUS client (Cisco ASA)
topics.summary: Description This article provides details and solution for OTP base password change issue with a third-part RADIUS client (Cisco ASA). Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution OTP-based password change when Cisco ASA is the RADIUS client is supported starting from FortiAuthenticator versions 6.6.10 and 8.0.2. However, clients often receive a 'password failure' error even when FortiAuthenticator is running an updated version. If the 'Password must change' option is disabled in LDAP, authentication is successful. 2026-05-08T04:39:22.697519-07:00 fac8 radiusd[28398]: (19) mschap: ERROR: No NT-Domain was found in the User-Name 2026-05-08T04:39:22.697543-07:00 fac8 radiusd[28398]: (19) mschap: EXPAND nt-domain: %{%{Fortinet-User-Realm}:-%{mschap:NT-Domain}} 2026-05-08T04:39:22.697552-07:00 fac8 radiusd[28398]: (19) mschap: --> nt-domain: 2026-05-08T04:39:22.766733-07:00 fac8 radiusd[28398]: (19) mschap: ntlm_auth said: Password-Change: No Password-Change-Error: When trying to update a password, this return status indicates that the value provided as the current password is not correct. . . 2026-05-08T04:39:22.868005-07:00 fac8 radiusd[28398]: (19) mschap: ERROR: ntlm auth password change failed: ipt says ipt says Change-Error: When trying to update a password, this return status indicates that the value provided as the current password is not correct. 2026-05-08T04:39:22.868063-07:00 fac8 radiusd[28398]: (19) mschap: ERROR: Password change failed 2026-05-08T04:39:22.868104-07:00 fac8 radiusd[28398]: (19) facauth: [mschap] = reject 2026-05-08T04:39:22.868126-07:00 fac8 radiusd[28398]: (19) facauth: } # authenticate = reject 2026-05-08T04:39:22.868161-07:00 fac8 radiusd[28398]: (19) facauth: Module-Failure-Message: mschap: No NT-Domain was found in the User-Name FortiAuthenticator performs the password change process after OTP verification. However, many third-party RADIUS clients use the OTP value (sent to FortiAuthenticator) as the 'password' to encrypt the new password. This causes the password change to fail because the OTP is not the user's actual password. To resolve this issue, disable the 'Request password reset after OTP verification option' under Authentication -> User Account Policies -> General in the FortiAuthenticator GUI. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiClient EMS SAML Authentication Failure when FortiClient shows a 'Server encountered an error, please try again later' message
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot SAML authentication issues in FortiClient EMS when FortiClient shows a ' Server encountered an error, please try again later ' message during user authentication. In this scenario, users are unable to register FortiClient with FortiClient EMS using an invitation code because the SAML authentication process fails. Scope FortiClient EMS. FortiGate. Solution If users encounter a server error when authenticating with SAML, perform the following checks: In FortiClient EMS , navigate to User Management -> SAML Configuration and edit the affected SAML profile. Verify the Service Provider (SP) certificate configured in the SAML profile. Ensure the certificate is a server certificate . Do not use a wildcard certificate, as it may prevent the SAML signing key from loading correctly. If necessary, temporarily remove the configured SP certificate and test the authentication again to determine whether the certificate is the source of the issue. Review the FortiClient EMS diagnostic logs for SAML-related errors. In particular, examine the following FortiClient EMS log file: python_logs/debug_ - - A common indication of this issue is the following error: xmlsec.Error: (1, 'cannot load key') This error typically indicates that FortiClient EMS is unable to load the private key associated with the configured SP certificate. After correcting the certificate configuration, retry the FortiClient registration using the invitation code. For additional information about configuring SAML authentication, refer to SAML Configuration . topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: TACACS Client with subnet in FortiAuthenticator is not working

Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution To configure a TACACS client with a subnet in FortiAuthenticator, follow these steps: Go to Authentication -> TACACS+ Service -> Clients . In this example, there are three clients configured, and the test client IP is 10.47.21.122. Go to Authentication -> TACACS+ Service -> Policies , verify that the subnet is added to the TACACS policy. Try accessing the device with the username and password that were created on FortiAuthenticator, and it shows 'Access denied'. Go to Logging -> Log Access -> Logs ; it shows 'Unknown user authentication from (null) with no token failed: Unable to find authpolicy to process'. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Addressing FortiClient Android v8.0.0 failing to pass any traffic via IPSec VPN tunnel
topics.summary: Description This article describes an issue where FortiClient Android v8.0.0, once connected to an IPsec VPN using UDP transport, is unable to pass any traffic through the tunnel. Scope FortiGate, FortiClient/EMS. Solution FortiClient v8.0.0 installed on Android and connected via an IPsec VPN tunnel (UDP) to FortiGate suffers from a known issue related to NPU offloading enabled on phase1-interface on FortiGate. Below are the steps to verify whether the NPU offloading is enabled and mitigate the issue. Log in to the FortiGate using the CLI. Run the command config vpn ipsec phase1-interface to enter the IPsec phase 1 interface configuration mode. Run the command edit phase1_interface_name to edit the phase 1 interface. Run the command show full-configuration | grep "npu" to check if NPU offload is enabled. If NPU offload is enabled, run the command set npu-offload disable to disable it. Save the changes and test whether traffic flows through the tunnel. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Addressing 'IKE message other than DPD retransmit to maximum.' error when connecting to IKEv2 VPN tunnel
topics.summary: Description This article describes the steps to resolve IKEv2 IPsec VPN connection issues with FortiClient, specifically when encountering the 'IKE message other than DPD retransmit to maximum' error. Scope FortiClient, FortiClientEMS, FortiGate, IPsec, IKEv2. Solution When the network connection is not reliable or ISP or perimeter network/security devices block or cause packet fragmentation of oversized packets, which is often the case with IPsec UDP packets, especially during public key transfer, the 'IKE message other than DPD retransmit to maximum.' error may occur, causing the connection to fail. This article offers a solution for this issue that can be found below: On FortiClientEMS, navigate to Endpoint Profiles -> Remote Access -> Select the profile in question and select Edit . Scroll down to Tunnels and select the tunnel to edit (if the FortiClientEMS version is 8.0.0, the tunnel section is located at the top of the page). In the Phase 1 settings, enable IKE Fragmentation . Save the changes. Refer to the IPsec VPN for more information on configuring IPsec VPN settings and learning about IKE Fragmentation. topics.title: Technical Tip: RADIUS Connectivity fails displaying error 'peer did not return a certificate' after the upgrade of FortiAuthenticator Cloud
topics.summary: Description This article describes a scenario in which, after upgrading FortiAuthenticator Cloud to v8.0.x, RADIUS connectivity can fail. Scope FortiAuthenticator v8.0.x Solution After upgrading FortiAuthenticator Cloud to v8.0.x, the admin may see 'error checking radius connectivity' on the FortiGate. RadSec (RADIUS over TLS) does mutual TLS. After v8.0.x, FortiAuthenticator Cloud started requiring a client certificate from the FortiGate side, not just accepting the server certificate. In the FortiAuthenticator Cloud, RADIUS over TLS logs, logscan can be verified through https:// /debug/radius. The admin can observe the error 'Peer did not return a certificate'. The client is now required and needs to be uploaded and configured in the FortiGate RADIUS configuration. Creating the user/client cert (on FortiAuthenticator) : Go to Certificate Management -> End Entities -> Users and create a new certificate request for the FortiGate acting as RadSec client. Sign it with FortiAuthenticator's own Local CA unless an external PKI is being used. Export the resulting certificate as PKCS#12 bundle including a private key in order to import it in FortiGate. Importing certificates on FortiGate : Import the CA first: System -> Certificates -> Import -> CA Certificate and upload the FortiAuthenticator local CA's public certificate (PEM). Import the client cert: System -> Certificates -> Import -> Certificate , using the PKCS#12 from FortiAuthenticator. Refer to this certificate in the RADIUS server configuration. Note : To generate a Client certificate, follow these instructions: Create a CSR on the FortiGate, navigating to Certificates -> Create/Import -> Generate CSR . Under Local CA, this will appear as: Download the certificate: On FortiAuthenticator, navigate to End Entities -> Users . The CSR downloaded from FortiGate needs to be imported on the FortiAuthenticator for signing. The same Certification Authority used for RADSEC can be used to sign this CSR, or any other Certification Authority on the FortiAuthenticator can be used. Ensure that the Certification Authority used to sign is imported to the FortiGate to trust the chain of certificate. Export the Signed Certificate from FortiAuthenticator. Add the signed Certificate to the FortiGate by navigating to Certificates -> Create/Import -> Create Certificate and importing the certificate downloaded. Status is changed from Pending to Valid: This certificate can be used on the RADIUS configuration section as client certificate. This is an added layer of security that the FortiCloud provides where the connection is checked twice with Certificate Authority before authentication starts.

topics.title: Technical Tip: Intune SCEP Challenge Validation Fails with FortiAuthenticator
topics.summary: Description This article describes an issue faced in FortiAuthenticator where the scepd daemon requests an OAuth token scoped to Microsoft Graph (https://graph.microsoft.com/.default) instead of the Microsoft Intune API (https://api.manage.microsoft.com/.default) during SCEP challenge validation. This causes the Intune SCEP validation endpoint to return an empty response, and certificate enrollment fails. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution To resolve the Intune SCEP challenge validation failure, follow these steps: Ensure that the necessary licenses are enabled, including Microsoft Entra ID P2, Microsoft Intune Endpoint Privilege Management, and Microsoft Intune Plan 1. Verify that the App registered for SCEP/Graph access has the required permissions, including scep_challenge_provider and Application.Read.All. Note : The Application.Read.All. permission requires manual approval from the directory admin. Check the FortiAuthenticator configuration to ensure that it is set up to use the correct SCEP validation URL. Review the debug logs from FortiAuthenticator to identify any issues with the SCEP validation process. For more information on configuring Intune certificate provisioning with FortiAuthenticator, refer to the FortiAuthenticator documentation: Intune Certificate Provisioning with FortiAuthenticator CA . topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Error AADSTS51004 with SAML authentication on FortiAuthenticator
topics.summary: Description This article describes the issue of encountering Error AADSTS51004 when attempting to perform two-factor authentication (2FA) using SAML on FortiAuthenticator with Office 365. The user can authenticate correctly on the FortiAuthenticator but encounters an error when redirecting to Office 365. Scope FortiAuthenticator, FortiGate. Solution To resolve the AADSTS51004 error, follow these steps: Verify that the Active Directory is synchronized correctly with Office 365. Check the attribute being sent by the FortiAuthenticator to ensure it matches the User Principal Name (UPN) declared in the Azure Active Directory. Confirm that the Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL is correctly configured. Refer to the Error AADSTS750054 - SAMLRequest or SAMLResponse must be present as query string parameters in HTTP request for SAML Redirect binding for troubleshooting SAML authentication issues. Additionally, review the FortiAuthenticator configuration to ensure that the attributes like email, username, userPrincipalName, etc., being sent are consistent with the expected value. If the issue persists, review the Azure Active Directory configuration to ensure that the user exists and the UPN is correctly set. incidents.solution: An Administrative Domain (ADOM) upgrade from version 7.4 to 7.6 fails due to a remote certificate missing its PEM wrapper, resulting in a certificate invalid error.SymptomsWhen attempting to upgrade an ADOM from version 7.4 to 7.6 in FortiManager, the process fails with the following error message:Fail (errno=-2):This remote certificate is invalidRoot causeThe upgrade fails because one or more remote certificates in the ADOM database are stored without the required PEM wrapper (the -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- and -----END CERTIFICATE----- lines). While the certificate may be valid for current operations, the ADOM upgrade process to version 7.6 rejects certificates that do not follow this standard format. Resolution Restore the PEM wrapper to the affected certificate using a script.Step 1: Identify the problematic certificateSelect Policy & Objects -> Advanced -> Remote Certificate in the root ADOM.Review the entries for certificates that appear incomplete, expired, or use default names.Use the Where Used feature to check if the suspicious certificate is referenced in SAML or PKI user configurations.Run the ADOM Upgrade Readiness check for the root ADOM and export the report to iden

incidents.symptom: This article describes a known issue with windows active directory 2025 when users try to change their ldap password
incidents.solution: Reported versions starting from v6.6.4. LDAP user password change fails through self-service portal when the active directory is windows server 2025. The error users get is: 'Password change failed. Please contact your system administrator.' In the logs: Failed to change LDAP user 'XXX' password: {Access Denied} A process has requested access to an object but has not been granted those access rights Contournement : s: To control this behavior, use the GPO setting: Under Computer Configuration -> Administrative Templates -> System -> Security Account Manager -> Configure SAM , change the password RPC methods policy. Or: Use secure LDAP (i.e. LDAPS) connection to AD server. This is a known issue with the id 1199749 and it is resolved in firmware version 8.0.4. sources.title: FortiClient VPN-only 7.4.3 – IPsec disconnect breaks Windows L2TP/IPsec (errors 789/791) – Still unresolved
sources.summary: Our municipality and affiliated public institutions have invested in Fortinet equipment and solutions for over a decade. It is extremely disappointing that a mature product branch has been left with a serious, reproducible regression affecting essential public services.Technical details: OS: Windows 11 Pro 25H2 and 26H2 Product: FortiClient VPN-only (IPsec) Affected builds: 7.4.3.4726 and 7.4.3.6002 (probably all versions from ~7.4.1?) Steps: Connect FortiClient IPsec → disconnect → attempt Windows native L2TP/IPsec VPN. Result: Windows VPN fails with RAS errors 789/791. Confirmed workaround: Restarting the Windows IKEEXT service immediately restores connectivity. Network routing and adapter states appear normal after disconnect. This issue has been publicly reported since at least February 17, 2025, with no confirmed permanent fix. Even the latest security-maintenance build, 7.4.3.6002, still reproduces it.Related reports: Feb 17, 2025: https://community.fortinet.com/support-forum-92/

incidents.symptom: Troubleshooting steps for installation failure in FortiManager version 7.6.8 due to the 'udp-not-quic' option under 'config firewall ssl-ssh-profile' when installing to FortiGate models with 2GB of memory
incidents.solution: In version 7.6.8, FortiManager has added some lines to the configuration to push. For example:config firewall ssl-ssh-profile edit "custom-deep-inspection" config https set udp-not-quick allow end config dot set udp-not-quick allow end next endWhen installing on FortiGate models with 2GB of memory, this change causes the installation to fail.These models do not support this option in FortiOS version 7.6.This behavior is due to a known issue, with ID 1352524 Contournement : Set 'udp-not-quic' to 'block' in the affected SSL/SSH profiles.Set udp-not-quic to block in the https and dot sections of the affected SSL/SSH profiles.Go to Policy & Objects -> Advanced.Select the CLI Configurations tab.In the left pane, under firewall, select ssl-ssh-profile.Select the affected profile (for example, custom-deep-inspection), then select Edit.In the Edit firewall ssl-ssh-profile window, scroll to the https section and set udp-not-quic to block.Scroll to the dot section and set udp-not-quic to block.Select OK.Repeat steps 4 to 7 for each SSL/SSH profile that is used by the 2GB FortiGate devices.Install the policy package again.Note: Some models may not accept this setting. For example, a comment on this article reports 'Operation not supported. detail: object not support' on a FortiGate 50G. Contact Fortinet Support if the error persists.Fix: A fix is expected in FortiManager firmware versions 7.6.9 and 8.0.3.Related document:Known issues

incidents.title: 1GbE SFP ports may fail to forward traffic on FortiGate 1800F/1801F after upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.8
incidents.summary: Description This articles describes an issue where the 1GbE SFP ports may fail to forward traffic on FortiGate 1800F/1801F after upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.8 Scope FortiGate 1800F, FortiGate 1801F, FortiOS 7.6.8 Solution Following an internal driver update introduced in FortiOS 7.6.8, the affected platforms - FortiGate 1800F and 1801F is unable to process traffic over its GE SFP slots. As a summary:GE SFP ports 17-24 are unable to process traffic.Traffic through SFP ports 25-40 is unaffected.Traffic through GE RJ45 ports is unaffected.

incidents.summary: DescriptionUpgrading a FortiGate device to version 7.6.8 may cause the web administration interface to become unavailable, resulting in the firewall sending TCP resets to HTTPS requests.ScopeFortiGate 7.6.6 and above.SolutionRoot causeIf the FortiGate belongs to the security fabric, the root is running 7.4.x, and the leaf FortiGate version is 7.6.8: the stability of the web administration service will be affected and application crash autod will be generated.ResolutionUpgrade the FortiGate root to the same version of the leaf FortiGate, or apply the…
incidents.symptom: Upgrading a FortiGate device to version 7.6.8 may cause the web administration interface to become unavailable, resulting in the firewall sending TCP resets to HTTPS requests
incidents.solution: Root causeIf the FortiGate belongs to the security fabric, the root is running 7.4.x, and the leaf FortiGate version is 7.6.8: the stability of the web administration service will be affected and application crash autod will be generated. Resolution Upgrade the FortiGate root to the same version of the leaf FortiGate, or apply the following workaround:config automation setting set fabric-sync disable endTroubleshooting the web interfaceIf the web interface does not respond, verify the current management port settings using the following command:get system global | grep -E "admin-sport|management-port"Run the https and http_auth daemons commands. If no information is shown, review whether the TCP port for the admin port is open, and whether the gnum 10000e and 10000f policies show the https is open to the interface the packet is entering through

incidents.title: LDAP Connection through ZTNA tunnel from FortiAuthenticator Cloud fails due to "Certificate Unknown"
incidents.summary: DescriptionThe connectivity failure observed when accessing the LDAP server behind FortiGate from FortiAuthenticator ('FAC') Cloud via a Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) tunnel.ScopeFortiOS.FortiAuthenticator.SolutionTo configure the ZTNA access to the LDAP server from FortiAuthenticator, refer to this document: Accessing an AD server with a zero trust tunnel on FortiAuthenticator.The following errors are observed on FortiAuthenticator when trying to query for group information.Sample error 1:As observed in the packet capture taken on the FortiGate…
incidents.symptom: The connectivity failure observed when accessing the LDAP server behind FortiGate from FortiAuthenticator ('FAC') Cloud via a Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) tunnel
incidents.solution: To configure the ZTNA access to the LDAP server from FortiAuthenticator, refer to this document: Accessing an AD server with a zero trust tunnel on FortiAuthenticator.The following errors are observed on FortiAuthenticator when trying to query for group information.Sample error 1:As observed in the packet capture taken on the FortiGate (FGT), the TLS handshake fails with a "Certificate Unknown" alert sent from the FortiAuthenticator (FAC) end.Sample error 2:For the ZTNA server certificate, the self-signed certificate generated on the FortiGate (FGT) was used. The corresponding Sub-CA and CA certificates were uploaded to FortiAuthenticator (FAC) to establish the certificate trust chain. However, despite importing these certificates, the same TLS handshake failure with a "Certificate Unknown" alert from the FAC end continues to occur.Resolution:It is recommended to use either a public CA-signed certificate or a FortiAuthenticator (FAC) local CA-signed certificate as the ZTNA server certificate on the FortiGate (FGT), instead of using the self-signed certificate generated by the FGT. This ensures proper certificate chain validation and avoids TLS handshake failures due to certificate

incidents.summary: DescriptionConnections to ZTNA destinations over RDP or HTTP take 10 to 20 seconds when IPv6 is enabled on the network adapter of a Windows endpoint running FortiClient. This article describes the symptoms, the cause, and the workarounds.ScopeFortiClient 7.4.7 and 7.4.9 for Windows with ZTNA enabled, managed by FortiClient EMS, connecting to FQDN-based destinations through a FortiGate ZTNA access proxy.SolutionSymptomsConnection delay: connecting to a ZTNA destination over RDP or HTTP takes 10 to 20 seconds.DNS behavior: nslookup for the ZTNA…
incidents.symptom: Connections to ZTNA destinations over RDP or HTTP take 10 to 20 seconds when IPv6 is enabled on the network adapter of a Windows endpoint running FortiClient. This article describes the symptoms, the cause, and the workarounds
incidents.solution: SymptomsConnection delay: connecting to a ZTNA destination over RDP or HTTP takes 10 to 20 seconds.DNS behavior: nslookup for the ZTNA destination FQDN times out or returns a non-existent domain response.IPv6 dependency: disabling IPv6 on the network adapter of the endpoint reduces the connection time to approximately 1 second.Unaffected destinations: destinations configured with literal IP addresses do not trigger a DNS lookup and are not affected.CauseFortiClient intercepts ZTNA traffic for FQDN-based destinations through a DNS proxy. An IPv6 DNS server bypasses this proxy, so FortiClient blocks IPv6 DNS queries by design while ZTNA is active. ZTNA does not currently support IPv6 DNS resolution.The Windows DNS client sends the query over IPv6 first, waits for a retry timeout of approximately 10 seconds, and then falls back to IPv4. This wait produces the delay.The FortiClient diagnostic logs confirm the condition with entries similar to the following.Block IPV6 DNS query: remoteIp=2001:db8::53 remotePort=53The limitation applies to DNS resolution over IPv6. aiReview.summary: Accès lent aux destinations ZTNA lorsque l'IPv6 est activé sur la carte réseau Windows.
aiReview.symptom: Les connexions aux destinations ZTNA via RDP ou HTTP prennent 10 à 20 secondes lorsque l'IPv6 est activé sur l'adaptateur réseau d'un poste Windows exécutant FortiClient.
aiReview.solution: Le client Windows envoie la requête DNS en IPv6 en premier, attend un délai d'attente d'environ 10 secondes, puis bascule sur l'IPv4. La désactivation d'IPv6 sur l'adaptateur réseau réduit le temps de connexion.
aiReview.note: Limites de preuve : aucune cause définitive en dehors des explications sur le proxy DNS IPv6.

incidents.symptom: DHCP IP address assignment failure only on specific VLANs 97 and 98 on a Bridge mode SSID on the FortiAP-221E model
incidents.solution: VLAN 97 and 98 are reserved for Internet use on the FortiAP-W2 models. Therefore, do not use those VLAN IDs in the FortiAP management VLAN, SSID static VLAN, and dynamically assigned VLAN. Refer to Reserved VLAN IDs.Since the FortiAP-221E is now a legacy model, and this behavior is as per the design and is expected on the E series FortiAP models, there are currently no plans to modify this functionality on this model. To move forward, consider either:Using alternative VLAN IDs instead of 97 and 98, or:Upgrading to a newer FortiAP model, as the current F, G, and K series FortiAPs support these VLAN IDs

incidents.symptom: When the session count on the FortiGate is not high, but softirq is high and contributes to HA port flapping:The HA port flapping causes HA role flap, and results in MAC address flapping on the upstream and downstream switch that connects to it.This issue occurred on an HA cluster that has session synchronization across the members.Note:There could be other factors that could cause high usage of softIRQ on the FortiGate, and initial troubleshooting should be done to determine what could have caused the high softIRQ:Technical Tip: Understanding and analyzing high SoftIRQCommon factors that cause high softirq:Layer 2 loopingBroadcast stormDoS/DDoS attackHigh volumes of denied traffic or asymmetric routingExcessive traffic volume and high session setup rates
incidents.solution: In this article, the HA flap was a result of a chain of incidents that is being illustrated below:Endhost creates multiple connections with a set of target servers at a short interval.FortiGate creates the sessions in its session table and updates the session to HA members via the session-pickup feature.All the members in the cluster experienced high softirq usage despite the session rate being low.The FortiGate did not demonstrate high network bandwidth usage from any network interfaces connected to the end host or servers.When the issue happens, the following logs indicating HA port flaps can be observed at the interval of 5-10 minutes:date=2026-10-05 time=17:19:46 eventtime=1791191986586179779 tz="+0800" logid="0108037902" type="event" subtype="ha" level="information" vd="root" logdesc="Heartbeat device interface up" msg="Heartbeat device(interface) up" ha_role="primary" devintfname="ha2" date=2026-10-05 time=17:19:24 eventtime=1791191965087143839 tz="+0800" logid="0108037901" type="event" subtype="ha" level="critical" vd="root" logdesc="Heartbeat device interface down" msg="Heartbeat device(interface) down" ha_role="primary" devintfname="ha2" date=2026-10-05 time=17:19:24 event

incidents.symptom: When a firewall policy runs flow-based inspection with Deep SSL Inspection and an IPS sensor, an HTTPS application can intermittently fail mid-session
incidents.solution: SymptomsUsers may experience intermittent failures when loading or submitting content on specific websites, resulting in a blank page.The browser may report net::ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR, with the failed request showing:Status = 0No HTTP versionNo server IP addressNo response bytes receivedFortiGate SSL inspection logs indicate that the affected sessions are otherwise processed successfully, including:action="accept" and utmaction="allow"Successful SSL/TLS handshake completion (handshake-done)mitm="yes" indicating successful deep inspectionA valid server certificateIn some cases, traffic flows terminate with action="client-rst" while utmaction="allow" remains unchanged.IPS debugging shows that the corresponding session is finalized (ips_tcp_layer_fini) during an idle period. When the client subsequently attempts to close or reuse the same connection, the IPS engine can no longer locate the associated session. As a result:The IPS engine reports that the session cannot be found.The subsequent request may be decoded incorrectly, often appearing as a smaller or incomplete request.The client may establish a new connection using a different source port.IPS Debug CollectionEnable IPS debugg Contournement : The following workarounds have been successfully implemented in affected environments:Option 1: Downgrade to an Earlier IPS Engine BuildUse an IPS engine version before 7.6.1183. IPS Engine 7.6.1182 has been verified not to exhibit this behavior.If FortiGuard automatic updates are enabled:Temporarily disable scheduled IPS engine updates after reverting to 7.6.1182.Prevent the device from automatically upgrading back to a later affected build.Re-enable automatic updates once a fixed IPS engine version is deployed.Option 2: Exempt the Affected Destination from Deep InspectionAdd the affected FQDN to the SSL/SSH Inspection Profile Exempt List to bypass deep inspection for the destination. Resolution Upgrade to an IPS engine version that contains the fix.The issue has been resolved in:IPS engine 7.6.9 (Build 1202) on the 7.6 branch IPS engine 8.0.3 (Build 0053) on the 8.0 branchAfter upgrading to a fixed IPS engine build, FortiGuard automatic updates can be safely re-enabled

incidents.title: Fields missing in Antivirus Log ID 8195 when using Content-Type: multipart/form-data
incidents.summary: DescriptionCertain fields are missing from Antivirus logs (Message ID 8195) when the HTTP Content-Type is multipart/form-data and proxy-based inspection is used.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptoms.When using proxy-based inspection for HTTP or HTTPS traffic with a multipart/form-dataContent-Type, the Antivirus logs (Message ID 8195 for monitored actions and Message ID 8194 for blocked actions) do not contain the following fields:agent.httpmethod.referralurl.This issue only affects the log information and does not impact the actual Antivirus detection,…
incidents.symptom: Certain fields are missing from Antivirus logs (Message ID 8195) when the HTTP Content-Type is multipart/form-data and proxy-based inspection is used
incidents.solution: Symptoms.When using proxy-based inspection for HTTP or HTTPS traffic with a multipart/form-dataContent-Type, the Antivirus logs (Message ID 8195 for monitored actions and Message ID 8194 for blocked actions) do not contain the following fields:agent.httpmethod.referralurl.This issue only affects the log information and does not impact the actual Antivirus detection, monitoring, blocking, or traffic flow.Root cause.Bug ID 1281140 (Resolved issues) in FortiOS causes these specific fields to be omitted from the log output when the traffic is processed using proxy-based inspection and contains multipart form data.Resolution.Affected versions:FortiOS version 7.6.6.FortiOS version 8.0.0.Resolved versions:FortiOS version 7.6.7.FortiOS version 8.0.1.Resolved issues 8.0.1Resolved issues 7.6.7Upgrade the FortiGate to FortiOS version 7.6.7 or FortiOS version 8.0.1 Contournement : If an upgrade is not immediately possible, change the firewall policy inspection mode from proxy-based to flow-based. This issue does not occur in flow-based inspection mode.CLI configuration:config firewall policy edit set inspection-mode flow next endImportant:Before changing the inspection mode, review the security profiles applied to the firewall policy and verify their compatibility with flow-based inspection

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: SSH Deep Scan setting is disabled automatically after saving the SSL/SSH inspection profile
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes a known issue where SSH Deep Scan cannot be successfully configured in the SSL/SSH inspection profile.ScopeFortiGate low-end models.SolutionOn certain entry-level FortiGate models (such as 40F, 50G, 60F, and 60E) with 2 GB of memory, after upgrading FortiOS from versions 7.4.8 to 7.4.10 or 7.4.11, an unexpected behavior is observed where the SSH Deep Scan option under the SSL/SSH inspection profile is no longer retained or cannot be enabled.
incidents.symptom: This article describes a known issue where SSH Deep Scan cannot be successfully configured in the SSL/SSH inspection profile
incidents.solution: On certain entry-level FortiGate models (such as 40F, 50G, 60F, and 60E) with 2 GB of memory, after upgrading FortiOS from versions 7.4.8 to 7.4.10 or 7.4.11, an unexpected behavior is observed where the SSH Deep Scan option under the SSL/SSH inspection profile is no longer retained or cannot be enabled. When attempting to enable it, the feature appears enabled; however, after returning to the same screen, the feature remains disabled. Additionally, the related CLI commands are no longer available, even though the option is still displayed in the GUI. When attempting to enable the feature through the CLI, the command cannot be found, as shown below.FGR60F-2 # config firewall ssl-ssh-profile FGR60F-2 (ssl-ssh-profile) # edit dip-certificate-inspection new entry 'dip-certificate-inspection' added FGR60F-2 (dip-certificate-inspection) # config ssh command parse error before 'ssh' Command fail. Return code 1 FGR60F-2 (dip-certificate-inspection) # endThis is a known issue affecting certain entry-level FortiGate models running specific FortiOS versions. The issue is scheduled to be resolved in FortiOS v7.4.13, v7.6.7, and v8.0.0

incidents.title: FortiGate EMS fabric connector fails to validate CA certificate
incidents.summary: DescriptionThe FortiClient/EMS fabric connector on FortiGate version 7.4.12 rejects a valid publicly signed FortiClient/EMS web server certificate with a CA not recognized error. This article describes the incident details, debugging, and solution of the issue.ScopeFortiGate, FortiClient EMS.SolutionAfter upgrading FortiOS, the FortiGate EMS fabric connector may fail to validate a valid EMS server certificate and display the error EMS server certificate is not signed by any known CA.
incidents.symptom: The FortiClient/EMS fabric connector on FortiGate version 7.4.12 rejects a valid publicly signed FortiClient/EMS web server certificate with a CA not recognized error. This article describes the incident details, debugging, and solution of the issue
incidents.solution: After upgrading FortiOS, the FortiGate EMS fabric connector may fail to validate a valid EMS server certificate and display the error EMS server certificate is not signed by any known CA. The issue may occur even when the certificate chain is valid, and the required CA certificates are installed on the FortiGate. Also, it might be resolved after revalidating or reinstalling the certificate chain in the FortiGate certificate store. Enable the following debug commands, reproduce the issue by testing the EMS connection, and then disable debugging.diagnose debug reset diagnose debug application fcnacd -1 diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose endpoint filter show-large-data yes diagnose debug enableAfter reproducing the issue, stop debugging:diagnose debug disable diagnose debug resetThe message "Could not verify EMS cert chain" indicates that certificate-chain validation failed. The message "EMS server certificate is not signed by any known CA" points to a CA trust or certificate-validation failure, but does not by itself prove that the CA certificate is missing. Check the configured CA reference and whether the certificate chain is being validated correctly.The message "EMS Contournement : Review the EMS connector configuration under "config endpoint-control fctems". If stale certificate verification settings are suspected, unset the certificate fingerprint and verified common name, then re-verify the EMS connection.config endpoint-control fctems edit 1 unset certificate-fingerprint unset verified-cn end endRelated Article:Troubleshooting Tip: Unable to connect FortiClient EMS due to a server certificate

The message "EMS server certificate is not signed by any known CA" points to a CA trust or certificate-validation failure, but does not by itself prove that the CA certificate is missing. Check the configured CA reference and whether the certificate chain is being validated correctly.The message "EMS Contournement : Review the EMS connector configuration under "config endpoint-control fctems". If stale certificate verification settings are suspected, unset the certificate fingerprint and verified common name, then re-verify the EMS connection.config endpoint-control fctems edit 1 unset certificate-fingerprint unset verified-cn end endRelated Article:Troubleshooting Tip: Unable to connect FortiClient EMS due to a server certificate

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiClient installer showing '{"result": {"retval": -1, "message": "File not found"}}' in email invitation
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes a FortiClient installer showing '{"result": {"retval": -1, "message": "File not found"}}' in the email invitation.ScopeFortiClient EMS version 7.4.8 and FortiClient EMS Cloud.SolutionWhen a user selects the FortiClient installer download link in an EMS invitation email, the browser displays the following error:The installer filename in the invitation URL may contain uppercase characters, while the actual filename on the EMS server uses lowercase characters.
incidents.symptom: This article describes a FortiClient installer showing '{"result": {"retval": -1, "message": "File not found"}}' in the email invitation
incidents.solution: When a user selects the FortiClient installer download link in an EMS invitation email, the browser displays the following error:The installer filename in the invitation URL may contain uppercase characters, while the actual filename on the EMS server uses lowercase characters. Since filenames can be case-sensitive depending on the underlying file system, this mismatch may cause the download to fail Contournement : Change the installer filename in the URL to lowercase.For example, change:https://10.47.4.59:10443/installers/default/7.4.8/FortiClientSetup_7.4.8_x64.exeTo:https://10.47.4.59:10443/installers/default/7.4.8/forticlientsetup_7.4.8_x64.exeNote: This is a workaround for the known issue documented in the FortiClient EMS 7.4.8 release notes. Refer to the applicable release notes for further information.Release notes: New known issues.Planned improvement:An improvement related to installer download is currently planned for FortiClient EMS 7.4.9. Inclusion remains subject to successful QA validation and may change. Consult the release notes when the version becomes available to confirm inclusion

incidents.title: Upgrading FortiGate devices to latest patch release without a firmware license
incidents.summary: DescriptionInstructions for initiating a patch-level upgrade when the device has no support contract.ScopeFortiOS 7.4 and 7.6FortiGate devices with no firmware contract.SolutionIn FortiOS 7.4.2 and higher, it is not possible to upgrade to later firmware versions in the GUI if the device has an expired firmware license.The FortiOS GUI will display the warnings such as "This is a FortiOS v7.4.5-build2702 firmware image that cannot be installed because the device's FortiGuard license for firmware upgrades could not be verified or may have expired.
incidents.symptom: Instructions for initiating a patch-level upgrade when the device has no support contract
incidents.solution: In FortiOS 7.4.2 and higher, it is not possible to upgrade to later firmware versions in the GUI if the device has an expired firmware license.The FortiOS GUI will display the warnings such as "This is a FortiOS v7.4.5-build2702 firmware image that cannot be installed because the device's FortiGuard license for firmware upgrades could not be verified or may have expired. Verify or renew the license to install upgrades." Even if a device has no valid support contract, it is strongly recommended to maintain a patched firmware version. See available upgrade methods below. Upgrade using forced FortiGuard update:This method applies to the following FortiOS firmware versions:FortiOS 7.4.8 and higherFortiOS 7.6.4 and higherThese firmware versions support forced firmware upgrade within the same minor firmware version even if the device does not have an existing firmware license.Verify the FortiGate has DNS and internet access, and use execute auto-upgrade check-for-new-image: FortiGate-40F # execute auto-upgrade check-for-new-image Manually triggering auto-upgrade new image check... Auto-upgrade new image check triggered. FortiGate-40F # Firmware Update from Management Service Upgrade to i

incidents.title: Administrator SSO authentication fails after upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8
incidents.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8, administrator SSO authentication fails. FortiOS access requires a local administrator or a RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS+ administrator account.ScopeFortiOS 7.6.8.SolutionAfter upgrade, administrator SSO will fail with the error message "Single Sign-On Failed", without presenting any option to enter an SSO administrator credential.The following FortiOS login methods are confirmed affected by the issue:Administrator FortiCloud SSO.Administrator third-party SSO, for example see Technical Tip: Configuring SAML SSO login…
incidents.symptom: After upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8, administrator SSO authentication fails. FortiOS access requires a local administrator or a RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS+ administrator account
incidents.solution: After upgrade, administrator SSO will fail with the error message "Single Sign-On Failed", without presenting any option to enter an SSO administrator credential.The following FortiOS login methods are confirmed affected by the issue:Administrator FortiCloud SSO.Administrator third-party SSO, for example see Technical Tip: Configuring SAML SSO login for FortiGate administrators with Entra ID acting as SAML IdP.Security Fabric SSO with root FortiGate as IdP, for example see Configuring single-sign-on in the Security Fabric.Confirmed not affected:VPN user SSO authentication.Other FortiOS versions including FortiOS 7.2.14, 7.4.13, 7.6.7 and 8.0.2.Local administrator authentication.Remote administrator authentication using RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS+.While access to the FortiGate from FortiManagement Cloud (FortiGate Cloud) is technically not affected, SSO authentication to the FortiGate is still not possible over this management path.Issue matching:To confirm the issue, check the FortiOS crashlog for a matching "FORTISM Violation" from the time of the access attempt. This can be done by accessing the FortiGate using a local administrator account and executing diagnose debug crashlog read | gr Contournement : At this time, the only available workaround is to use another administrator authentication method.If no suitable administrator account exists, console access to a physical device can be used to recover access, see Technical Tip: Boot the backup firmware and config via console.If the device is centrally managed by FortiManager or a valid FortiManagement Cloud subscription, an administrator can be added. See Recover access to FortiGate via FortiManagement Cloud.Related article:Technical Tip: Create a 'break glass' admin account on the FortiGate as a backup for remote authentication/MFA (Recommendation)

incidents.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.8, administrators may be unable to configure an IP address for new VPN tunnels via the GUIScopeFortiOS 7.6.8.SolutionIf you try to configure only the IP address, the following behavior is observed: The FortiGate will not display any error message, but the Tunnel interface will remain with the default IP address 0.0.0.0/0.0.0.0.If you try to configure the tunnel IP address and the Remote IP address at the same time, the IP field will revert back to 0.0.0.0 and the GUI will display an error message:Error…
incidents.symptom: After upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.8, administrators may be unable to configure an IP address for new VPN tunnels via the GUI
incidents.solution: If you try to configure only the IP address, the following behavior is observed: The FortiGate will not display any error message, but the Tunnel interface will remain with the default IP address 0.0.0.0/0.0.0.0.If you try to configure the tunnel IP address and the Remote IP address at the same time, the IP field will revert back to 0.0.0.0 and the GUI will display an error message:Error message:IP must be set if remote IP is defined.Must set ip if remote-ip is defined.Object set operator error, -118 discard the setting. Solution The issue is under investigation, and a permanent fix is not available yet Contournement : Configure the IP address and remote address via the CLI with the following commands:config system interface edit set ip 255.255.255.255 set remote-ip end

This behavior results in Intrusion Prevention System scanning failures, which may cause certain traffic sessions or websites to be…
incidents.symptom: The ipsengine daemon crashes frequently on FortiGate devices running FortiOS 7.4.x / 7.6.x when FortiSandBox scanning is enabled in AntiVirus profiles
incidents.solution: SymptomAfter upgrading to FortiOS 7.4.x or 7.6.x, the ipsengine daemon has been observed to crash repeatedly.The crash logs indicate a segmentation fault (Signal 11). This behavior results in Intrusion Prevention System scanning failures, which may cause certain traffic sessions or websites to be blocked.The following command below allows you to check the latest ipsengine crashes that occurred:Note:When an AntiVirus profile is configured to use FortiSandBox scanning (either Cloud or On-Premises), this will trigger a crash in the ipsengine.diagnose debug crashlog read | grep ipsengine -A 1 15512: 2026-09-08 07:26:43 application ipsengine 07.004.604 15513: 2026-09-08 07:26:43 *** signal 11 (Segmentation fault) received *** ... 15587: 2026-09-08 07:30:26 application ipsengine 07.004.604 15588: 2026-09-08 07:30:26 *** signal 11 (Segmentation fault) received *** Contournement : Disable the FortiSandBox scanning feature within all AntiVirus profiles used in Firewall policies. This allows other security profiles, such as SSL Inspection, Web Filtering, and IPS, to continue functioning without crashing the engine.Log in to the FortiGate GUI.Select Security Fabric -> AntiVirus.Edit the AntiVirus profiles used in the firewall policies.Under the APT Protection Option, set Send files to FortiSandbox for inspection to disabled.Select OK to save the changes.Alternatively, use the Command Line Interface (CLI) to disable the feature:config antivirus profile edit " " config http set fortisandbox disable end config ftp set fortisandbox disable end config imap set fortisandbox disable end config pop3 set fortisandbox disable end config smtp set fortisandbox disable end next endThe permanent fix for this Known Issue is already included in FortiOS 7.4.13, 7.6.7, and 8.0.0.Resolved issues | FortiGate / FortiOS 7.4.13 | Fortinet Document Library - 1182611Resolved issues | FortiGate / FortiOS 7.6.7 | Fortinet Document Library - 1182611Resolved issues | FortiGate / FortiOS 8.0.0 | Fortinet Document Library - 1182611Related article: FortiGate / FortiOS - Administration Guide -

sources.solution: SymptomAfter upgrading to FortiOS 7.4.x or 7.6.x, the ipsengine daemon has been observed to crash repeatedly.The crash logs indicate a segmentation fault (Signal 11). incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiClient VPN before logon fails to connect when using windows credentials
incidents.summary: DescriptionFortiClient version 7.4 fails to establish a VPN connection before user logon using Windows credentials.ScopeFortiClient version 7.4.SolutionSymptoms.Users cannot connect to the SSL VPN or IPsec VPN using the VPN Before Logon feature after upgrading to FortiClient version 7.4. The connection fails at the Windows logon screen, and no logs are generated on the FortiGate.Root cause.In FortiClient version7.4, a change in behavior causes the client to check for credentials before initiating the connection.
incidents.symptom: FortiClient version 7.4 fails to establish a VPN connection before user logon using Windows credentials
incidents.solution: Symptoms.Users cannot connect to the SSL VPN or IPsec VPN using the VPN Before Logon feature after upgrading to FortiClient version 7.4. The connection fails at the Windows logon screen, and no logs are generated on the FortiGate.Root cause.In FortiClient version7.4, a change in behavior causes the client to check for credentials before initiating the connection. If the Prompt for Username setting is disabled, FortiClient may fail to retrieve the necessary credentials from Windows, causing the pre-logon connection to halt. This differs from FortiClient version 7.2, which attempted to start the connection even if credentials were not immediately found.Resolution Contournement : To resolve this issue in FortiClient version 7.4, enable the prompt for usernames in the endpoint profile:Log in to the FortiClient EMS console.Select Endpoint Profiles -> System Settings.Select the profile applied to the affected endpoints and select Edit.Navigate to the VPN tunnel settings.Enable the prompt for username option.Save the changes and deploy the profile to the endpoints.Settings in SSL VPN tunnel configuration:Settings in IPsec VPN tunnel configuration:Permanent solution.This behavior is not present in FortiClient version 8.0.0 and above. Upgrade the FortiClient installation to FortiClient version 8.0.0 or above to restore the VPN Before Logon behavior without requiring the username prompt

incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot a FortiAuthenticator ZTNA certificate error on FortiGate. Scope FortiAuthenticator, FortiGate. Solution FortiAuthenticator v6.4.4 introduced a Zero Trust Tunnel Feature, which is used to securely connect with an on-prem Active Directory Server(LDAP). Zero trust tunnels FortiAuthenticator v6.4.4 This article assumes that the initial setup for this feature has been completed: Setting up a zero trust tunnel If the ZTNA tunnel is failing on the FortiGate, check the ZTNA traffic logs on FortiGate: Log…
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to troubleshoot a FortiAuthenticator ZTNA certificate error on FortiGate
incidents.solution: FortiAuthenticator v6.4.4 introduced a Zero Trust Tunnel Feature, which is used to securely connect with an on-prem Active Directory Server(LDAP). Zero trust tunnels FortiAuthenticator v6.4.4 This article assumes that the initial setup for this feature has been completed: Setting up a zero trust tunnel If the ZTNA tunnel is failing on the FortiGate, check the ZTNA traffic logs on FortiGate: Log & Report -> ZTNA Traffic. In the screenshot above, the error 'Traffic denied because cert auth failed' shows up. To resolve this issue, ensure the ZTNA CA certificate has already been uploaded onto the FortiGate: If the CA certificate does not exist, import it and make sure to take note of the name after importing the CA certificate. In the screenshot above, the name is 'CA_Cert_2'. The FortiGate will need to use the CA certificate in order to trust the FortiAuthenticator certificate for the ZTNA tunnel. After confirming the CA certificate, configure the following option through the FortiGate CLI: config authentication setting set user-cert-ca end Note: The authentication rule and scheme settings should also be configured as described in the documentation below: Configuring certificate authe
