incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tips: Admin is logged out of the GUI immediately after login (login must be entered twice) on FortiGate version 7.6.7
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes an issue on FortiOS version 7.6.7: some administrators are kicked back to the login page right after a successful GUI login; it is necessary to enter credentials a second time before the dashboard loads. In other cases, the first attempt shows a blank/white page, and a later attempt loads normally. The login may be recorded in the event log together with an HTTPS connection error, even though authentication itself succeeds.ScopeFortiOS version 7.6.7.SolutionSymptoms:After entering the username and password, the login…
incidents.symptom: This article describes an issue on FortiOS version 7.6.7: some administrators are kicked back to the login page right after a successful GUI login; it is necessary to enter credentials a second time before the dashboard loads. In other cases, the first attempt shows a blank/white page, and a later attempt loads normally. The login may be recorded in the event log together with an HTTPS connection error, even though authentication itself succeeds
incidents.solution: Symptoms:After entering the username and password, the login page reappears instead of the dashboard. Entering the credentials a second time succeeds and the GUI loads.The issue affects GUI (HTTPS) logins only, SSH sessions are not affected. It may be seen across Chrome, Edge, and Firefox, and sometimes in /private mode as well.An 'HTTPS connection error' may be logged in the event log.Root cause:When signing in through a web browser, the page loads a large number of small resources all at once (far more than in earlier releases). The web interface's activity monitor mistakes this normal burst of activity for a brief attack and interrupts the login, dropping back to the login page, even though the username and password were already accepted.This is why the login can appear in the event log as successful while the page still sends back: authentication succeeds, but the session is cut before the dashboard finishes loading.Related known issues in the 7.6.7 release notes:Bug ID 1300025 – Admin session termination (especially Chrome/Edge) Contournement : clear browser cache/cookies.Bug ID 1306049 – Blank page after upgrade to 7.6.7. Workaround involves disabling HTTP rate-limiter settings.Resolution:Fixed in FortiOS version 7.6.8 (and above version 8.0.1). The fix scopes the unauthenticated request-body monitor to body-carrying methods only, raises the unauthenticated request timeout from 1 s to 10 s, and reworks the rate-limiter token pricing and refund logic so a normal GUI bootstrap is not mistaken for an attack and killed.Upgrade to FortiOS version 7.6.8 or above to resolve the issue.Workaround (until upgrade):Until the upgrade can be performed, one of the following avoids the problem:Clear the browser cache and cookies associated with the FortiGate, then log in again.Access the GUI in the browser's Incognito/InPrivate mode.Simply log in a second time; the second attempt loads the dashboard normally.Diagnostic Commands:Useful while reproducing the issue:diagnose debug resetdiagnose debug console timestamp enablediagnose debug application httpsd -1diagnose debug application node -1diagnose debug application http_authd -1 # or http_authdiagnose debug enableStop with:diagnose debug disable diagnose debug reset

incidents.title: Traffic logs generated on FortiGate proxy policies despite logging being disabled
incidents.summary: DescriptionFortiGate generates excessive traffic logs for proxy policies even when the logtraffic setting is disabled, leading to increased log volume on FortiAnalyzer.ScopeFortiGate, FortiAnalyzer.SolutionAfter upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.6 or 7.6.7, the volume of daily logs sent to FortiAnalyzer increases significantly. Traffic logs with Log ID 13 continue to be generated for policies where logging is explicitly disabled using the set logtraffic disable command.A bug in the logging logic of FortiOS 7.6.x causes traffic logs to be generated for proxy…
incidents.symptom: FortiGate generates excessive traffic logs for proxy policies even when the logtraffic setting is disabled, leading to increased log volume on FortiAnalyzer
incidents.solution: After upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.6 or 7.6.7, the volume of daily logs sent to FortiAnalyzer increases significantly. Traffic logs with Log ID 13 continue to be generated for policies where logging is explicitly disabled using the set logtraffic disable command.A bug in the logging logic of FortiOS 7.6.x causes traffic logs to be generated for proxy policies regardless of the logtraffic configuration. This issue affects both explicit proxy policies and standard firewall policies configured with inspection-mode proxy.Resolution:Upgrade the FortiGate device to FortiOS 7.6.8 or a later version. This release contains the fix for the logging logic that prevents the unauthorized generation of traffic logs when logging is disabled.Verification steps:To confirm if the issue is present, check the logs on FortiAnalyzer for the following characteristics:Filter logs by logid 13.Verify if the logs are associated with a policy where set logtraffic disable is configured.Check if the affected policies use inspection-mode proxy or are defined as proxy-policy.Example of a policy configuration affected by this behavior:config firewall policy edit xxxx set inspection-mode proxy set logtraffic disable nex

incidents.title: HA cluster firmware upgrade stuck after the Secondary unit is upgraded successfully
incidents.summary: DescriptionA firmware upgrade behavior issue observed in a High Availability (HA) cluster. In an HA cluster, when the FGCP Multi-Version Cluster (MVC) upgrade mode is enabled using set uninterruptible-upgrade enable, the upgrade behavior will upgrade the Secondary unit first followed by the Primary unit.However, there are cases where the firmware upgrade may not proceed to the Primary unit even after the Secondary unit has been successfully upgraded.For example:The Secondary unit has been successfully upgraded to firmware version 7.6.7.However, the…
incidents.symptom: A firmware upgrade behavior issue observed in a High Availability (HA) cluster. In an HA cluster, when the FGCP Multi-Version Cluster (MVC) upgrade mode is enabled using set uninterruptible-upgrade enable, the upgrade behavior will upgrade the Secondary unit first followed by the Primary unit.However, there are cases where the firmware upgrade may not proceed to the Primary unit even after the Secondary unit has been successfully upgraded.For example:The Secondary unit has been successfully upgraded to firmware version 7.6.7.However, the Primary unit remains on firmware version 7.4.11
incidents.solution: Recommended action:Do not reboot the Primary unit or initiate a failover.Re-run the firmware upgrade from the Primary unit to trigger the upgrade process again.This approach will usually resolve the issue and allow the firmware upgrade to proceed as expected

incidents.title: FortiClient Web Filter browser extension fails to uninstall during an on-fabric to off-fabric transition
incidents.summary: Description When the Web Filter extension is not uninstalled when the endpoint moves from on-fabric to off-fabric while 'Keep Extension When Endpoint is Off-Fabric' is disabled and 'Web Browser Plugin for HTTPS Web Filtering' is enabled. Scope FortiClient Endpoint version 8.0.0, FortiClient Windows. Solution Issue scenario: FortiClient v8.0.0.0103 GA. Enable the Web Filter profile. Disable 'Keep Extension When Endpoint is Off-Fabric'.
incidents.symptom: When the Web Filter extension is not uninstalled when the endpoint moves from on-fabric to off-fabric while 'Keep Extension When Endpoint is Off-Fabric' is disabled and 'Web Browser Plugin for HTTPS Web Filtering' is enabled
incidents.solution: Issue scenario: FortiClient v8.0.0.0103 GA. Enable the Web Filter profile. Disable 'Keep Extension When Endpoint is Off-Fabric'. Enable 'Web Browser Plugin for HTTPS Web Filtering'. Verify the extension is installed while on-fabric. Move the endpoint to off-fabric and observe that the extension is not uninstalled. Issue resolved In: FortiClient version 8.0.1. Solution description: Fixed a bug where the policy watchdog unconditionally re-added the browser extension force-install policy. The fix ensures that when 'Keep Extension When Endpoint is Off-Fabric' is disabled, the policy is removed during the transition to an inactive filtering state (including on-fabric to off-fabric). Both the periodic policy-check and extended-keepalive-absence paths now respect the policy gate to prevent the extension from being resurrected. Additionally, SafeSearch hosts-file enforcement was updated to align with actual extension presence. incidents.title: FortiGate Single Sign-On users logged off when Enforce Kerberos is enabled
incidents.summary: DescriptionUsers are automatically logged off from FortiGate Single Sign-On after enabling the Enforce Kerberos setting in the Collector Agent.ScopeFortiGate, FSSO Collector AgentSolutionA known issue exists where the workstation check fails when "Enforce Kerberos" is enabled. Users are de-authenticated when the workstation check fails after the dead entry timeout.Upgrade the FortiGate Single Sign-On Collector Agent to version 5.0.0335 or later.
incidents.symptom: Users are automatically logged off from FortiGate Single Sign-On after enabling the Enforce Kerberos setting in the Collector Agent
incidents.solution: A known issue exists where the workstation check fails when "Enforce Kerberos" is enabled. Users are de-authenticated when the workstation check fails after the dead entry timeout.Upgrade the FortiGate Single Sign-On Collector Agent to version 5.0.0335 or later. This version addresses WMI workstation check failures when "Enforce Kerberos" is enabled by adding reverse DNS lookup to resolve workstation IP addresses to hostnames.Download the FortiGate Single Sign-On Collector Agent version 5.0.0335 from the Fortinet Support Portal.Install the updated Collector Agent on the server.Enable the "Enforce Kerberos" setting in the Collector Agent configuration.Monitor the user sessions to verify that they are no longer automatically logged off after one hour.Related article:Technical Tip: FortiGate FSSO Collector Agent v5.0.0323 and earlier do not support Windows Server 2025 with default polling mode

incidents.title: FortiClient Endpoints fail to match assigned Entra ID group policies and fall into the default policy due to a synchronization issue between the user identity and the device object.
incidents.summary: Description FortiClient Endpoints that are members of a specific Entra ID group do not match the corresponding group policy in FortiClient EMS. These endpoints are assigned to the default policy. Scope FortiClient EMS and FortiClient Endpoint. Solution FortiClient EMS cannot correctly retrieve the Azure device object ID for certain users. This occurs when a mismatch or failure happens in the lookup process between the reported user identity and the Entra ID device object, resulting in a 404 Not Found error during the API call to Microsoft Graph.
incidents.symptom: FortiClient Endpoints that are members of a specific Entra ID group do not match the corresponding group policy in FortiClient EMS. These endpoints are assigned to the default policy
incidents.solution: FortiClient EMS cannot correctly retrieve the Azure device object ID for certain users. This occurs when a mismatch or failure happens in the lookup process between the reported user identity and the Entra ID device object, resulting in a 404 Not Found error during the API call to Microsoft Graph. Error example: ERROR update/sysinfo.go:344 [TID:KiK5dhcVVQ][site:default][uid:A11E1B23714F48A4910032061E4E7122]: Could not get azure device object id: search for device object id: http.GET(https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/devices(deviceId='0e427e3a-5d65-40bb-bfa5-b1b72f940d1b')?%24select=id) return status: 404 Not Found Permanent solution : Update FortiClient EMS to version 7.4.8 or above. This version includes the fix for the identity matching bug. If updating to version 7.4.8 is not immediately possible, use the following workaround: Create a new group in Entra ID. Add the computer accounts directly to this new group instead of adding user accounts. Assign the desired FortiClient EMS policy to this new computer-based group. incidents.title: rxqid default value was changed after upgrade
incidents.summary: DescriptionAfter an upgrade from versions 7.0.14, 7.2.8, and 7.4.4 to versions 7.0.15, 7.2.9, and 7.4.5, the rxqid value was changed and may cause RX drops on the interface.ScopeFortiOS.SolutionSymptomsUnder system 'affinity-packet-redistribution ' is the rxqid setting. It is the ID of the receive queue on an interface used to perform packet redistribution across multiple CPU cores. The value is from to .In 7.0.14, 7.2.8, and 7.4.4, the default value is 0.
incidents.symptom: After an upgrade from versions 7.0.14, 7.2.8, and 7.4.4 to versions 7.0.15, 7.2.9, and 7.4.5, the rxqid value was changed and may cause RX drops on the interface
incidents.solution: SymptomsUnder system 'affinity-packet-redistribution ' is the rxqid setting. It is the ID of the receive queue on an interface used to perform packet redistribution across multiple CPU cores. The value is from to .In 7.0.14, 7.2.8, and 7.4.4, the default value is 0. After upgrading FortiOS to 7.0.15, 7.2.9, 7.4.5, and above, the default value is changed to 255. In some cases, it can cause an increase in interface RX drops.7.0.14 7.2.8 7.4.4:FGT # get system status | grep Version: Version: FortiGate-VM64-KVM v7.4.4,build2662,240514 (GA.F) FGT # show system affinity-packet-redistribution config system affinity-packet-redistribution edit 1 set interface "port2" set affinity-cpumask "0xff" next end FGT # show full system affinity-packet-redistribution config system affinity-packet-redistribution edit 1 set interface "port2" set rxqid 0 set round-robin disable set affinity-cpumask "0xff" next end7.0.15 7.2.9 7.4.5 and above:FGT # get system status | grep Version: Version: FortiGate-VM64-KVM v7.4.5,build2702,240916 (GA.M) FGT # show system affinity-packet-redistribution config system affinity-packet-redistribution edit 1 set interface "port2" set affinity-cpumask "0xff" next end FGT # sh

incidents.title: FortiGate GUI unreachable due to ACME interface configuration

incidents.symptom: An issue where the administrative web interface (httpsd) becomes unreachable when the ACME client is configured to listen on an interface that is down, such as an IPsec tunnel
incidents.solution: SymptomsThe FortiGate GUI is not reachable, and users receive a 500 error when attempting to load the administration page. The httpsd process may not be running or fails to start. This issue can affect both the primary and secondary units in a High Availability cluster.Root CauseThe FortiGate management web server (httpsd) hosts the ACME client used for Let's Encrypt certificate challenges. If the ACME client is configured to listen on an interface that is currently down (for example, an IPsec tunnel), the web server cannot bind its listener to that interface. This causes the httpsd process to shut down, which blocks all administrative web access, including access via the management port. Resolution Contournement : Remove the interface binding from the ACME configuration to allow the web server to start.Connect to the FortiGate via the Command Line Interface (CLI).Run the following commands to unset the ACME interface:config system acme unset interface endThe GUI should become accessible immediately after removing the interface setting.Permanent

incidents.title: CSRF validation error, SAML IdP Proxy with federated domains
incidents.summary: Description An issue where users encounter a CSRF validation error when authenticating via SAML IdP Proxy with federated domains, such as Microsoft 365. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution When a user attempts to authenticate using a federated domain (for example, Microsoft 365) via the FortiAuthenticator SAML IdP Proxy, the process fails. The user is redirected from the identity provider back to the FortiAuthenticator endpoint /saml-idp-proxy/ and receives the following error message: Request failed CSRF validation: CSRF cookie not set.
incidents.symptom: An issue where users encounter a CSRF validation error when authenticating via SAML IdP Proxy with federated domains, such as Microsoft 365
incidents.solution: When a user attempts to authenticate using a federated domain (for example, Microsoft 365) via the FortiAuthenticator SAML IdP Proxy, the process fails. The user is redirected from the identity provider back to the FortiAuthenticator endpoint /saml-idp-proxy/ and receives the following error message: Request failed CSRF validation: CSRF cookie not set. Refresh your browser and try again. This is a known issue in FortiAuthenticator version 6.6.10 and 8.0.3 which causes the system to fail to set the required CSRF token cookie during the SAML redirection process. When the browser performs the subsequent POST request to the login endpoint, the validation fails because the expected CSRF cookie is missing from the request headers. Resolution is to upgrade FortiAuthenticator to version 6.6.11, 8.0.4 or higher. This issue is resolved in firmware version 6.6.11 and 8.0.4. Internal engineering ticket ID is 1325777. incidents.title: FortiSASE secure edge tunnel stays down after a FortiOS upgrade because of a Diffie-Hellman group mismatch
incidents.summary: DescriptionFortiGate secure edge tunnel to FortiSASE stops negotiating after the FortiGate is upgraded to FortiOS 7.6.5, why the tunnel comes up when the Diffie-Hellman (DH) groups are set to 5 and 14 and then drops again with the groups back at 20 and 21, and how to fix the condition permanently.This article also explains why the tunnel settings on FortiManager are not the source of truth for this tunnel, and how to make the workaround persist on FortiOS builds that do not contain the code fix.ScopeFortiGate configured as a FortiSASE secure edge,…
incidents.symptom: FortiGate secure edge tunnel to FortiSASE stops negotiating after the FortiGate is upgraded to FortiOS 7.6.5, why the tunnel comes up when the Diffie-Hellman (DH) groups are set to 5 and 14 and then drops again with the groups back at 20 and 21, and how to fix the condition permanently.This article also explains why the tunnel settings on FortiManager are not the source of truth for this tunnel, and how to make the workaround persist on FortiOS builds that do not contain the code fix
incidents.solution: SymptomA FortiGate operating as a FortiSASE secure edge has a VDOM, commonly named SASE, configured for LAN extension. The tunnel to the FortiSASE edge service is not created by an administrator. FortiOS creates and maintains it automatically, under a phase 1 interface named with the prefix ul-, for example ul-npu0_vlink1, and the interface carries the description "[fgconn] Do NOT edit. Automatically generated by extension controller".After the FortiGate is upgraded to FortiOS 7.6.5 or 7.6.6, the tunnel no longer establishes. The VPN logs show a large number of IKEv2 phase 1 proposals sent to the FortiSASE peer with no answer, each cycle ending in a negotiation timeout. The responder cookie in those log entries is all zeroes, which means the peer never replied. See the following logs for examples of Fortinet Tunnel ID, local IP, and interface names.date=2026-10-12 time=23:10:55 type=VPN subtype=tunnel action=tunnel-down vd=SASE vpntunnel="ul-npu0_vlink1" duration=28678 locip=172.16.10.90 remip=192.0.2.10 remport=4500 locport=4500 version="IKEv2" role="initiator" date=2026-10-12 time=23:17:46 type=VPN subtype=phase1 logid=0101037127 action=SA_INIT vpntunnel="ul-npu0_vlink1" status="

incidents.symptom: Steps to resolve the "Failed to save changes" error encountered when saving a custom Application Control signature
incidents.solution: A syntax error can occur when saving a custom Application Control signature if the signature definition contains line breaks or formatting that prevents the parser from correctly interpreting the opening and closing parentheses.When attempting to save a custom Application Control signature, the GUI displays the error "Failed to save changes".To investigate the issue, run the following commands.diagnose debug disable diagnose debug reset diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose debug cli 8 diagnose debug cmdb-trace diagnose debug enableThe CLI and CMDB trace debug output indicates that the closing or opening parenthesis cannot be identified. incidents.title: FortiManager firmware upgrade preview shows "No record found" even with an assigned device
incidents.summary: DescriptionAn explanation for a "No record found" message occurring in the Firmware Upgrade Preview of a Firmware Template in FortiManager even when a device is assigned to the template. Steps to resolve it are provided.ScopeFortiManager.FortiGate.SolutionThe Firmware Upgrade Preview only lists devices that match the platform selected in the template. If the template platform is different from the platform of the assigned device, the preview has nothing to calculate and shows "No record found".
incidents.symptom: An explanation for a "No record found" message occurring in the Firmware Upgrade Preview of a Firmware Template in FortiManager even when a device is assigned to the template. Steps to resolve it are provided
incidents.solution: The Firmware Upgrade Preview only lists devices that match the platform selected in the template. If the template platform is different from the platform of the assigned device, the preview has nothing to calculate and shows "No record found". No other error is shown, and the device still appears under "Assigned to Device/Group".This is easy to miss with virtual FortiGates, because several platform names look similar (for example FortiGate-VM64 and FortiGate-VM64-KVM).The device platform shows in the FortiGate CLI:FGT-SPOKE # get sys status Version: FortiGate-VM64-KVM v7.4.9,build2829,250924 (GA.M) First GA patch build date: 230509 Current Security Level: High Firmware Signature: certified Virus-DB: 1.00000(2018-04-09 18:07) Extended DB: 1.00000(2018-04-09 18:07) ....................... ............... .........The template platform is FortiGate-VM64, which does not match FortiGate-VM64-KVM.To avoid this, set the template Platform to "GA Versions" instead of a specific platform. The template is then not tied to one platform, and the Firmware Upgrade Preview selects the correct FortiGate platform for each assigned device.Go to Device Manager -> Firmware Templates and edit the templa

incidents.title: High packet drops occur during traffic bursts on a FortiGate VM hosted in Google Cloud Platform
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes the case when a FortiGate VM hosted on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) experiences significant packet loss and latency during high bursts of traffic. While interface-level counters do not show RX drops, the internal RX queue statistics indicate drops.ScopeFortiGate VM, GCP.SolutionThe issue is caused by RX queue buffer exhaustion. When the GCP instance presents only one RX queue, the ring buffer descriptors are exhausted during traffic bursts, leading to packet drops.
incidents.symptom: This article describes the case when a FortiGate VM hosted on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) experiences significant packet loss and latency during high bursts of traffic. While interface-level counters do not show RX drops, the internal RX queue statistics indicate drops
incidents.solution: The issue is caused by RX queue buffer exhaustion. When the GCP instance presents only one RX queue, the ring buffer descriptors are exhausted during traffic bursts, leading to packet drops. incidents.title: FortiManager user session disconnection issues when using Cloudflare ZTNA
incidents.summary: Description When administrators access the FortiManager GUI via Cloudflare ZTNA (Zero Trust Network Access), the login session may automatically terminate or disconnect roughly 30 seconds after logging in. This typically occurs because proxy routing, load-balancing, or edge POP switches cause minor fluctuations in the client's apparent source IP address, triggering session security validation failures on the FortiManager side.
incidents.symptom: When administrators access the FortiManager GUI via Cloudflare ZTNA (Zero Trust Network Access), the login session may automatically terminate or disconnect roughly 30 seconds after logging in. This typically occurs because proxy routing, load-balancing, or edge POP switches cause minor fluctuations in the client's apparent source IP address, triggering session security validation failures on the FortiManager side
incidents.solution: To resolve this issue, you need to configure FortiManager to bypass strict source IP validation checks for active sessions. Log in to the FortiManager CLI as an administrator and execute the following commands: config system global set skip-ip-check-in-session enable end Once this setting is enabled, FortiManager will ignore intermediate source IP modifications or fluctuations during an active session, allowing Cloudflare ZTNA users to maintain a stable, uninterrupted connection to the GUI. incidents.title: FortiPAM retrieves an incorrect FortiClient EMS serial number
incidents.summary: Description FortiPAM retrieves an incorrect FortiClient EMS serial number for synchronized tags, preventing ZTNA access for tagged devices. Scope FortiPAM, FortiClient EMS. Solution Devices with assigned tags in FortiClient EMS cannot access FortiPAM via ZTNA. The tags synchronized from FortiClient EMS to FortiPAM are associated with an incorrect serial number that does not match the actual FortiClient EMS console serial number.
incidents.symptom: FortiPAM retrieves an incorrect FortiClient EMS serial number for synchronized tags, preventing ZTNA access for tagged devices
incidents.solution: Devices with assigned tags in FortiClient EMS cannot access FortiPAM via ZTNA. The tags synchronized from FortiClient EMS to FortiPAM are associated with an incorrect serial number that does not match the actual FortiClient EMS console serial number. Root Cause FortiPAM retrieves the default tenant serial number instead of the specific tenant serial number in multi-tenant FortiClient EMS environments. This is identified as BUG 1343587. Permanent Fix Update FortiClient EMS to version 7.4.9 or later Contournement : Perform the following steps to clear the invalid tags and refresh the synchronization: Clear the invalid tags associated with the incorrect serial number by running the following command on FortiPAM: diagnose endpoint tags remove-by-sn Restart the fabric connector daemon to refresh the data: diag test app fcnacd 99 Verify that the tags are synchronized with the correct serial number using the following commands: diagnose test application fcnacd 2 diagnose test application fcnacd 7 Like Reply Follow Share Powered by Gainsight Terms & Conditions Cookie settings Accessibility statement Sign up Already have an account? incidents.title: Unable to delete the default admin account after migration to AHV
incidents.summary: Description An issue where the default admin account cannot be deleted from FortiManager after migration to a Nutanix AHV environment. Scope This issue has been reported in FortiManager 7.4.11, where the previous environment used was 7.4.8. Solution This is a known issue in FortiManager version 7.4.11 and 7.6.7. incidents.title: Slow dynamic VLAN assignment when using 802.1X and MAC authentication bypass
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes a delay in transitioning a FortiSwitch port to the configured Guest VLAN after a RADIUS server rejects an authentication request. Changing the authentication priority in the 802.1X security policy can help reduce the delay.ScopeFortiGate, FortiSwitch.SolutionSymptomsWhen a device connects to a FortiSwitch port configured for 802.1X and MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB), the port may take approximately one minute to transition from the default VLAN to the configured Guest VLAN after the RADIUS server returns an…
incidents.symptom: This article describes a delay in transitioning a FortiSwitch port to the configured Guest VLAN after a RADIUS server rejects an authentication request. Changing the authentication priority in the 802.1X security policy can help reduce the delay
incidents.solution: SymptomsWhen a device connects to a FortiSwitch port configured for 802.1X and MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB), the port may take approximately one minute to transition from the default VLAN to the configured Guest VLAN after the RADIUS server returns an Access-Reject response.In comparison, when the RADIUS server returns an Access-Accept response, authentication and network access are typically completed much faster.Root CauseThe delay may be related to the authentication priority configured in the 802.1X security policy. When the priority is set to "legacy", the switch may take longer to process the authentication sequence and transition to the Guest VLAN following an authentication failure. Resolution Step 1: Update the Authentication Priority.Log in to the FortiGate CLI and change the authentication priority from "legacy" to "dot1x-mab" in the applicable 802.1X security policy.config switch-controller security-policy 802-1X edit " " set auth-priority dot1x-mab next endReplace with the name of the applicable 802.1X security policy.This setting prioritizes 802.1X and MAB authentication according to the configured authentication sequence and may reduce the time required to transit

incidents.title: RADIUS attributes of users cleared during CSV file import
incidents.summary: Description Importing users via a CSV file with the 'Keep existing user accounts' option enabled may clear RADIUS attributes of existing accounts and prevent user authentication. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution RADIUS attributes of users that are not in the CSV file are deleted after importing a new CSV file. When performing a bulk user import via CSV in FortiAuthenticator, selecting Advanced Options -> Keep existing user accounts clears the 'Certificate Binding' attribute for some existing user accounts.
incidents.symptom: Importing users via a CSV file with the 'Keep existing user accounts' option enabled may clear RADIUS attributes of existing accounts and prevent user authentication
incidents.solution: RADIUS attributes of users that are not in the CSV file are deleted after importing a new CSV file. When performing a bulk user import via CSV in FortiAuthenticator, selecting Advanced Options -> Keep existing user accounts clears the 'Certificate Binding' attribute for some existing user accounts. Affected users lose authentication access. Issue 1-a: Importing a local user CSV file wipes user-bound RADIUS attributes. Issue 1-b: Certificates of users that are not in the CSV file are deleted. Issue 2: CSV Export does not include certificates of type 'Trusted CA'. Issue 3: CSV Export confuses local and remote users with the same ID. These are known issues tracked under the engineering ticket ID 1208720. See: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.2 Release Notes . Reported firmware version: 6.6.6 Resolution: Upgrade FortiAuthenticator to a version where the issue is resolved. The fix is available in the following versions: FortiAuthenticator 6.6.8 FortiAuthenticator 8.0.2

incidents.symptom: This article describes a known issue affecting FortiGate G-Series devices where downgrading or upgrading from v8.0.1 to v8.0.x via the GUI fails, displaying the error status 'Upgrade Failed'
incidents.solution: Example error: During the firmware upgrade attempt, the device status may display the following:Steps to replicate the issue: Log in to a FortiGate G-Series device running FortiOS v8.0.1 build 0245 (Feature).Attempt to upgrade the firmware to FortiOS v8.0.2 using the online upgrade method via FortiGate Cloud or the GUI.Observe that the firmware upgrade fails. The device status displays 'Online - Upgrade failed', and the Upgrade Status displays 'Upgrade failed'. In some instances, the device status may show 'Rebooting with new firmware', while the Upgrade Status displays 'Firmware info unavailable'.Check the console output and observe the following messages:Image verification OK! Failed to get the image encryption key!Retry the firmware upgrade by manually uploading the FortiOS v8.0.2 firmware image through the GUI. The upgrade fails again.Verify that the device remains on FortiOS v8.0.1 build 0245 Contournement : Upgrade the firmware using TFTP via the CLI. Refer to the following guide for the upgrade procedure:Technical Tip: FortiGate TFTP Upgrade Permanent fix:This issue is scheduled to be fixed in FortiOS v8.0.3 build 0270

incidents.title: FortiManager policy package import error "Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device"
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot and fix an import error issue when it shows "Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device". Scope FortiManager, FortiGate. Solution When FortiManager import policy package from FortiGate shows fails as following: The Download Import Report shows as following: "system external-resource",FAIL,"(name=TL-IP-BlockList1, oid=2634, reason=invalid value. object: sys_external_resource. detail: Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device)"…
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to troubleshoot and fix an import error issue when it shows "Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device"
incidents.solution: When FortiManager import policy package from FortiGate shows fails as following: The Download Import Report shows as following: "system external-resource",FAIL,"(name=TL-IP-BlockList1, oid=2634, reason=invalid value. object: sys_external_resource. detail: Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device)" "system external-resource",FAIL,"(name=TL-BlockURL_IP_Group1, oid=2636, reason=invalid value. object: sys_external_resource. detail: Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device)" What happened is FortiManager being unable to copy the password from system external-resource due to it being encrypted. To solve the issue, disable the "private-data-encrytion" in Device Manager -> Device & Groups -> select the FortiGate -> CLI Configurations -> System -> Global. After changing the setting, FortiManager's Import Configuration does not fail anymore. incidents.title: FortiGate 201G upgrade from FortiOS version 8.0.1 to FortiOS version 8.0.2 fails during reboot
incidents.summary: DescriptionUpgrading a FortiGate 201G from FortiOS 8.0.1 to 8.0.2 via the GUI may cause the reboot process to stall and fail.ScopeFortiGate 201G, FortiOS version 8.0.1.SolutionWhen performing a firmware upgrade from FortiOS version 8.0.1 to version 8.0.2 on a FortiGate 201G using the GUI, the system initiates the reboot process but fails to complete it. The process is stuck at the 'Rebooting new firmware' stage and does not finish.Console prints the console prints 'Image verification OK!' followed by 'Failed to get the image encryption key!'.

incidents.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrading to version 7.6.8, when using the FortiGate as an Explicit Proxy with the default settings, chat messages for Copilot will be blocked.ScopeFortiOS version 7.6.8+.SolutionAfter upgrading to version 7.6.8, users who are trying to talk to Copilot may see the following message appear:This is similar behaviour to what would occur on versions 7.6.6 and 7.6.7 due to a known issue in those versions tracked under 1308272 and 1257499.
incidents.symptom: After upgrading to version 7.6.8, when using the FortiGate as an Explicit Proxy with the default settings, chat messages for Copilot will be blocked
incidents.solution: After upgrading to version 7.6.8, users who are trying to talk to Copilot may see the following message appear:This is similar behaviour to what would occur on versions 7.6.6 and 7.6.7 due to a known issue in those versions tracked under 1308272 and 1257499. If on these versions, refer to this article instead:Troubleshooting Tip: Resolving Microsoft Copilot access issues with FortiGate inspecting traffic with a policy in proxy-mode and Application Control/IPS.If being on version 7.6.8 and have this issue, check the Forward Traffic logs filtered to the user's source IP. The following log may be visible:The traffic is being allowed by UTM, but denied by the proxy due to 'traffic denied because uri too long'. The maximum length of a request for an Explicit Proxy is defined by 'max-request-length', and this message will be seen when the proxy blocks the request due to exceeding this limit.The following commands can be used to change this limit:config web-proxy profile set max-request-length 64 endOnce this value is changed to the maximum, the traffic is allowed

incidents.title: LDAPS authentication fails due to an incorrect member-attr configuration
incidents.summary: DescriptionSteps to resolve an issue when users fail to authenticate via LDAPS because the member-attr is incorrectly set to tokenGroups, preventing the FortiGate from matching users to their assigned groups.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionUsers cannot authenticate via LDAPS even though the LDAP server returns a success response. The authentication fails during the group matching phase.The FortiGate is configured to use the tokenGroups attribute to retrieve group memberships.
incidents.symptom: Steps to resolve an issue when users fail to authenticate via LDAPS because the member-attr is incorrectly set to tokenGroups, preventing the FortiGate from matching users to their assigned groups
incidents.solution: Users cannot authenticate via LDAPS even though the LDAP server returns a success response. The authentication fails during the group matching phase.The FortiGate is configured to use the tokenGroups attribute to retrieve group memberships. incidents.title: FortiManager Policy Package install fails with verification error due to "antiphish: max-body-len" parameter
incidents.summary: Description An issue where FortiManager Policy Package installation fails with a verification error due to the " antiphish: max-body-len" parameter under webfilter profiles. Scope FortiManager and FortiProxy 7.4.9 and higher, FortiProxy 7.6.1 and higher Solution When installing a Policy Package from FortiManager to FortiProxy 7.4.9, the installation fails with verification messages similar to the following: (vdom root: webfilter profile "monitor-all" antiphish:max-body-len) remote original: to be installed: 65536 <--- done generating verification…
incidents.symptom: An issue where FortiManager Policy Package installation fails with a verification error due to the " antiphish: max-body-len" parameter under webfilter profiles
incidents.solution: When installing a Policy Package from FortiManager to FortiProxy 7.4.9, the installation fails with verification messages similar to the following: (vdom root: webfilter profile "monitor-all" antiphish:max-body-len) remote original: to be installed: 65536 <--- done generating verification report install failed The same message may be reported for multiple webfilter profiles. The root cause is a difference in the default value of the max-body-len parameter between FortiProxy and FortiManager. Starting with FortiProxy 7.4.9 and 7.6.1, the default value of max-body-len was changed from 65535 to 1024 . However, FortiManager continues to use 65535 as the default value for this parameter. This difference in default values can result in installation verification failure in FortiManager. To work around the issue, configure FortiManager to use the optimal installation verification mode: config system dm set verify-install optimal end Like Reply Follow Share Powered by Gainsight Terms & Conditions Cookie settings Accessibility statement Sign up Already have an account? Scope FortiManager and FortiProxy 7.4.9 and higher, FortiProxy 7.6.1 and higher Solution When installing a Policy Package from FortiManager to FortiProxy 7.4.9, the installation fails with verification messages similar to the following: (vdom root: webfilter profile "monitor-all" antiphish:max-body-len) remote original: to be installed: 65536 <--- done generating verification report install failed The same message may be reported for multiple webfilter profiles. incidents.title: How to fix "error firewall service custom protocol" after ADOM upgrade
incidents.summary: Description A fix for the installation issue with multiple "firewall service custom" objects that may occur after an ADOM upgrade. Post vdom failed: error firewall service custom protocol- TCP_UDP_20101 TCP/UDP/SCTP:-999 - invalid value - prop[protocol]: option(TCP/UDP/SCTP) Copy objects for vdom Main_VDOM "firewall ssl-ssh-profile", "certificate-inspection", id=18459, SKIP - (null) "firewall ssl-ssh-profile", "deep-inspection", id=18474, SKIP - (null) Scope FortiManager.
incidents.symptom: A fix for the installation issue with multiple "firewall service custom" objects that may occur after an ADOM upgrade. Post vdom failed: error firewall service custom protocol- TCP_UDP_20101 TCP/UDP/SCTP:-999 - invalid value - prop[protocol]: option(TCP/UDP/SCTP) Copy objects for vdom Main_VDOM "firewall ssl-ssh-profile", "certificate-inspection", id=18459, SKIP - (null) "firewall ssl-ssh-profile", "deep-inspection", id=18474, SKIP - (null)
incidents.solution: When upgrading from FortiOS 7.4 to 7.6, the default protocol changes from TCP/UDP/SCTP to TCP/UDP/UDP-Lite/SCTP. To match this logic, a 7.6 ADOM should be used in FortiManager. However, it might appear that after upgrading the ADOM, "firewall service custom" objects fail to be installed. When drilling down to the object, it can be observed that the UUID of the object is set to ZERO, which is causing the issue during the installation: To resolve this problem and generate a correct UUID, it is possible to add the comment to the object, click the "Ok" button to update the object, and verify that a new UUID was generated. However, it may be challenging if it requires updating a bunch of such objects. To address this situation, use a script: Step 1: First, print a list of all objects to check how many have a ZERO UUID. execute fmpolic print-adom-object 167 +all Step 2: Take note of all affected objects and create a script. config firewall service custom edit "Jitsi_TCP_4443" unset uuid end Step 3: Run the script against the "Policy Package or ADOM DB". Step 4: Verify the object has a new, updated UUID and the installation runs without an error

incidents.title: Upgrade firmware fails with 'New image is too big'
incidents.summary: Description This article describes troubleshooting steps for issues related to the error 'New image is too big '. Scope FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer. Solution Typically, this error occurs during a FortiAnalyzer or FortiManager 8.0.X firmware update when the target device lacks sufficient flash memory storage to accommodate the new firmware image. This is most commonly documented for FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer VM platforms, where the error message reads: 'New image is too big'.
incidents.symptom: This article describes troubleshooting steps for issues related to the error 'New image is too big '
incidents.solution: Typically, this error occurs during a FortiAnalyzer or FortiManager 8.0.X firmware update when the target device lacks sufficient flash memory storage to accommodate the new firmware image. This is most commonly documented for FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer VM platforms, where the error message reads: 'New image is too big'. This error is not caused by a bug ; it is due to a system requirement to upgrade the products to the latest and larger firmware releases, as indicated here: The minimum size for the flash disk in FortiAnalyzer-VM is 4 GB Most common causes: Insufficient flash disk space : The flash partition does not have enough free space to store the new firmware image during the upgrade process. Small virtual disk allocation : The VM was originally provisioned with a flash disk that is too small for the target firmware version. Diagnostic steps: Take the firmware update from version 8.0.0 to 8.0.1 for FortiAnalyzer VM as an example. Check flash disk usage: Run the following command on the FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer CLI to view the flash disk size and current usage: diagnose system flash list Example output showing the flash disk status: ImageName Version TotalSize(KB) Used(KB) U

incidents.title: FortiManager to FortiGate policy install fails with a custom protocol error
incidents.summary: Description Troubleshooting steps for a custom protocol error that occurs when performing a policy installation to FortiGate. Scope FortiManager. Solution The following issue may be encountered by users when performing policy installation to FortiGate v7.6 to a v7.4 ADOM in FortiManager. This issue occurs because the protocol types defined in the default firewall service objects differ between ADOM versions. For example, in v7.4, the default protocol for the DNS service is TCP/UDP/SCTP , whereas in v7.6, it has been updated to TCP/UDP/UDP-Lite/SCTP .
incidents.symptom: Troubleshooting steps for a custom protocol error that occurs when performing a policy installation to FortiGate
incidents.solution: The following issue may be encountered by users when performing policy installation to FortiGate v7.6 to a v7.4 ADOM in FortiManager. This issue occurs because the protocol types defined in the default firewall service objects differ between ADOM versions. For example, in v7.4, the default protocol for the DNS service is TCP/UDP/SCTP , whereas in v7.6, it has been updated to TCP/UDP/UDP-Lite/SCTP . To resolve this issue, upgrade the ADOM to v7.6 so that the default firewall service object definitions in FortiManager align with those on the FortiGate. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiClient Deployment Stuck at "Endpoint Notified" Without an Upgrade Prompt
incidents.summary: Description This article explains how to troubleshoot FortiClient deployment issues when FortiClient EMS shows the status as Endpoint Notified, but the endpoint does not display an upgrade notification. Scope FortiClient EMS, FortiClient deployment and upgrade troubleshooting. Solution Issue: During a FortiClient upgrade deployment, the deployment status in FortiClient EMS may show Endpoint Notified, while the endpoint does not display an upgrade notification or proceed with the upgrade.
incidents.symptom: This article explains how to troubleshoot FortiClient deployment issues when FortiClient EMS shows the status as Endpoint Notified, but the endpoint does not display an upgrade notification
incidents.solution: Issue: During a FortiClient upgrade deployment, the deployment status in FortiClient EMS may show Endpoint Notified, while the endpoint does not display an upgrade notification or proceed with the upgrade. In this situation, review the FortiClient diagnostic logs to determine whether the endpoint received the upgrade command and whether the installer download was successful. Troubleshooting Steps: Collect the FortiClient diagnostic logs from the affected endpoint. Navigate to the following log file within the diagnostic results: Diagnostic_Result\FCDiagData\general\logs\trace\FortiESNAC.log Search for keywords such as Install , upgrade , or Received upgrade command to identify the upgrade process and any related errors. The log entries can help determine whether the upgrade command was received and whether the installer download was initiated. Example: The following log entry indicates that the endpoint has an upgrade instruction: [2026-10-01 15:45:10.6351388 UTC+11:00] [12344:12348] [FortiESNAC 302 debug] run_installer_cmd.save() success [2026-10-01 15:45:10.6351634 UTC+11:00] [12344:12348] [FortiESNAC 176 debug] startSWUpdate 176 create g_hDownloadSetTimer [2026-10-01 15:45:10.63

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FSSO group lookup fails because of LDAP search 'Timed out' in 5 seconds, ignoring timeout settings
incidents.summary: Description This article describes a known issue in FortiAuthenticator where an LDAP search for users fails due to a 'Timed out' error within 5 seconds, regardless of configured timeout settings. For this reason, FortiAuthenticator fails to perform group lookup, and users are missing in FSSO sessions. Scope FortiAuthenticator, LDAP, FSSO. Solution This issue has occurred in cases where FSSO sessions are missing, and users were unable to access both internal and external resources because the firewall policies were configured based on user groups.

incidents.title: Unable to delete a VDOM from FortiManager when its management VDOM is in a different ADOM
incidents.summary: Description How to delete the VDOM using FortiManager when the management VDOM is not present in the same ADOM as the target VDOM. Scope FortiManager. Solution FortiManager enforces a device/VDOM model constraint that prevents deleting a VDOM while its management VDOM resides in a different ADOM. This article explains the constraint and provides two practical workarounds. FortiManager's ADOM (Administrative Domain) architecture determines how VDOMs are assigned and managed.
incidents.symptom: How to delete the VDOM using FortiManager when the management VDOM is not present in the same ADOM as the target VDOM
incidents.solution: FortiManager enforces a device/VDOM model constraint that prevents deleting a VDOM while its management VDOM resides in a different ADOM. This article explains the constraint and provides two practical workarounds. FortiManager's ADOM (Administrative Domain) architecture determines how VDOMs are assigned and managed. In Normal Device Mode, all VDOMs from a single FortiGate must be placed in the same ADOM. In Advanced Device Mode, individual VDOMs from the same FortiGate can be assigned to separate ADOMs, enabling multi-tenant management. The deletion restriction occurs because FortiManager's device database tracks the management VDOM's ADOM assignment. When the management VDOM is in a different ADOM than the target VDOM, FortiManager cannot process the deletion through its normal device database operations. This is consistent with expected behavior where FortiManager displays errors when the management VDOM is not in the current ADOM for example, the error 'The management VDOM for device xxxxxx is not in the current advanced ADOM' Contournement : 1: Move the VDOM to the Same ADOM. Temporarily move the non-management VDOM so that both the management VDOM and the target VDOM reside in the same ADOM, then delete the VDOM. Workaround 2: Delete Directly on the FortiGate and Resync. Delete the VDOM directly on the FortiGate (bypassing FortiManager's ADOM restriction), then resynchronize the FortiGate on FortiManager. Verify the VDOM is removed from FortiManager's device database. Note : If the VDOM was created in FortiManager's device database but not properly saved, you may encounter an "Internal error" (code -20001) when attempting deletion. In such cases, run the following command on FortiManager to fix the database: diagnose cdb upgrade check resync-dev-vdoms This resyncs and removes any missing VDOMs from the device database

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiGate unable to ping FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer even the ping is allow
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot FortiGate unable to ping FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer even the ping is allow. Scope FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer. Solution Device information: FortiGate port1 = 10.47.6.72/20 ; port4 = 10.133.6.72/20. FortiAnalyzer port1 = 10.47.3.243/20 ; port3 = 10.133.3.243/20. Expected scenario: FortiGate port1 is able to ping FortiAnalyzer port1. FortiGate port4 is able to ping FortiAnalyzer port3.
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to troubleshoot FortiGate unable to ping FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer even the ping is allow
incidents.solution: Device information: FortiGate port1 = 10.47.6.72/20 ; port4 = 10.133.6.72/20. FortiAnalyzer port1 = 10.47.3.243/20 ; port3 = 10.133.3.243/20. Expected scenario: FortiGate port1 is able to ping FortiAnalyzer port1. FortiGate port4 is able to ping FortiAnalyzer port3. Issue scenario: FortiGate port1 is able to ping FortiAnalyzer port1. FortiGate port4 is unable to ping FortiAnalyzer port3. Check steps: In FortiAnalyzer, check that both port1 and port3 configurations are allowed to use the ping service. At FortiAnalyzer, check whether all Administrator Accounts are configured as Trusted Hosts. Solution steps: When in FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer, all Administrator Accounts are configured as Trusted Hosts, the FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer Administrative Access settings will be allowed based on the Trusted Host information. Therefore in FortiAnalyzer, one of the Administrator Accounts must be configured as a Trusted Host that only allows for the IP address range 10.133.0.0/16. After that, FortiGate port4 will be able to ping FortiAnalyzer port3, and also FortiGate port1 will be able to ping FortiAnalyzer port1. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: How to resolve the issue of FortiClient Mac installer not working when Apple's Gatekeeper is set to 'App Store only'
incidents.summary: Description This article describes the issue of the FortiClient Mac installer not working when Apple's Gatekeeper is set to 'App Store only'. Scope FortiClient. Solution When trying to deploy the FortiClient Mac installer via a Jamf Pro instance, the installer generated by FortiClient/EMS does not work in this context. To resolve the issue of the FortiClient Mac installer not working with Gatekeeper, follow these steps: Locate the FortiClient app in Finder (e.g., Downloads folder). 'Right-click' (or 'Ctrl-click') the FortiClient app icon.
incidents.symptom: This article describes the issue of the FortiClient Mac installer not working when Apple's Gatekeeper is set to 'App Store only'
incidents.solution: When trying to deploy the FortiClient Mac installer via a Jamf Pro instance, the installer generated by FortiClient/EMS does not work in this context. To resolve the issue of the FortiClient Mac installer not working with Gatekeeper, follow these steps: Locate the FortiClient app in Finder (e.g., Downloads folder). 'Right-click' (or 'Ctrl-click') the FortiClient app icon. Select Open from the context menu. A warning dialog will appear; select Open. This creates a specific exception for that specific application. After doing this once, FortiClient will open normally by double-clicking in the future. Alternatively, it is possible to try temporarily disabling Gatekeeper: Go to System Preferences -> Security & Privacy -> General . Select the lock icon and enter the password to make changes. Change the setting from App Store to App Store and identified developers (or anywhere if available on older macOS). Install FortiClient. Change the setting back to App Store after the installation is completed. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: SCEP decryption failure with aes-256-cbc encryption
incidents.summary: Description This article describes the cause of SCEP decryption failures on FortiAuthenticator when receiving enrollment requests encrypted with aes-256-cbc from certain third-party devices. Scope FortiAuthenticator, FortiManager, FortiGate. Solution When a third-party device uses aes-256-cbc encryption for SCEP enrollment requests, FortiAuthenticator may fail to decrypt the PKCS#7 enveloped data. This results in a decryption failure during the SCEP process.
incidents.symptom: This article describes the cause of SCEP decryption failures on FortiAuthenticator when receiving enrollment requests encrypted with aes-256-cbc from certain third-party devices
incidents.solution: When a third-party device uses aes-256-cbc encryption for SCEP enrollment requests, FortiAuthenticator may fail to decrypt the PKCS#7 enveloped data. This results in a decryption failure during the SCEP process. Root cause: The issue is caused by a compatibility problem in how FortiAuthenticator handles SCEP requests encrypted with aes-256-cbc. While other encryption methods like des-ede3-cbc work correctly, requests using aes-256-cbc trigger a decryption error in the SCEP daemon. Symptoms: The following error messages appear in the FortiAuthenticator debug logs: PKCS7 message encrypted with aes-256-cbc (427) utils.cpp:386: decryption failed mo_pkcs7unwrap.cpp:526: cannot decrypt PKCS#7 enveloped data error:1C800064:Provider routines:ossl_cipher_unpadblock:bad decrypt Resolution: This is a known issue tracked under engineering ticket 1198353 and is expected to be resolved in an upcoming FortiAuthenticator 8.0.4 GA release. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Intermediate CA cannot be exported as PKCS#12 on FortiAuthenticator version 6.6.10
incidents.summary: Description This article describes the reason why, on FortiAuthenticator 6.6.10, exporting an intermediate CA certificate with its private key in PKCS#12 format fails with the error 'Cannot export PKCS#12 certificate' . incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiManager unable to create a FortiAP K series operation profile even though FortiManager is compatible with FortiAP K series
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot when FortiManager is unable to create a FortiAP K series operation profile, even though FortiManager is compatible with FortiAP K series. Scope FortiManager and FortiGate. Solution In FortiManager, run the following CLI command to check compatibility between FortiManager and FortiAP Models: diagnose dvm supported-platforms list The results show that FortiManager is compatible with the FortiAP 231K model, however, FortiManager is unable to create an Operation Profile.
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to troubleshoot when FortiManager is unable to create a FortiAP K series operation profile, even though FortiManager is compatible with FortiAP K series
incidents.solution: In FortiManager, run the following CLI command to check compatibility between FortiManager and FortiAP Models: diagnose dvm supported-platforms list The results show that FortiManager is compatible with the FortiAP 231K model, however, FortiManager is unable to create an Operation Profile. This is because the results show that FortiManager is compatible with FortiAP 231K model for version 7.4, but not version 7.2. Therefore, FortiManager ADOM version 7.2 will not able to create an Operation Profile for FortiAP 231K. To create an Operation Profile for FortiAP 231K, use FortiManager ADOM version 7.4. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: SCIM user and group synchronization failure between FortiAuthenticator and FortiGate
incidents.summary: Description This article explains how to resolve an issue where users and groups do not synchronize from FortiAuthenticator to FortiGate despite a successful TLS connection. Scope FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator. Solution When FortiAuthenticator acts as a SCIM client and FortiGate acts as a SCIM server, the synchronization of users and groups may fail if the base URL is configured incorrectly. Even if the TLS connection is established, the FortiGate SCIM daemon may fail to associate the incoming request with the configured SCIM client.
incidents.symptom: This article explains how to resolve an issue where users and groups do not synchronize from FortiAuthenticator to FortiGate despite a successful TLS connection
incidents.solution: When FortiAuthenticator acts as a SCIM client and FortiGate acts as a SCIM server, the synchronization of users and groups may fail if the base URL is configured incorrectly. Even if the TLS connection is established, the FortiGate SCIM daemon may fail to associate the incoming request with the configured SCIM client. The issue occurs when the base-url in the FortiGate SCIM configuration includes a port number. The base URI should typically consist of the protocol, domain name, and initial path. Including the port number in the base-url prevents the FortiGate from correctly identifying the SCIM client, resulting in the following debug error: diagnose debug reset diagnose debug application scim -1 diagnose debug enable url:https://10.5.146.127/scim/v2/Users/user_2 HTTP/1.1 used to find client:NULL. can't found client or client disabled. change state from wait_req to disconnect change state from disconnect to done change state from init to accepting change state from accepting to connect SSL_accept succeeded. Resolution Log in to the FortiGate command line interface. Verify the current SCIM configuration to check for a port number in the base-url: show user scim Remove the port numbe

incidents.symptom: This article describes how to resolve the 'Error importing configuration file' message when importing a modified FortiClient configuration file on macOS

incidents.title: Technical Tip: FortiClient installer download fails when the package name contains spaces
incidents.summary: Description This article describes a FortiClient installer download failure associated with spaces in the installer package name and provides a workaround with examples. Scope FortiClient EMS 7.4.8 and FortiClient EMS Cloud. Solution A space in the installer package name may cause the executable download to fail, even when the package directory is accessible and lists the installer files. Example 1: Package name containing a space: For the package named fct 7.4 , the directory listing displays the executable forticlientsetup_7.4.8_x64.exe.
incidents.symptom: This article describes a FortiClient installer download failure associated with spaces in the installer package name and provides a workaround with examples
incidents.solution: A space in the installer package name may cause the executable download to fail, even when the package directory is accessible and lists the installer files. Example 1: Package name containing a space: For the package named fct 7.4 , the directory listing displays the executable forticlientsetup_7.4.8_x64.exe. However, selecting the executable returns the following error: Not Found The requested resource was not found on this server. Example download path: /installers/default/fct%207.4/forticlientsetup_7.4.8_x64.exe The %20 sequence represents the space in the package name. The directory listing shows that the file is present, but does not confirm that its download will succeed. Example 2: Package name without spaces: For the package named 7.4.8 , selecting the executable opens the browser's Save As dialog, showing that the download can be initiated. Example download path: /installers/default/7.4.8/forticlientsetup_7.4.8_x64.exe Contournement : Create a new installer package in FortiClient EMS using a name without spaces, such as prueba_server_EMS. Wait for package creation to complete. Open the newly generated download link and select the executable to verify that the download starts successfully. Distribute the new download link after validation. Replacing %20 with an underscore in the existing URL alone does not create a corresponding package. Use the download link generated for the newly created installer. Additional checks: If the download still fails, verify the required network connectivity and license synchronization status before generating another package. Planned improvement: An improvement related to installer download links for package names containing spaces is currently planned for FortiClient EMS 7.4.9 . Inclusion remains subject to successful QA validation and may change. Consult the release notes when the version becomes available to confirm inclusion. Until the improvement is available and validated, continue using installer package names without spaces. incidents.title: Technical Tip: Clarification of the 'cannot get DNS name of domain x.x.x.x from Domain Manager' in FSSO debug log when Entra ID is being used
incidents.summary: Description This article clarifies the error log message 'cannot get DNS name of domain x.x.x.x from Domain Manager' in the FSSO debug log in the FortiAuthenticator when Entra ID is being used and remote LDAP is not configured. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution FortiAuthenticator FSSO supports logon events from native Microsoft Entra ID-joined workstations through the FortiClient SSOMA (FortiClient Single Sign-On Mobility Agent).
incidents.symptom: This article clarifies the error log message 'cannot get DNS name of domain x.x.x.x from Domain Manager' in the FSSO debug log in the FortiAuthenticator when Entra ID is being used and remote LDAP is not configured
incidents.solution: FortiAuthenticator FSSO supports logon events from native Microsoft Entra ID-joined workstations through the FortiClient SSOMA (FortiClient Single Sign-On Mobility Agent). For example, when an endpoint joined to Microsoft Entra ID connects to the network, FortiClient SSOMA sends the user identity and endpoint IP address to FortiAuthenticator. FortiAuthenticator then performs a group membership lookup against Microsoft Entra ID through the OAuth API and shares the retrieved Entra ID group membership information with the FortiGate. The configuration example can be found in the following document: FortiAuthenticator SSOMA for native Microsoft Entra ID joined workstation In a normal scenario, the following FSSO debug messages can be observed at 'https:// /debug/fsso-agent/' when FortiAuthenticator processes the SSOMA logon event and performs the Entra ID group membership lookup through the OAuth API: 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] FortiClient connected: 2540D4605FDD4FB125FD1B532DECD268/192.168.1.20 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] Received 1 event(s) from FCT: 192.168.1.20 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] FCT LOGON 2026-02-10-10:50:23/1970-01-01-10:00:00 FortiClient (null):L2003.TESTDOMAIN

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: certificate-based VPN authentication on FortiClient Android fails for devices managed by Microsoft Intune
incidents.summary: Description This article describes a configuration issue that prevents certificate-based VPN authentication on FortiClient Android to work correctly, when the device running FortiClient Android is managed by Microsoft Intune. This article also proposes a proper solution for the issue in question. Scope FortiClient EMS, FortiClient Android. Solution FortiClient EMS supports Microsoft Intune integration, including FortiClient Android and FortiClient iOS for mobile platforms.
incidents.symptom: This article describes a configuration issue that prevents certificate-based VPN authentication on FortiClient Android to work correctly, when the device running FortiClient Android is managed by Microsoft Intune. This article also proposes a proper solution for the issue in question
incidents.solution: FortiClient EMS supports Microsoft Intune integration, including FortiClient Android and FortiClient iOS for mobile platforms. Certificate-based VPN authentication can be configured to authenticate FortiClient Android and FortiClient iOS mobile devices. The Intune Deployment provides all the details on how to deploy FortiClient using Microsoft Intune integration. Certificates can be deployed to mobile devices using two distinct certificate profiles for Microsoft Intune (see Trusted root certificate profiles for Microsoft Intune ): SCEP certificate profile. PKCS certificate profile. In the course of certificate-based VPN authentication setup procedure, if an SCEP certificate profile is deployed to Android devices, no configured VPN connections can be established. FortiClient Android will fail immediately, without trying to connect to the FortiGate unit (VPN peer device). Due to a Microsoft Intune limitation, SCEP certificate profiles do not support VPN configuration for general Android devices. incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to fix an error that occurs with a virtual appliance and manual static IP address assignment in the appliance console of FortiClient EMS. It specifically occurs after a FortiClient EMS server v7.4.8 fresh installation. Scope FortiClient EMS. Solution During FortiClient EMS server installation as a VMWare Virtual Appliance, manual static IP address assignment on a fresh login via the GUI may result in an error message stating that the IP address has changed under the FortiClient EMS settings page.
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to fix an error that occurs with a virtual appliance and manual static IP address assignment in the appliance console of FortiClient EMS. It specifically occurs after a FortiClient EMS server v7.4.8 fresh installation
incidents.solution: During FortiClient EMS server installation as a VMWare Virtual Appliance, manual static IP address assignment on a fresh login via the GUI may result in an error message stating that the IP address has changed under the FortiClient EMS settings page. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Authentication Failure for Administrator Role Users After Upgrading FortiAuthenticator
incidents.summary: Description This article describes an issue where administrator role users are unable to authenticate after upgrading FortiAuthenticator from version 6.6.2 to 6.6.10, while other users can log in successfully. The issue is related to CHAP authentication. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution If an administrator-role user is unable to authenticate through SSL VPN after upgrading FortiAuthenticator to version 6.6.10, recreate the affected user account in FortiAuthenticator and reassign the FortiToken.
incidents.symptom: This article describes an issue where administrator role users are unable to authenticate after upgrading FortiAuthenticator from version 6.6.2 to 6.6.10, while other users can log in successfully. The issue is related to CHAP authentication
incidents.solution: If an administrator-role user is unable to authenticate through SSL VPN after upgrading FortiAuthenticator to version 6.6.10, recreate the affected user account in FortiAuthenticator and reassign the FortiToken. Perform the following steps: Delete the affected administrator user from FortiAuthenticator. Re-import the user from the configured LDAP server. Reassign the FortiToken to the newly imported user. Test SSL VPN authentication with the affected user. After completing these steps, the user should be able to authenticate successfully through SSL VPN. This procedure can be used as a workaround when only specific administrator-role users are affected following the FortiAuthenticator upgrade. incidents.symptom: This article describes a known issue that causes FortiClient installations on distributions using DNF5 to fail due to a lack of digest
incidents.solution: Fedora Linux 43 and higher updates the included RPM package manager to RPM 6.0, which deprecates support for SHA1 digests. When attempting to install the FortiClient v7.4.7 and earlier as an RPM package with DNF on these distributions, the install will fail and the following error message may be seen: package forticlient-7.4.7.5438-1.el7.x86_64 does not verify: no digest This occurs because the current FortiClient RPM package headers only including SHA1 digests Contournement : DNF does not allow skipping the digest check for packages. It is possible to workaround this issue using a different package management tool, for example the included RPM: sudo dnf install dnf-utils nss-tools sudo rpm -i --nodigest forticlient-7.4.7.5438-1.el7.x86_64.rpm Note: Unlike DNF, RPM does not automatically install dependencies. If the FortiClient installation still fails, verify any missing dependencies. Resolution: The issue is resolved in the following FortiClient Linux versions, which include a SHA256 signature: FortiClient Linux v7.4.8. FortiClient Linux v8.0.0. Note: the latest FortiClient Standalone version is currently v7.4.7. A FortiClient Standalone version with the fix is planned for release in FortiClient Linux v8.0.2. incidents.title: Technical Tip: How to fix BdsDxe : failed to load Boot0001 UEFI NUTANUX VDISK in Nutanix Environment
incidents.summary: Description This article describes a failed deployment of a FortiAnalyzer instance when performing VM migrations from VMware (ESXi) to Nutanix. Scope FortiAnalyzer. Solution Error: Reason: Wrong boot mode selection: FortiAnalyzer firmware images have strict requirements regarding the hypervisor BIOS type. The boot disk is attached to the wrong bus: FortiAnalyzer images expect the virtual disk to be mapped correctly so the bootloader can initialize.
incidents.symptom: This article describes a failed deployment of a FortiAnalyzer instance when performing VM migrations from VMware (ESXi) to Nutanix
incidents.solution: Error: Reason: Wrong boot mode selection: FortiAnalyzer firmware images have strict requirements regarding the hypervisor BIOS type. The boot disk is attached to the wrong bus: FortiAnalyzer images expect the virtual disk to be mapped correctly so the bootloader can initialize. Missing or unassigned secondary data: DiskFortiAnalyzer is a logging and reporting tool; it cannot function or boot correctly without a dedicated storage partition. Resolution: Change the boot mode in the Nutanix Environment: In the Nutanix Prism console, go to Update VM -> Boot Configuration -> Change the boot mode from UEFI to Legacy BIOS (or Default) . Cloned .qcow2 boot image disk: Clone the image and explicitly attach it to the SCSI bus (e.g., SCSI Index 0). Add a new disk to the instance: Create a second, empty disk on the SCSI bus (e.g., 100 GB+ depending on licensing requirements) alongside the primary boot disk

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiClient auto-patch failure due to certificate validation issues
incidents.summary: Description This article describes a scenario where the FortiClient auto-patch feature fails to download and install patches due to certificate validation issues. The user may encounter an error code 60, indicating a problem with the TLS certificate validation. Scope FortiClient v7.2 and v7.4. Solution The FortiClient vulnerability scan logs will show the following error: installerURL: https://github.com/notepad-plus-plus/notepad-plus-plus/releases/download/v8.9.1/npp.8.9.1.Installer.x64.exe ...
incidents.symptom: This article describes a scenario where the FortiClient auto-patch feature fails to download and install patches due to certificate validation issues. The user may encounter an error code 60, indicating a problem with the TLS certificate validation
incidents.solution: The FortiClient vulnerability scan logs will show the following error: installerURL: https://github.com/notepad-plus-plus/notepad-plus-plus/releases/download/v8.9.1/npp.8.9.1.Installer.x64.exe ... Downloading installer. Attempt: 1/3 Download attempt 1 failed with error code: 60 Downloading installer. Attempt: 2/3 Download attempt 2 failed with error code: 60 Downloading installer. Attempt: 3/3 Download attempt 3 failed with error code: 60 ... Downloading Error. Max attempts reached. Please check the installer URL: https://github.com/notepad-plus-plus/notepad-plus-plus/releases/download/v8.9.1/npp.8.9.1.Installer.x64.exe This log can be found on the following path and the file name is vcm_result: 'C:\Program Files\Fortinet\FortiClient\logs\vcm'. To resolve the FortiClient Auto-Patch failure due to certificate validation issues, follow these steps: Verify that the Windows Automatic Root Certificate Update feature is enabled on the endpoint. This feature is enabled by default on Windows 10 and later versions. Check the Windows Trusted Root Certification Authorities store to ensure it is up-to-date. The store can be updated manually by running the command: certutil -generateSSTFromWU r

incidents.summary: Description This article describes how the error 'Image validation failed: The current image model number is different from the appliance's.' can occur on FortiAuthenticator VM when trying to update from firmware version 6.6.7, and how to resolve it. Scope FortiAuthenticator VM v6.6.7. Solution Under some circumstances, the error message 'Image validation failed: The current image model number is different from the appliance's.' may crop up when trying to upgrade a VM from firmware version 6.6.7.
incidents.symptom: This article describes how the error 'Image validation failed: The current image model number is different from the appliance's.' can occur on FortiAuthenticator VM when trying to update from firmware version 6.6.7, and how to resolve it
incidents.solution: Under some circumstances, the error message 'Image validation failed: The current image model number is different from the appliance's.' may crop up when trying to upgrade a VM from firmware version 6.6.7. The error usually includes the detail '(current appliance model is FACVMS)'. After uploading the target firmware, FortiAuthenticator can show an error as depicted here: This occurs under the following conditions: The FortiAuthenticator VM is currently in firmware version 6.6.7 (either deployed or upgraded to it). A subscription license was uploaded to FortiAuthenticator VM. Subscription licenses can be identified by the serial number beginning with 'FACVMSxxxxxxxxx' and is visible in the dashboard. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Incorrect VLAN assignment when using FortiAuthenticator dynamic VLANs
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot incorrect VLAN assignment when FortiAuthenticator is used to return dynamic VLAN attributes in RADIUS Access-Accept messages. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution Incorrect VLAN assignment may occur when FortiAuthenticator is configured for RADIUS Authentication if the same remote LDAP user or computer object is a member of more than one Active Directory or FortiAuthenticator user group, and when each group has a different RADIUS VLAN attribute configured.
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to troubleshoot incorrect VLAN assignment when FortiAuthenticator is used to return dynamic VLAN attributes in RADIUS Access-Accept messages
incidents.solution: Incorrect VLAN assignment may occur when FortiAuthenticator is configured for RADIUS Authentication if the same remote LDAP user or computer object is a member of more than one Active Directory or FortiAuthenticator user group, and when each group has a different RADIUS VLAN attribute configured. For example, if a user or device is a member of both the Students and the Staff group, then the FortiAuthenticator will return both VLANs to the NAC (e.g., FortiGate). Since the NAC (Network Enforcement Device, e.g. a FortiGate) can only assign 1 x VLAN, the latter of the two will be assigned to the client device, which may or may not be correct, possibly resulting in a Student being placed in the Staff VLAN (or vice versa). To troubleshoot this behaviour, check the RADIUS Access-Accept message in FortiAuthenticator's RADIUS debug (i.e. https:// /debug/radius) and confirm whether more than one VLAN is being returned. Correct example (1 x PVID is returned): Tunnel-Medium-Type += IEEE-802 Tunnel-Private-Group-Id += "58" Tunnel-Type += VLAN Problem example (2 x PVIDs are returned): Tunnel-Medium-Type += IEEE-802 Tunnel-Medium-Type += IEEE-802 Tunnel-Private-Group-Id += "58" Tunnel-Type += VLA
