Solution Confirm whether the network environment has implemented deep inspection or certificate replacement. Test the connection to the EMS cloud telemetry using a mobile hotspot to cross-verify. Access the path provided below to review either FortiESNAC_1.log or FortiESNAC_2.log based on the latest modification date.

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Incorrect user triggered for push notification
incidents.summary: Description This article describes a known issue that push notification triggers for wrong user intermittently, FortiAuthenticator debug logs show a different username being matched. The user is able to log in using the token manually, but the push notification is not being received. Scope FortiAuthenticator, FortiAuthenticator Agent. Solution For example: The user 'Emerson' is getting incorrect random Fortitoken push triggers that appear to be originating from the user 'Emer'.
incidents.symptom: This article describes a known issue that push notification triggers for wrong user intermittently, FortiAuthenticator debug logs show a different username being matched. The user is able to log in using the token manually, but the push notification is not being received
incidents.solution: For example: The user 'Emerson' is getting incorrect random Fortitoken push triggers that appear to be originating from the user 'Emer'. If the user 'Emerson' accepts the invalid push, the reply times out in the app. In FortiAuthenticator logs, when the issue happens: the 'Emer' user shows as 'Emerson', and 'Emerson' is also an active user. See the following log. It is meant to be an entry for the 'Emer' user, but it shows as 'Emerson': 2026-06-15T16:07:42.003325-04:00 HQFAC radiusd[6015]: (53417) facauth: Updated auth log 'lab.local/Emerson' for attempt from REST API: Remote LDAP user authentication from (null) with FortiToken failed: invalid token. The issue seems to happen randomly. The user 'Emer' is able to log in using manual token entry. This is a known issue with the id 1312120 and is resolved in firmware version 8.0.4. There is a special build on v8.0.3: contact Fortinet Support to get the special build. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: 'ZTNA Application Not Found' error with 'Error Code 022' in ZTNA TCP forwarding
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot the ZTNA Application Not Found error with error code 022 when FortiClient attempts to access an application using ZTNA TCP forwarding. Scope FortiGate, FortiClient, ZTNA. Solution When attempting to access an application using ZTNA TCP forwarding, FortiClient may display the ZTNA Application Not Found error with error code 022: This error can occur when the destination application requested by FortiClient does not match a real server configured under the FortiGate ZTNA Access Proxy API gateway.
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to troubleshoot the ZTNA Application Not Found error with error code 022 when FortiClient attempts to access an application using ZTNA TCP forwarding
incidents.solution: When attempting to access an application using ZTNA TCP forwarding, FortiClient may display the ZTNA Application Not Found error with error code 022: This error can occur when the destination application requested by FortiClient does not match a real server configured under the FortiGate ZTNA Access Proxy API gateway. Collect the FortiClient diagnostic logs from an affected endpoint and review the following log file: FCDiagData\general\logs\trace\fortitcs\_1.log Search for ZTNA Application Not Found or error code 022 and review the corresponding TCP-forwarding request. For example: [2026-08-04 17:23:52.3686208] [fortitcs] Request: GET /tcp?address=app.example.com&port=443&tls=0 HTTP/1.1 Host: ztna.example.com:10443 Accept: */* Authorization: ***** Cookie: ***** Upgrade: tcp-forwarding/1.0 User-Agent: Forticlient X-Fos-Auth: [2026-08-04 17:23:52.4849079] [fortitcs] response code: 403 html Reply: ZTNA Access Denied ZTNA Application Not Found Error Code: 022 Error Message: The page you requested has been blocked because the real server in the API gateway cannot be found. The request identifies the destination application and destination port: GET /tcp?address=app.example.com&port=443

incidents.title: Technical Tip: Error 'relation does not exist' when running a custom SQL dataset on FortiAnalyzer v7.6.3
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to address the following error which may occur when executing a custom SQL dataset on FortiAnalyzer v7.6.3: ERROR: relation "adom***_fgt_wlog" does not exist LINE 5: ...vname","csf","devgrps" ,ti6.epname AS epname FROM adom***_FG... incidents.title: Technical Tip: EAP-TLS Authentication Fails with error 'Authentication failed for EAP method type 13'
incidents.summary: Description This article describes the steps to troubleshoot EAP authentication failure on FortiAuthenticator. The user is experiencing issues with EAP authentication, resulting in an error message indicating that authentication failed for EAP method type 13 (EAP-TLS). This message is generic and returned by the client/supplicant whenever the TLS handshake or certificate validation fails during EAP-TLS negotiation. The actual reason must be identified from FortiAuthenticator debug logs, client-side logs, or packet captures.
incidents.symptom: This article describes the steps to troubleshoot EAP authentication failure on FortiAuthenticator. The user is experiencing issues with EAP authentication, resulting in an error message indicating that authentication failed for EAP method type 13 (EAP-TLS). This message is generic and returned by the client/supplicant whenever the TLS handshake or certificate validation fails during EAP-TLS negotiation. The actual reason must be identified from FortiAuthenticator debug logs, client-side logs, or packet captures
incidents.solution: To troubleshoot EAP authentication failure on FortiAuthenticator, follow these steps: Verify CA and certificate configuration Confirm that the CA certificate is correctly configured and has the appropriate Client Authentication or Server Authentication entries under its Key Usage / Extended Key Usage list. On the FortiGate CLI, run the following command to check the configured WiFi CA and server certificate: get system global | grep wifi This will show the 'wifi-ca-certificate' and 'wifi-certificate' currently in use, allowing to confirm the correct certificates are assigned. Check the certificate chain. Ensure that the Root CA and any Intermediate CA(s) that issued the client and/or server certificates are installed and trusted: On FortiAuthenticator: under Certificate Management -> Certificate Authorities -> Trusted CAs . On the client device: In the OS/device trusted root and intermediate certificate store. A missing intermediate CA is a common cause of TLS validation failure even when the leaf certificate is valid. Verify CRL/OCSP reachability: Verify that the client can reach the CRL/OCSP endpoints. If not required, consider disabling revocation checks for testing. Investigate

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiClientEMS Upgrade Failure due to Grafana Package Error
incidents.summary: Description This article describes a solution to an issue where the upgrade of FortiClientEMS fails due to a Grafana package error. The upgrade from version 7.4.7 to 7.4.8 results in a failed upgrade. The error message observed: Setting up grafana (13.1.1) ... mv: cannot move '/usr/share/grafana/data/plugins-bundled' to '/var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled': Directory not empty dpkg: error processing package grafana (--configure): installed grafana package post-installation script subprocess returned error exit status 1 Errors were encountered while…
incidents.symptom: This article describes a solution to an issue where the upgrade of FortiClientEMS fails due to a Grafana package error. The upgrade from version 7.4.7 to 7.4.8 results in a failed upgrade. The error message observed: Setting up grafana (13.1.1) ... mv: cannot move '/usr/share/grafana/data/plugins-bundled' to '/var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled': Directory not empty dpkg: error processing package grafana (--configure): installed grafana package post-installation script subprocess returned error exit status 1 Errors were encountered while processing: grafana dpkg configure failed. Aborting
incidents.solution: The EMS v7.4.8 upgrade includes a Grafana package update (to v13.1.1 in this case). During the package installation, the post-installation script attempts to move the bundled plugins directory from the package's default location (/usr/share/grafana/data/plugins-bundled) to the runtime data directory (/var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled). The error Directory not empty means that /var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled already existed and contained files when the mv command tried to move the new bundled plugins there. Note: This is a known issue with Grafana v13.1.1: Upgrade to Grafana 13.1.1 had errors . To resolve the EMS upgrade failure due to a Grafana package error, follow these steps: Run the command to rename the plugins-bundled directory. sudo mv /var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled /var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled.bak Run the command to configure the packages. sudo dpkg --configure -a Retry the upgrade process to complete the installation of FortiClient/EMS version 7.4.8. By following these steps, the upgrade failure due to the Grafana package error should be resolved, and the FortiClientEMS upgrade should complete successfully. forticlientems Like Reply Follow Share Powered by Gainsight

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: How to troubleshoot a FortiAnalyzer-BigData firmware upgrade that fails the NTP pre-upgrade check due to NTP server rate limiting
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot a FortiAnalyzer-BigData firmware upgrade that fails the NTP pre-upgrade check due to NTP server rate limiting. It also explains the difference between NTP synchronization on the FortiAnalyzer-BigData Main Host and the Security Event Manager Controller, and why the controller may generate significantly more NTP requests than the Main Host. Scope FortiAnalyzer-BigData.
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to troubleshoot a FortiAnalyzer-BigData firmware upgrade that fails the NTP pre-upgrade check due to NTP server rate limiting. It also explains the difference between NTP synchronization on the FortiAnalyzer-BigData Main Host and the Security Event Manager Controller, and why the controller may generate significantly more NTP requests than the Main Host
incidents.solution: Starting from FortiAnalyzer-BigData v7.2.7 , the firmware upgrade process includes an NTP preflight validation. Accurate and consistent time synchronization is important for the distributed BigData cluster. If the configured NTP server cannot be successfully validated, the firmware upgrade is blocked. A typical symptom is that NTP synchronization on the Main Host appears healthy: diagnose system ntp status MS Name/IP address Stratum Poll Reach LastRx Last sample =============================================================================== ^* ntp-server.example.com 2 9 377 301 -92us[-123us] +/- 622us However, checking NTP from the Security Event Manager Controller may intermittently fail: fazbdadm check ntp ntpdate: rate limit response from server. ntpdate: no server suitable for synchronization found [ERR] NTP server ntp-server.example.com is not valid or not reachable Running the same command again may succeed: fazbdadm check ntp server , stratum 2, offset -0.000775, delay 0.02631 adjust time server offset -0.000775 sec NTP server ntp-server.example.com is valid~ This behavior can occur when the external NTP infrastructure applies rate limiting to the Security Event Manager Cont

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Getting error message 'Error resizing disk partition' in FortiClient EMS in AWS environment
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to resolve the issue 'Error resizing disk partition' in FortiClient EMS in an AWS environment. Scope FortiClient EMS v7.4 onwards in an AWS environment. Solution When FortiClient EMS is deployed in an AWS environment, run the command below to expand disk space: execute lvm expand-disk --disk.name nvme0n1 It shows the error: 'Error resizing disk partition: exit status 5'. Solution : This is currently a known issue when FortiClient EMS is deployed in an AWS environment specifically.

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiClient EMS SAML Authentication Failure when FortiClient shows a 'Server encountered an error, please try again later' message
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot SAML authentication issues in FortiClient EMS when FortiClient shows a ' Server encountered an error, please try again later ' message during user authentication. In this scenario, users are unable to register FortiClient with FortiClient EMS using an invitation code because the SAML authentication process fails. Scope FortiClient EMS. FortiGate. Solution If users encounter a server error when authenticating with SAML, perform the following checks: In FortiClient EMS , navigate to User Management…
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to troubleshoot SAML authentication issues in FortiClient EMS when FortiClient shows a ' Server encountered an error, please try again later ' message during user authentication. In this scenario, users are unable to register FortiClient with FortiClient EMS using an invitation code because the SAML authentication process fails
incidents.solution: If users encounter a server error when authenticating with SAML, perform the following checks: In FortiClient EMS , navigate to User Management -> SAML Configuration and edit the affected SAML profile. Verify the Service Provider (SP) certificate configured in the SAML profile. Ensure the certificate is a server certificate . Do not use a wildcard certificate, as it may prevent the SAML signing key from loading correctly. If necessary, temporarily remove the configured SP certificate and test the authentication again to determine whether the certificate is the source of the issue. Review the FortiClient EMS diagnostic logs for SAML-related errors. In particular, examine the following FortiClient EMS log file: python_logs/debug_ - - A common indication of this issue is the following error: xmlsec.Error: (1, 'cannot load key') This error typically indicates that FortiClient EMS is unable to load the private key associated with the configured SP certificate. After correcting the certificate configuration, retry the FortiClient registration using the invitation code. For additional information about configuring SAML authentication, refer to SAML Configuration . Like 2 Reply Follow Shar

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: TACACS Client with subnet in FortiAuthenticator is not working
incidents.summary: Description This article describes that the user is unable to authenticate with a TACACS username that is configured in FortiAuthenticator, resulting in an error message 'Unknown user authentication from (null) with no token failed: Unable to find authpolicy to process'. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution To configure a TACACS client with a subnet in FortiAuthenticator, follow these steps: Go to Authentication -> TACACS+ Service -> Clients .
incidents.symptom: This article describes that the user is unable to authenticate with a TACACS username that is configured in FortiAuthenticator, resulting in an error message 'Unknown user authentication from (null) with no token failed: Unable to find authpolicy to process'
incidents.solution: To configure a TACACS client with a subnet in FortiAuthenticator, follow these steps: Go to Authentication -> TACACS+ Service -> Clients . In this example, there are three clients configured, and the test client IP is 10.47.21.122. Go to Authentication -> TACACS+ Service -> Policies , verify that the subnet is added to the TACACS policy. Try accessing the device with the username and password that were created on FortiAuthenticator, and it shows 'Access denied'. Go to Logging -> Log Access -> Logs ; it shows 'Unknown user authentication from (null) with no token failed: Unable to find authpolicy to process'. To solve the issue, go to Authentication -> TACACS+ Service -> Clients , delete the client name 'FortiGate-60F', which is configured as IP 10.47.21.122. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiAuthenticator v6.6.9 - users unable to authenticate against LDAP Trusted Domains
incidents.summary: Description This article describe how to resolve user authentication issues with LDAP after upgrading from FortiAuthenticator v6.5.6 to v6.6.9. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution By using an Active Directory forest with multiple domains, it appears that in version 6.5.6, communication between trusted domains worked even when the Allow Trusted Domain option was disabled. Starting with version 6.6.9 however, this option must be enabled for cross-domain authentication to function correctly.

Servers -> LDAP , Windows Active Directory Domain Authentication section: After upgrading to FortiAuthenticator v6.6.9, issues may be encountered where users authenticating via LDAP are no longer able to log in. To resolve this issue, enable the Allow Trusted Domain option in the LDAP server configuration: After enabling the Allow Trusted Domain option, FortiAuthenticator will be able to authenticate users from different trusted domains within the forest. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Addressing 'IKE message other than DPD retransmit to maximum.' error when connecting to IKEv2 VPN tunnel
incidents.summary: Description This article describes the steps to resolve IKEv2 IPsec VPN connection issues with FortiClient, specifically when encountering the 'IKE message other than DPD retransmit to maximum' error. Scope FortiClient, FortiClientEMS, FortiGate, IPsec, IKEv2. Solution When the network connection is not reliable or ISP or perimeter network/security devices block or cause packet fragmentation of oversized packets, which is often the case with IPsec UDP packets, especially during public key transfer, the 'IKE message other than DPD retransmit to…
incidents.symptom: This article describes the steps to resolve IKEv2 IPsec VPN connection issues with FortiClient, specifically when encountering the 'IKE message other than DPD retransmit to maximum' error
incidents.solution: When the network connection is not reliable or ISP or perimeter network/security devices block or cause packet fragmentation of oversized packets, which is often the case with IPsec UDP packets, especially during public key transfer, the 'IKE message other than DPD retransmit to maximum.' error may occur, causing the connection to fail. This article offers a solution for this issue that can be found below: On FortiClientEMS, navigate to Endpoint Profiles -> Remote Access -> Select the profile in question and select Edit . Scroll down to Tunnels and select the tunnel to edit (if the FortiClientEMS version is 8.0.0, the tunnel section is located at the top of the page). In the Phase 1 settings, enable IKE Fragmentation . Save the changes. Refer to the IPsec VPN for more information on configuring IPsec VPN settings and learning about IKE Fragmentation. incidents.title: Technical Tip: RADIUS Connectivity fails displaying error 'peer did not return a certificate' after the upgrade of FortiAuthenticator Cloud
incidents.summary: Description This article describes a scenario in which, after upgrading FortiAuthenticator Cloud to v8.0.x, RADIUS connectivity can fail. Scope FortiAuthenticator v8.0.x Solution After upgrading FortiAuthenticator Cloud to v8.0.x, the admin may see 'error checking radius connectivity' on the FortiGate. RadSec (RADIUS over TLS) does mutual TLS. After v8.0.x, FortiAuthenticator Cloud started requiring a client certificate from the FortiGate side, not just accepting the server certificate.
incidents.symptom: This article describes a scenario in which, after upgrading FortiAuthenticator Cloud to v8.0.x, RADIUS connectivity can fail
incidents.solution: After upgrading FortiAuthenticator Cloud to v8.0.x, the admin may see 'error checking radius connectivity' on the FortiGate. RadSec (RADIUS over TLS) does mutual TLS. After v8.0.x, FortiAuthenticator Cloud started requiring a client certificate from the FortiGate side, not just accepting the server certificate. In the FortiAuthenticator Cloud, RADIUS over TLS logs, logscan can be verified through https:// /debug/radius. The admin can observe the error 'Peer did not return a certificate'. The client is now required and needs to be uploaded and configured in the FortiGate RADIUS configuration. Creating the user/client cert (on FortiAuthenticator) : Go to Certificate Management -> End Entities -> Users and create a new certificate request for the FortiGate acting as RadSec client. Sign it with FortiAuthenticator's own Local CA unless an external PKI is being used. Export the resulting certificate as PKCS#12 bundle including a private key in order to import it in FortiGate. Importing certificates on FortiGate : Import the CA first: System -> Certificates -> Import -> CA Certificate and upload the FortiAuthenticator local CA's public certificate (PEM). incidents.title: Technical Tip: Intune SCEP Challenge Validation Fails with FortiAuthenticator
incidents.summary: Description This article describes an issue faced in FortiAuthenticator where the scepd daemon requests an OAuth token scoped to Microsoft Graph (https://graph.microsoft.com/.default) instead of the Microsoft Intune API (https://api.manage.microsoft.com/.default) during SCEP challenge validation. This causes the Intune SCEP validation endpoint to return an empty response, and certificate enrollment fails. Scope FortiAuthenticator.
incidents.symptom: This article describes an issue faced in FortiAuthenticator where the scepd daemon requests an OAuth token scoped to Microsoft Graph (https://graph.microsoft.com/.default) instead of the Microsoft Intune API (https://api.manage.microsoft.com/.default) during SCEP challenge validation. This causes the Intune SCEP validation endpoint to return an empty response, and certificate enrollment fails
incidents.solution: To resolve the Intune SCEP challenge validation failure, follow these steps: Ensure that the necessary licenses are enabled, including Microsoft Entra ID P2, Microsoft Intune Endpoint Privilege Management, and Microsoft Intune Plan 1. Verify that the App registered for SCEP/Graph access has the required permissions, including scep_challenge_provider and Application.Read.All. Note : The Application.Read.All. permission requires manual approval from the directory admin. Check the FortiAuthenticator configuration to ensure that it is set up to use the correct SCEP validation URL. Review the debug logs from FortiAuthenticator to identify any issues with the SCEP validation process. For more information on configuring Intune certificate provisioning with FortiAuthenticator, refer to the FortiAuthenticator documentation: Intune Certificate Provisioning with FortiAuthenticator CA . incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Error AADSTS51004 with SAML authentication on FortiAuthenticator
incidents.summary: Description This article describes the issue of encountering Error AADSTS51004 when attempting to perform two-factor authentication (2FA) using SAML on FortiAuthenticator with Office 365. The user can authenticate correctly on the FortiAuthenticator but encounters an error when redirecting to Office 365. Scope FortiAuthenticator, FortiGate. Solution To resolve the AADSTS51004 error, follow these steps: Verify that the Active Directory is synchronized correctly with Office 365.
incidents.symptom: This article describes the issue of encountering Error AADSTS51004 when attempting to perform two-factor authentication (2FA) using SAML on FortiAuthenticator with Office 365. The user can authenticate correctly on the FortiAuthenticator but encounters an error when redirecting to Office 365
incidents.solution: To resolve the AADSTS51004 error, follow these steps: Verify that the Active Directory is synchronized correctly with Office 365. Check the attribute being sent by the FortiAuthenticator to ensure it matches the User Principal Name (UPN) declared in the Azure Active Directory. Confirm that the Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL is correctly configured. Refer to the Error AADSTS750054 - SAMLRequest or SAMLResponse must be present as query string parameters in HTTP request for SAML Redirect binding for troubleshooting SAML authentication issues. Additionally, review the FortiAuthenticator configuration to ensure that the attributes like email, username, userPrincipalName, etc., being sent are consistent with the expected value. If the issue persists, review the Azure Active Directory configuration to ensure that the user exists and the UPN is correctly set. Confirm that the Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL is correctly configured. Refer to the Error AADSTS750054 - SAMLRequest or SAMLResponse must be present as query string parameters in HTTP request for SAML Redirect binding for troubleshooting SAML authentication issues. Additionally, review the FortiAuthenticator configuration to ensure that the attributes like email, username, userPrincipalName, etc., being sent are consistent with the expected value. If the issue persists, review the Azure Active Directory configuration to ensure that the user exists and the UPN is correctly set.
